## 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Tujuan | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Migration strategy | Flyway/Liquibase flow | Schema berubah terkontrol | Manual DB hotfix tidak terlacak |
| Versioning | Ordered migrations | Deterministic deployment | Migration out of order |
| Mapper compatibility | SQL/resultMap sync | App tetap jalan saat schema evolve | Column hilang/rename merusak runtime |
| Safe column changes | Add/backfill/enforce/remove | Avoid breaking deploy | Add NOT NULL langsung lock/fail |
| Enum/status migration | DB enum/text/domain enum sync | State contract stabil | Unknown status crash TypeHandler |
| Index rollout | Online-ish index changes | Performa tanpa blocking besar | Lock table saat peak |
| Backfill | Isi data lama | Konsistensi data historis | Batch besar lock/timeout |
| Constraint rollout | Data quality | Enforce invariant DB | Constraint gagal karena data legacy |
| Function/procedure migration | DB code lifecycle | PL/pgSQL compatible | Function signature break mapper |
| Rollback strategy | Recover failed deploy | Operational safety | Rollback app tapi DB sudah berubah |
| Contract testing | Prove schema ↔ MyBatis ↔ API | Prevent drift | Migration lolos tapi API rusak |
| Release choreography | Expand-contract | Zero/low downtime deploy | App baru/old tidak compatible |

---

# 4. Flyway vs Liquibase Decision

| Concern | Flyway | Liquibase |
|---|---|---|
| SQL-first PostgreSQL | Sangat cocok | Cocok juga dengan formatted SQL |
| Declarative changelog | Tidak utama | Kuat |
| Preconditions | Terbatas dibanding Liquibase | Kuat |
| Rollback metadata | Ada fitur tertentu/edition-dependent; SQL rollback sering manual | Rollback lebih eksplisit di changeset |
| Team habit | Developer SQL-heavy | Enterprise governance-heavy |
| Mapper XML review | Sama-sama wajib | Sama-sama wajib |
| Drift prevention | `validate`, schema history | `DATABASECHANGELOG`, validation |
| Multi-env control | Config-based | Contexts/labels kuat |

Rule praktis:

```text id="p5oivw"
Jika tim PostgreSQL/MyBatis SQL-heavy:
  Flyway SQL migrations sangat natural.

Jika organisasi butuh governance changeSet, context, label, rollback metadata:
  Liquibase lebih kaya.
```

Yang penting bukan tool-nya saja, tetapi governance:

```text id="qee2tr"
[ ] Migration masuk repo.
[ ] Migration masuk CI.
[ ] Migration dites dengan PostgreSQL nyata.
[ ] MyBatis mapper XML dites setelah migration.
[ ] Contract API dites setelah migration.
```

---

# 5. Migration Naming & Ordering

## 5.1 Flyway Naming

Contoh:

```text id="rxbndc"
src/main/resources/db/migration/
├── V202607130001__create_orders.sql
├── V202607130002__create_order_items.sql
├── V202607130003__add_order_priority_nullable.sql
├── V202607130004__backfill_order_priority.sql
├── V202607130005__enforce_order_priority_not_null.sql
└── R__refresh_order_search_view.sql
```

Pattern:

```text id="oyptov"
V{timestamp_or_sequence}__description.sql
R__repeatable_object.sql
```

Flyway versioned migrations punya version dan description serta dijalankan sekali, sedangkan repeatable migrations dijalankan ulang jika checksum berubah. ([github.com](https://github.com/flyway/flywaydb.org/blob/gh-pages/documentation/concepts/migrations.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 5.2 Liquibase Changeset Naming

```yaml id="4rmhmu"
databaseChangeLog:
  - changeSet:
      id: 202607130001-create-orders
      author: platform-team
      changes:
        - createTable:
            tableName: orders
            columns:
              - column:
                  name: id
                  type: uuid
                  constraints:
                    primaryKey: true
                    nullable: false
```

Liquibase changeset identity bukan hanya `id`, tetapi kombinasi `author`, `id`, dan changelog file path; `id` tidak harus integer dan tidak menentukan urutan run sendiri. ([docs.liquibase.com](https://docs.liquibase.com/secure/user-guide-5-1/what-is-a-changeset?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 6. Expand-Contract Migration Pattern

Untuk zero/low downtime, hindari perubahan schema yang hanya compatible dengan satu versi app. Gunakan pola **expand → migrate/backfill → switch app → contract**.

```text id="cj70jx"
Phase 1 - Expand schema
  Add nullable column / new table / new index.
  Old app still works.
  New app can write/read new structure.

Phase 2 - Dual write / dual read
  App writes old + new field if needed.
  App can read old and new.

Phase 3 - Backfill
  Populate new column/table from old data.

Phase 4 - Enforce
  Add constraints after data valid.

Phase 5 - Switch
  New app uses new field/table as primary.

Phase 6 - Contract
  Remove old column/path only after old app/client gone.
```

Decision rule:

```text id="twfpfk"
Migration harus compatible dengan:
- app version currently running
- app version being deployed
- rollback app version, if rollback is part of operational plan
```

---

# 7. Safe Column Changes

## 7.1 Add nullable column first

```sql id="1fmvsb"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD COLUMN priority text;
```

MyBatis impact:

```xml id="p3kiiu"
<result property="priority" column="priority"/>
```

Java record impact:

```java id="uocyew"
public record OrderRecord(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatus status,
        OrderPriority priority
) {}
```

But do not immediately require API clients to send priority.

---

## 7.2 Backfill separately

```sql id="7xbfss"
UPDATE orders
SET priority = 'NORMAL'
WHERE priority IS NULL;
```

For large tables, prefer batching:

```sql id="q6nfpq"
UPDATE orders
SET priority = 'NORMAL'
WHERE id IN (
    SELECT id
    FROM orders
    WHERE priority IS NULL
    ORDER BY id
    LIMIT 1000
);
```

Repeat until zero rows. Avoid one massive update if table is large.

---

## 7.3 Enforce NOT NULL after backfill

```sql id="qy7eqt"
ALTER TABLE orders
ALTER COLUMN priority SET NOT NULL;
```

Checklist before enforcing:

```text id="e8s9pr"
[ ] Backfill completed.
[ ] New app writes column.
[ ] Old app no longer writes null, or default exists.
[ ] Integration test proves insert succeeds.
[ ] Production data check shows no null.
```

---

# 8. Safe Column Rename

Column rename is dangerous because MyBatis XML references columns explicitly.

Unsafe:

```sql id="33j4z2"
ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN order_number TO reference_number;
```

This breaks old mapper XML:

```xml id="v6euyf"
<result property="orderNumber" column="order_number"/>
```

## Safer pattern

### Phase 1 - Add new column

```sql id="b5gj9b"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD COLUMN reference_number text;
```

### Phase 2 - Backfill

```sql id="g4llq8"
UPDATE orders
SET reference_number = order_number
WHERE reference_number IS NULL;
```

### Phase 3 - Dual write app

Mapper insert/update writes both:

```xml id="avzn8s"
INSERT INTO orders (
    id,
    order_number,
    reference_number,
    status
) VALUES (
    #{id},
    #{orderNumber},
    #{referenceNumber},
    #{status}
)
```

### Phase 4 - Read new, fallback old

```sql id="fjo4id"
SELECT
    id,
    COALESCE(reference_number, order_number) AS reference_number,
    status
FROM orders
WHERE id = #{id}
```

### Phase 5 - Switch contract

API response uses `referenceNumber`, optionally still returns deprecated `orderNumber`.

### Phase 6 - Remove old after deprecation

```sql id="9b8pee"
ALTER TABLE orders
DROP COLUMN order_number;
```

Only after all old app versions and old clients are gone.

---

# 9. Safe Column Drop

Before dropping column:

```text id="3ew1sf"
[ ] No mapper XML references the column.
[ ] No resultMap references the column.
[ ] No TypeHandler depends on it.
[ ] No OpenAPI schema exposes it.
[ ] No DTO/MapStruct mapper uses it.
[ ] No report/job/function/view uses it.
[ ] Production telemetry confirms no usage.
[ ] Rollback plan does not need the column.
```

Drop pattern:

```text id="c81w4r"
Phase 1: stop writing column
Phase 2: stop reading column
Phase 3: remove API field or mark deprecated long enough
Phase 4: deploy app without dependency
Phase 5: drop column in later release
```

Never combine “stop reading” and “drop column” in same risky deployment unless downtime/rollback plan is explicit.

---

# 10. resultMap Drift Governance

`resultMap` drift happens when DB schema/query result changes but Java mapping does not.

## 10.1 Common drift

| Change | Drift |
|---|---|
| Column renamed | `column="old_name"` becomes null/error |
| Column type changed | TypeHandler/JDBC mapping fails |
| Column removed | Query fails |
| New NOT NULL column | Insert fails |
| Enum value added | `Enum.valueOf` fails |
| Query alias changed | resultMap field null |
| Function return table changed | resultMap mismatch |
| View changed | mapper silently maps wrong/null |

## 10.2 Guardrail test

```java id="ur27j6"
@Test
void shouldLoadOrderResultMapAfterMigration() {
    try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession()) {
        OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

        UUID id = insertOrderFixture(session);

        OrderRecord order = mapper.findById(id);

        assertNotNull(order);
        assertNotNull(order.id());
        assertNotNull(order.orderNumber());
        assertNotNull(order.status());
    }
}
```

## 10.3 Mapper XML compatibility checklist

```text id="2639pc"
[ ] Every migration changing table/view/function has mapper search.
[ ] Every new NOT NULL column updates insert SQL.
[ ] Every renamed column uses expand-contract.
[ ] Every enum/status value updates TypeHandler/domain enum.
[ ] Every view/function result change has resultMap test.
[ ] Every dropped column has app code removal before DB drop.
```

---

# 11. Enum / Status Migration

## 11.1 If status stored as text

Migration:

```sql id="8p9hqj"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD CONSTRAINT orders_status_check
CHECK (status IN ('DRAFT', 'SUBMITTED', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', 'CANCELLED'));
```

Adding new status:

```sql id="yb5ztw"
ALTER TABLE orders
DROP CONSTRAINT orders_status_check;

ALTER TABLE orders
ADD CONSTRAINT orders_status_check
CHECK (status IN (
    'DRAFT',
    'SUBMITTED',
    'APPROVED',
    'REJECTED',
    'CANCELLED',
    'ESCALATED'
));
```

Java impact:

```java id="8puv8z"
public enum OrderStatus {
    DRAFT,
    SUBMITTED,
    APPROVED,
    REJECTED,
    CANCELLED,
    ESCALATED
}
```

TypeHandler impact:

```java id="rlsgdf"
return value == null ? null : OrderStatus.valueOf(value);
```

If DB may contain future/unknown value, `valueOf` can crash. Consider safe mapping only if business allows unknown internal state.

---

## 11.2 If PostgreSQL enum type is used

Adding enum value:

```sql id="3dq1qy"
ALTER TYPE order_status ADD VALUE 'ESCALATED';
```

Be cautious: PostgreSQL enum removal/rename is less flexible than check constraint over text. For systems with frequent state evolution, text + check constraint can be operationally easier.

Decision:

| Strategy | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL enum | Strong DB type | Harder evolution/removal |
| text + check constraint | Easier migration | Slightly less type-specific |
| lookup table | Flexible + metadata | Join/management overhead |

---

# 12. Index Rollout

PostgreSQL `CREATE INDEX` improves performance but inappropriate indexes can slow writes and consume resources. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 12.1 Basic index

```sql id="rnx5ee"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted
ON orders (tenant_id, status, submitted_at DESC, id DESC);
```

## 12.2 Concurrent index for large production table

```sql id="u793hl"
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted
ON orders (tenant_id, status, submitted_at DESC, id DESC);
```

PostgreSQL supports `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` to build an index without blocking concurrent inserts/updates/deletes in the same way as a normal index build, but it has restrictions and takes more work/time; consult the `CREATE INDEX` documentation for details in your PostgreSQL version. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Important governance note:

```text id="y25trq"
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a normal transaction block.
Many migration tools wrap migrations in transactions by default.
So concurrent index migration may need special configuration/split migration.
```

## 12.3 Index rollout checklist

```text id="fzxwjy"
[ ] Query needing index identified.
[ ] EXPLAIN before/after captured.
[ ] Index name follows convention.
[ ] Large table uses concurrent build if needed.
[ ] Migration transaction behavior compatible.
[ ] Write overhead considered.
[ ] Duplicate/unused index checked.
[ ] Rollback/drop plan exists.
```

---

# 13. Constraint Rollout

## 13.1 Add check constraint safely

For large existing tables, avoid immediate full validation if needed.

```sql id="1q4t22"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD CONSTRAINT orders_total_amount_non_negative
CHECK (total_amount >= 0) NOT VALID;
```

Then validate later:

```sql id="ytvcqu"
ALTER TABLE orders
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_total_amount_non_negative;
```

Pattern:

```text id="atzpyp"
1. Add NOT VALID constraint.
2. Fix/backfill invalid legacy rows.
3. Validate constraint.
4. Update tests to expect constraint.
```

## 13.2 Unique constraint rollout

If data may have duplicates:

```text id="o4buoz"
1. Detect duplicates.
2. Clean/merge duplicates.
3. Create unique index concurrently.
4. Attach/add constraint if needed.
5. Translate SQLSTATE 23505 to API 409.
```

---

# 14. Backfill Strategy

Backfill must not destroy production performance.

## 14.1 Bad backfill

```sql id="xj44jo"
UPDATE orders
SET priority = 'NORMAL'
WHERE priority IS NULL;
```

For huge table this can create long transaction, lots of WAL, locks, replication lag.

## 14.2 Batch backfill

```sql id="grmctt"
WITH batch AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM orders
    WHERE priority IS NULL
    ORDER BY id
    LIMIT 1000
)
UPDATE orders o
SET priority = 'NORMAL'
FROM batch
WHERE o.id = batch.id;
```

Run repeatedly via job/migration orchestration.

## 14.3 Backfill checklist

```text id="c4mdrm"
[ ] Batch size defined.
[ ] Sleep/throttle if needed.
[ ] Progress measurable.
[ ] Idempotent.
[ ] Can resume safely.
[ ] Does not block OLTP traffic excessively.
[ ] Replication/WAL impact considered.
[ ] Data validation query exists.
```

---

# 15. Function / Procedure Migration

MyBatis can call PostgreSQL functions/procedures, so DB code is also contract.

## 15.1 Function result change is breaking

Before:

```sql id="74kd5z"
CREATE FUNCTION search_orders(...)
RETURNS TABLE (
    id uuid,
    order_number text,
    status text
)
...
```

After adding column:

```sql id="gnjgwa"
RETURNS TABLE (
    id uuid,
    reference_number text,
    status text,
    priority text
)
```

MyBatis `resultMap` must change with it.

## 15.2 Safer function versioning

```sql id="u6hakg"
CREATE FUNCTION search_orders_v1(...)
RETURNS TABLE (...);

CREATE FUNCTION search_orders_v2(...)
RETURNS TABLE (...);
```

Mapper:

```xml id="ci68t1"
<select id="searchOrdersV2" resultMap="OrderV2ResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        reference_number,
        status,
        priority
    FROM search_orders_v2(#{tenantId}, #{status})
</select>
```

Checklist:

```text id="qu7hxv"
[ ] Function signature changes treated as mapper-impacting.
[ ] Function return columns explicitly tested.
[ ] Old function retained until old app gone.
[ ] Repeatable migration used carefully for replaceable functions/views.
[ ] Rollback story exists.
```

---

# 16. Rollback Strategy

Rollback database changes is harder than rollback app code.

## 16.1 Types of rollback

| Type | Description | Safe? |
|---|---|---|
| App rollback only | Deploy previous app version | Safe only if DB remains backward-compatible |
| Forward fix | New migration fixes issue | Often safest in production |
| DB rollback | Undo migration | Risky if data changed |
| Restore backup | Disaster recovery | Last resort / data loss window |
| Feature flag off | Disable new code path | Good if planned |

Liquibase rollback behavior depends on rollback method; for example, rolling back to a tag created with `tagDatabase` removes all deployed changesets after that tag row and the tag row itself, whereas tag command behavior differs. ([docs.liquibase.com](https://docs.liquibase.com/secure/reference-guide-5-2/init-update-and-rollback-commands/rollback?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 16.2 Rollback-safe migration principle

```text id="lrxtns"
A migration is rollback-friendly if:
- old app can still run after migration
- new columns are additive
- old columns not dropped yet
- data transform is reversible or not needed
- app behavior can be disabled by flag
```

## 16.3 Avoid rollback trap

Dangerous same-release bundle:

```text id="uz2ka5"
Migration:
  drop old column

App:
  no longer uses old column

Problem:
  if app rollback needed, old app fails because column gone.
```

Safer:

```text id="ac0i6h"
Release A:
  app stops reading old column

Release B:
  migration drops old column after rollback window
```

---

# 17. Contract Testing Across Migration

## 17.1 Test pipeline

```text id="q8hq8z"
Start PostgreSQL container
  ↓
Apply migrations from scratch
  ↓
Load MyBatis config
  ↓
Run mapper XML load test
  ↓
Run repository integration tests
  ↓
Run JerseyTest success/error
  ↓
Run OpenAPI example-as-test
```

## 17.2 Test cases

| Change | Test |
|---|---|
| Add column | Insert via mapper still works |
| Add NOT NULL | Old insert path updated |
| Rename column | Old/new dual read/write tests |
| Drop column | Mapper XML no reference |
| Add enum/status | TypeHandler maps new value |
| Add index | EXPLAIN reviewed for critical query |
| Add constraint | Invalid data rejected and mapped |
| Backfill | Legacy rows get expected data |
| Function change | resultMap matches return columns |
| Procedure change | side effect correct |
| Error mapping | SQLSTATE maps to stable API error |
| OpenAPI field change | Golden response/contract updated intentionally |

## 17.3 Mapper XML reference check

Simple grep should be part of review:

```bash id="0nsgov"
grep -R "order_number" src/main/resources/mybatis src/main/java api-contract
```

For serious governance, add static checks or schema-aware tests.

---

# 18. CI/CD Migration Pipeline

```text id="ffrwo9"
Pull Request
  ↓
Static review:
  - migration naming
  - no destructive migration without plan
  - mapper XML references checked
  - OpenAPI diff checked
  ↓
CI:
  - start PostgreSQL
  - apply migration from empty DB
  - run MyBatis integration tests
  - run JerseyTest
  - run OpenAPI contract tests
  ↓
Pre-prod:
  - apply migration to prod-like copy
  - run smoke tests
  - run EXPLAIN for critical query
  - run backfill dry-run if possible
  ↓
Prod:
  - apply expand migration
  - deploy app
  - monitor errors/locks/query time
  - run backfill if separated
  - enforce/contract later
```

---

# 19. Migration Review Checklist

## 19.1 Schema

```text id="7exqrb"
[ ] Is change additive or destructive?
[ ] Does old app still work after migration?
[ ] Does new app work before/after migration?
[ ] Is there a rollback/forward-fix plan?
[ ] Are large table operations safe?
[ ] Does migration run inside/outside transaction as needed?
[ ] Are locks understood?
```

## 19.2 MyBatis

```text id="fr9pgd"
[ ] Mapper XML updated.
[ ] resultMap updated.
[ ] Insert/update statements include new required column.
[ ] TypeHandler updated if enum/type changed.
[ ] Dynamic SQL branch updated.
[ ] Function/procedure calls updated.
[ ] Mapper integration tests updated.
```

## 19.3 API

```text id="9hu6qs"
[ ] DTO update is backward-compatible.
[ ] OpenAPI updated.
[ ] Error catalog updated if constraint/error changed.
[ ] Golden files updated intentionally.
[ ] Validation constraints align with DB constraints.
[ ] Deprecated fields have migration note.
```

## 19.4 PostgreSQL production safety

```text id="s5d95n"
[ ] Large index uses concurrent strategy if needed.
[ ] Backfill is batched.
[ ] NOT NULL/check/unique constraints are staged.
[ ] Query plans reviewed for critical paths.
[ ] Replication/WAL impact considered.
[ ] Lock timeout/statement timeout considered.
```

---

# 20. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Add NOT NULL column without default/backfill | Insert old app gagal | Add nullable → backfill → enforce |
| Rename column directly | Old mapper XML rusak | Add new column + dual read/write |
| Drop column same release | App rollback gagal | Contract later |
| Update huge table in one transaction | Lock/WAL/replication lag | Batched backfill |
| Create normal index on huge hot table | Blocking/impact writes | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` if appropriate |
| Change PostgreSQL enum casually | Rollback/evolution sulit | Consider text + check/lookup |
| Change function return columns | resultMap drift | Version function or update tests |
| No migration integration test | Runtime fail after deploy | PostgreSQL container test |
| OpenAPI not updated | Client docs drift | Contract CI |
| SQLSTATE not translated | DB detail leaks / wrong API status | Error translator |

---

# 21. Production Definition of Done

```text id="2wjxu0"
Migration
[ ] Migration file committed.
[ ] Naming/order correct.
[ ] From-empty-db migration passes.
[ ] From-previous-version migration passes.
[ ] Rollback/forward-fix strategy documented.

MyBatis
[ ] Mapper XML updated.
[ ] resultMap updated.
[ ] Mapper XML load test passes.
[ ] Repository integration test passes.
[ ] TypeHandler updated/tested if needed.

PostgreSQL
[ ] Large operations staged.
[ ] Index strategy reviewed.
[ ] Constraint rollout safe.
[ ] Backfill idempotent/batched if needed.
[ ] SQLSTATE mapping updated.

API
[ ] DTO/OpenAPI updated if API impact.
[ ] Error contract updated if needed.
[ ] Golden/contract tests updated.
[ ] Backward compatibility reviewed.

Ops
[ ] Monitoring plan exists.
[ ] Migration runbook exists for risky change.
[ ] Deployment order clear.
[ ] Rollback/forward-fix owner clear.
```

# Cheatsheet - MyBatis Security & Data Isolation  
## SQL injection via `${}`, tenant isolation, row-level access, sensitive data logging, DB least privilege

## 1. Introduction

Di aplikasi **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis + PostgreSQL**, security persistence layer harus diperlakukan sebagai **defense-in-depth**, bukan hanya “pakai prepared statement”.

Target utamanya:

```text id="pb9q52"
[ ] Tidak ada SQL injection.
[ ] Tenant/user tidak bisa membaca data yang bukan miliknya.
[ ] Authorization tidak hanya bergantung pada UI/client.
[ ] Query list/search selalu tenant-scoped.
[ ] SQL error tidak membocorkan detail internal.
[ ] Log tidak membocorkan PII/secret.
[ ] DB user aplikasi memakai least privilege.
[ ] Test membuktikan cross-tenant access gagal.
```

MyBatis aman untuk parameter value jika memakai `#{}` karena MyBatis membuat `PreparedStatement` parameter, tetapi `${}` adalah string substitution mentah dan MyBatis tidak mengubah/escape string tersebut. Dokumentasi MyBatis sendiri memberi contoh `${}` untuk kasus seperti `ORDER BY`, sekaligus menegaskan bahwa `#{}` hampir selalu lebih aman dan lebih disukai. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 2. Security Boundary Diagram

```text id="3r3mt7"
Client Request
  │
  ├─ Authorization header / token
  ├─ Query params
  ├─ Path params
  └─ Request body
       │
       ▼
Jersey Resource
  │
  ├─ Authenticate
  ├─ Resolve actor
  ├─ Resolve tenant
  ├─ Validate DTO
  └─ Reject unsafe input early
       │
       ▼
Application Service
  │
  ├─ Enforce use-case permission
  ├─ Pass server-derived tenantId
  ├─ Do not trust tenantId from body
  └─ Define domain action
       │
       ▼
Repository / MyBatis
  │
  ├─ Use #{...} for values
  ├─ Use ${...} only with allow-listed server fragments
  ├─ Always include tenant filter
  ├─ Avoid SELECT *
  └─ Translate SQLSTATE safely
       │
       ▼
PostgreSQL
  │
  ├─ Least privilege role
  ├─ Optional RLS policies
  ├─ Constraints
  ├─ Views/functions if needed
  └─ Audit/monitoring
```

---

## 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Fungsi utama | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| SQL parameter binding | `#{}` | Bind value via prepared statement | Developer pakai `${}` untuk value |
| SQL string substitution | `${}` | Inject SQL fragment | SQL injection jika input user masuk |
| Sort allow-list | enum → SQL column | Safe dynamic `ORDER BY` | Raw `sort` query param |
| Filter allow-list | enum/criteria DTO | Safe dynamic search | Raw SQL filter fragment |
| Tenant isolation | server-derived tenant ID | Prevent cross-tenant data access | `tenantId` dari request body |
| Row-level access | owner/role/resource policy | Object-level authorization | Cek permission hanya di UI |
| PostgreSQL RLS | DB-level row policy | Defense-in-depth | App bypass policy dengan owner role |
| Least privilege | DB role privileges | Limit blast radius | App user punya superuser/DDL |
| Sensitive logging | redaction/masking | Prevent PII leak | Log raw SQL parameters |
| Error safety | SQLSTATE → API error | Stable safe error response | SQL/table/constraint detail bocor |
| Mapper XML review | security PR gate | Catch risky `${}`/missing tenant filter | Mapper XML dianggap harmless |
| Security testing | cross-tenant/injection tests | Prove control works | Hanya happy path test |

---

# 4. SQL Injection di MyBatis

## 4.1 Safe value binding dengan `#{}`

```xml id="hu04eg"
<select id="findById" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM orders
    WHERE id = #{id}
</select>
```

`#{id}` menjadi parameter `PreparedStatement`.

Equivalent concept:

```sql id="mhqxg4"
SELECT id, order_number, status
FROM orders
WHERE id = ?
```

OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet menempatkan prepared statements / parameterized queries sebagai primary defense karena database membedakan code SQL dari data input. ([OWASP Cheat Sheet Series](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 4.2 Dangerous string substitution dengan `${}`

Bahaya:

```xml id="ie9tzd"
<select id="searchOrders" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
    ORDER BY ${sort}
</select>
```

Jika `sort` berasal dari query param:

```text id="wnh1oz"
?sort=submitted_at desc; delete from orders; --
```

Maka SQL fragment bisa dimanipulasi.

Dokumentasi MyBatis FAQ secara eksplisit memperingatkan bahwa penggunaan `${...}` memiliki risiko SQL injection. ([GitHub](https://github.com/mybatis/mybatis-3/wiki/FAQ?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 4.3 Rule utama `#{}` vs `${}`

| Case | Gunakan | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| Value biasa | `#{}` | `WHERE id = #{id}` |
| String value | `#{}` | `WHERE status = #{status}` |
| UUID | `#{}` | `WHERE customer_id = #{customerId}` |
| Date/time | `#{}` | `submitted_at >= #{from}` |
| Pagination limit | `#{}` | `LIMIT #{limit}` |
| SQL column name | `${}` hanya dari allow-list | `ORDER BY ${sortColumn}` |
| Direction ASC/DESC | `${}` hanya dari enum | `${sortDirection}` |
| Table name dynamic | Hindari; jika harus, allow-list | `${tableName}` |
| Raw WHERE fragment | Jangan | dangerous |
| Raw user-provided SQL | Jangan pernah | critical |

---

# 5. Safe Sorting Pattern

## 5.1 API DTO

```java id="q03ku2"
public record SearchOrderRequest(
        OrderStatusDto status,
        UUID customerId,
        OrderSortFieldDto sortField,
        SortDirectionDto sortDirection,
        @Min(1) @Max(100) Integer size
) {}
```

```java id="n1iihc"
public enum OrderSortFieldDto {
    SUBMITTED_AT,
    ORDER_NUMBER,
    STATUS
}

public enum SortDirectionDto {
    ASC,
    DESC
}
```

## 5.2 Server-side SQL allow-list

```java id="77pm7v"
public enum OrderSortField {
    SUBMITTED_AT("submitted_at"),
    ORDER_NUMBER("order_number"),
    STATUS("status");

    private final String sqlColumn;

    OrderSortField(String sqlColumn) {
        this.sqlColumn = sqlColumn;
    }

    public String sqlColumn() {
        return sqlColumn;
    }
}
```

Mapper from DTO:

```java id="fkg02i"
public OrderSearchCriteria toCriteria(
        SearchOrderRequest request,
        UUID tenantId
) {
    OrderSortField sortField = switch (
            request.sortField() == null
                    ? OrderSortFieldDto.SUBMITTED_AT
                    : request.sortField()
    ) {
        case SUBMITTED_AT -> OrderSortField.SUBMITTED_AT;
        case ORDER_NUMBER -> OrderSortField.ORDER_NUMBER;
        case STATUS -> OrderSortField.STATUS;
    };

    SortDirectionDto direction = request.sortDirection() == null
            ? SortDirectionDto.DESC
            : request.sortDirection();

    return new OrderSearchCriteria(
            tenantId,
            request.status(),
            request.customerId(),
            request.size() == null ? 20 : request.size(),
            sortField.sqlColumn(),
            direction.name()
    );
}
```

## 5.3 Mapper XML

```xml id="a5zrde"
<select id="searchOrders" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    <where>
        tenant_id = #{tenantId}

        <if test="status != null">
            AND status = #{status}
        </if>

        <if test="customerId != null">
            AND customer_id = #{customerId}
        </if>
    </where>
    ORDER BY ${sortColumn} ${sortDirection}, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Ini aman hanya karena:

```text id="3hth22"
sortColumn    berasal dari enum server-side
sortDirection berasal dari enum server-side
limit         tetap memakai #{}
filter value  tetap memakai #{}
```

---

# 6. Safe Filtering Pattern

## 6.1 Jangan menerima raw filter SQL

Anti-pattern:

```java id="z5wpd7"
public record SearchRequest(
        String whereClause
) {}
```

Anti-pattern XML:

```xml id="lcm95s"
WHERE ${whereClause}
```

Ini harus ditolak.

---

## 6.2 Gunakan typed criteria

```java id="wjd37k"
public record OrderSearchCriteria(
        UUID tenantId,
        OrderStatus status,
        UUID customerId,
        Instant submittedFrom,
        Instant submittedTo,
        int limit,
        String sortColumn,
        String sortDirection
) {}
```

XML:

```xml id="a1momg"
<select id="searchOrders" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    <where>
        tenant_id = #{tenantId}

        <if test="status != null">
            AND status = #{status}
        </if>

        <if test="customerId != null">
            AND customer_id = #{customerId}
        </if>

        <if test="submittedFrom != null">
            AND submitted_at &gt;= #{submittedFrom}
        </if>

        <if test="submittedTo != null">
            AND submitted_at &lt; #{submittedTo}
        </if>
    </where>
    ORDER BY ${sortColumn} ${sortDirection}, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

OWASP juga merekomendasikan allow-list input validation untuk bagian query yang memang tidak bisa diparameterisasi sebagai value, misalnya nama tabel/kolom atau arah sort. ([OWASP Cheat Sheet Series](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 7. Tenant Isolation

## 7.1 Tenant ID harus server-derived

Jangan:

```java id="j3nka3"
public record CreateOrderRequest(
        UUID tenantId,
        UUID customerId,
        List<CreateOrderItemRequest> items
) {}
```

Lebih aman:

```java id="xrxx99"
public record CreateOrderRequest(
        UUID customerId,
        List<CreateOrderItemRequest> items
) {}
```

Resource:

```java id="s2x1mm"
@POST
public Response create(
        @Valid CreateOrderRequest request,
        @Context SecurityContext securityContext
) {
    AuthenticatedActor actor = actorResolver.resolve(securityContext);
    TenantId tenantId = actor.tenantId();

    CreateOrderCommand command = apiMapper.toCommand(
            tenantId,
            actor.userId(),
            request
    );

    OrderResult result = orderService.create(command);

    return Response.status(Response.Status.CREATED)
            .entity(apiMapper.toResponse(result))
            .build();
}
```

Rule:

```text id="656u49"
tenantId:
  - dari token/session/mTLS/server context
  - bukan dari request body biasa
  - bukan dari query param biasa
  - selalu diteruskan ke service/repository
```

---

## 7.2 Repository API tenant-scoped

```java id="2tgo0w"
public interface OrderRepository {

    Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);

    List<Order> search(TenantId tenantId, OrderSearchCriteria criteria);

    void insert(TenantId tenantId, Order order);

    void update(TenantId tenantId, Order order);
}
```

Mapper interface:

```java id="9of9po"
public interface OrderSqlMapper {

    OrderRecord findByIdForTenant(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("id") UUID id
    );

    List<OrderRecord> searchOrders(OrderSearchCriteria criteria);

    int updateStatusForTenant(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("id") UUID id,
            @Param("status") OrderStatus status,
            @Param("expectedVersion") long expectedVersion
    );
}
```

Mapper XML:

```xml id="g5oaxb"
<select id="findByIdForTenant" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        status,
        version
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND id = #{id}
</select>
```

Update:

```xml id="jjk9ds"
<update id="updateStatusForTenant">
    UPDATE orders
    SET
        status = #{status},
        version = version + 1,
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND id = #{id}
      AND version = #{expectedVersion}
</update>
```

Checklist:

```text id="blxt9y"
[ ] Every read query has tenant filter.
[ ] Every update/delete query has tenant filter.
[ ] Every list/search query has tenant filter.
[ ] Repository method requires tenant context.
[ ] Tests prove tenant A cannot access tenant B data.
```

---

# 8. Reusable Tenant Filter

Reusable SQL fragment:

```xml id="t5n2iz"
<sql id="TenantFilter">
    tenant_id = #{tenantId}
</sql>
```

Usage:

```xml id="dh2b5d"
<select id="findByIdForTenant" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM orders
    WHERE <include refid="TenantFilter"/>
      AND id = #{id}
</select>
```

Caution:

```text id="yj2vyr"
Reusable fragment membantu konsistensi,
tetapi jangan membuat reviewer jadi lengah.

Tetap review final SQL shape dan test cross-tenant.
```

Better naming:

```xml id="7pwzj9"
<select id="findByIdForTenant" ...>
```

Nama method yang mengandung `ForTenant` membantu reviewer melihat security intent.

---

# 9. Object-Level Authorization

Tenant isolation belum cukup. Dalam satu tenant, user bisa punya permission berbeda.

Contoh rules:

```text id="5ur4sf"
User A boleh lihat order milik branch A.
User B hanya boleh approve order sampai amount tertentu.
Supervisor boleh lihat semua order tenant.
Finance boleh lihat payment detail.
Support boleh lihat masked customer data.
```

## 9.1 Service-level permission check

```java id="w3cxp2"
public OrderResult approve(ApproveOrderCommand command) {
    return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);

        Order order = repository.findById(
                command.tenantId(),
                command.orderId()
        ).orElseThrow(() -> DomainException.notFound("ORDER_NOT_FOUND"));

        permissionService.requireCanApprove(
                command.actor(),
                order
        );

        order.approve(command.actor().userId());

        repository.update(command.tenantId(), order);

        return OrderResult.from(order);
    });
}
```

Rule:

```text id="3n1igx"
Authorization:
  - coarse-grained bisa di resource/filter
  - object-level harus di service/domain setelah resource dimuat
  - repository tetap tenant-scoped
```

---

## 9.2 Query-level authorization for list/search

Jika list harus dibatasi berdasarkan actor:

```java id="xkqh58"
public record OrderVisibilityCriteria(
        UUID tenantId,
        UUID actorUserId,
        Set<String> branchCodes,
        boolean canViewAllBranches
) {}
```

XML:

```xml id="dmyy6q"
<select id="searchVisibleOrders" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        branch_code,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM orders
    <where>
        tenant_id = #{tenantId}

        <if test="!canViewAllBranches">
            AND branch_code IN
            <foreach collection="branchCodes"
                     item="branchCode"
                     open="("
                     separator=","
                     close=")">
                #{branchCode}
            </foreach>
        </if>

        <if test="status != null">
            AND status = #{status}
        </if>
    </where>
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Checklist:

```text id="7l2m8q"
[ ] Visibility criteria derived from server-side permission.
[ ] User cannot pass branchCodes directly unless validated against grants.
[ ] Empty allowed branch list returns empty result, not all result.
[ ] List/count/export use the same visibility rule.
```

---

# 10. PostgreSQL Row-Level Security sebagai Defense-in-Depth

PostgreSQL Row Security Policies dapat membatasi row mana yang bisa dilihat atau dimodifikasi oleh role tertentu; policy bisa diterapkan per command, per role, atau keduanya. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 10.1 Enable RLS

```sql id="yzbotz"
ALTER TABLE orders ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

## 10.2 Policy using session setting

```sql id="5pi5s3"
CREATE POLICY orders_tenant_isolation
ON orders
USING (
    tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid
)
WITH CHECK (
    tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid
);
```

Before query, set tenant:

```sql id="s2u6zl"
SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001';
```

MyBatis mapper:

```xml id="r0lzzr"
<update id="setCurrentTenant">
    SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant_id', #{tenantId}, true)
</update>
```

Transaction flow:

```java id="cfiv2a"
transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
    SecuritySqlMapper securityMapper =
            session.getMapper(SecuritySqlMapper.class);

    securityMapper.setCurrentTenant(command.tenantId().value());

    OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);

    ...
});
```

Important:

```text id="8hymbu"
RLS bukan pengganti application-level authorization.
RLS adalah defense-in-depth jika query lupa tenant filter.
```

---

## 10.3 RLS caveats

```text id="79v6db"
[ ] Role owner/table owner can bypass unless configured carefully.
[ ] Superuser bypasses RLS.
[ ] FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY may be needed for table owner scenarios.
[ ] Session variable must be set inside transaction.
[ ] Connection pool reuse means session state must not leak.
[ ] Use SET LOCAL or transaction-local set_config(..., true).
[ ] Test tenant A/B in same pooled environment.
```

PostgreSQL documentation notes that table owners normally bypass row security, although a table owner can choose to be subject to policies with `ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 11. DB Least Privilege

OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet recommends minimizing privileges assigned to every database account and explicitly warns against giving application accounts DBA/admin rights. ([GitHub](https://github.com/nokia/OWASP-CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.1 Separate roles

```sql id="4ry1ai"
CREATE ROLE app_owner NOLOGIN;
CREATE ROLE app_runtime LOGIN PASSWORD '...';
CREATE ROLE app_migration LOGIN PASSWORD '...';
CREATE ROLE app_readonly LOGIN PASSWORD '...';
```

Suggested responsibility:

| Role | Privilege |
|---|---|
| `app_owner` | Owns schema objects, no login |
| `app_migration` | DDL/migration privileges |
| `app_runtime` | Only DML needed by app |
| `app_readonly` | Read-only reporting/support |
| `postgres/superuser` | Not used by app |

PostgreSQL privileges are granted using `GRANT`; the special role name `PUBLIC` grants to every role, and group roles can manage privileges collectively. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-priv.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 11.2 Runtime grants

Example:

```sql id="pn8mzr"
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE appdb TO app_runtime;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA app TO app_runtime;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
ON app.orders, app.order_items
TO app_runtime;

GRANT USAGE, SELECT
ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA app
TO app_runtime;
```

Avoid:

```sql id="ve6h2y"
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE appdb TO app_runtime;
ALTER ROLE app_runtime SUPERUSER;
```

## 11.3 Function execution grants

If using functions/procedures:

```sql id="goev65"
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION app.calculate_order_total(uuid)
TO app_runtime;
```

Checklist:

```text id="e5u7j3"
[ ] Runtime role cannot DDL.
[ ] Runtime role cannot drop tables.
[ ] Runtime role cannot bypass RLS unintentionally.
[ ] Migration role separate from runtime role.
[ ] Readonly role cannot write.
[ ] Default privileges configured for future tables.
[ ] PUBLIC privileges reviewed/revoked if needed.
```

---

# 12. Sensitive Data Logging

## 12.1 What not to log

```text id="3k12a9"
[NO] password
[NO] access token / refresh token
[NO] authorization header
[NO] full national ID / KTP / passport
[NO] full card/payment data
[NO] full customer address if not needed
[NO] full request body for write endpoints
[NO] raw SQL with sensitive parameters
[NO] SQL exception detail sent to client
```

## 12.2 What to log safely

```text id="zx7h6z"
[OK] correlationId
[OK] endpoint template
[OK] HTTP status
[OK] API error code
[OK] mapper method name
[OK] durationMs
[OK] row count
[OK] SQLSTATE
[OK] tenant hash, not raw tenant if sensitive
[OK] actor hash/user ID depending policy
```

## 12.3 MyBatis logging policy

Development:

```text id="wpgdvm"
boleh lebih verbose di local,
tetapi tetap hindari secret/token.
```

Production:

```text id="x0szbx"
log mapper method + duration + error code,
bukan raw SQL parameter sensitif.
```

Example safe log:

```java id="ehtph4"
log.info(
        "db.query mapper={} durationMs={} rows={} correlationId={}",
        "OrderSqlMapper.searchOrders",
        durationMs,
        rows,
        correlationId
);
```

Example risky log:

```java id="7wxuzv"
log.info("SQL={} params={}", sql, params);
```

# 13. Error Response Safety

## 13.1 Bad response

```json id="4kzj7f"
{
  "error": "duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"orders_order_number_key\"",
  "sql": "insert into orders ...",
  "table": "orders"
}
```

## 13.2 Good response

```json id="gmigvh"
{
  "code": "DUPLICATE_RESOURCE",
  "message": "Resource already exists",
  "correlationId": "req-123",
  "errors": []
}
```

Internal log may include diagnostic:

```text id="e61zma"
level=WARN
code=DUPLICATE_RESOURCE
sqlState=23505
mapper=OrderSqlMapper.insertOrder
correlationId=req-123
```

Rule:

```text id="fdvvi1"
Client gets stable public error.
Logs get enough diagnostic.
No raw SQL / schema / stack trace in response.
```

---

# 14. SQLSTATE Translation

PostgreSQL documentation advises applications to test error code rather than textual error message because error codes are less likely to change and are not affected by localization. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-priv.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Common mapping:

| SQLSTATE | Meaning | HTTP | API code |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `23505` | unique violation | 409 | `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE` |
| `23503` | foreign key violation | 409/422 | `REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| `23514` | check violation | 409/422 | `CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` |
| `42501` | insufficient privilege | 403/500 depending cause | `DATABASE_PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| `40001` | serialization failure | retry then 409/503 | `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` |
| `40P01` | deadlock detected | retry then 409/503 | `DEADLOCK_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` |
| `57014` | query canceled | 504 | `QUERY_TIMEOUT` |

Translator:

```java id="j2oof5"
public RuntimeException translate(RuntimeException exception) {
    SQLException sqlException = findSqlException(exception);

    if (sqlException == null) {
        return new PersistenceException(
                "PERSISTENCE_ERROR",
                "Persistence operation failed",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.UNKNOWN,
                exception
        );
    }

    return switch (sqlException.getSQLState()) {
        case "23505" -> new PersistenceException(
                "DUPLICATE_RESOURCE",
                "Resource already exists",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
                exception
        );
        case "23503" -> new PersistenceException(
                "REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND",
                "Referenced resource was not found",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
                exception
        );
        case "42501" -> new PersistenceException(
                "DATABASE_PERMISSION_DENIED",
                "Persistence operation is not allowed",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.FORBIDDEN,
                exception
        );
        default -> new PersistenceException(
                "PERSISTENCE_ERROR",
                "Persistence operation failed",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.UNKNOWN,
                exception
        );
    };
}
```

# 15. Safe Dynamic SQL Review Rules

## 15.1 Allowed `${}` cases

```text id="8xmp6t"
[OK] sortColumn from enum allow-list
[OK] sortDirection from enum ASC/DESC
[OK] partition/table suffix from internal config allow-list
[OK] index hint/SQL fragment from server constant
```

## 15.2 Forbidden `${}` cases

```text id="mp3ize"
[NO] request.getParameter("sort")
[NO] request body field
[NO] raw filter expression
[NO] search text
[NO] ID value
[NO] status value
[NO] tenantId
[NO] date range
[NO] user-provided table name
```

## 15.3 Mapper XML grep gate

Use CI/static review:

```bash id="kqi20g"
grep -R "\${" src/main/resources/mybatis
```

Every match must have justification:

```text id="9zwfa0"
[ ] Is this SQL fragment server-controlled?
[ ] Is it allow-listed?
[ ] Is there a test for malicious input?
[ ] Is there a safer #{...} alternative?
```

# 16. Tenant Isolation Test Matrix

## 16.1 Read by ID

```java id="lmtcyc"
@Test
void tenantACannotReadTenantBOrder() {
    UUID tenantA = UUID.randomUUID();
    UUID tenantB = UUID.randomUUID();

    UUID orderB = insertOrderForTenant(tenantB);

    Optional<Order> result = repository.findById(
            new TenantId(tenantA),
            orderB
    );

    assertTrue(result.isEmpty());
}
```

## 16.2 Update by ID

```java id="smffrn"
@Test
void tenantACannotUpdateTenantBOrder() {
    UUID tenantA = UUID.randomUUID();
    UUID tenantB = UUID.randomUUID();

    UUID orderB = insertOrderForTenant(tenantB);

    int updatedRows = mapper.updateStatusForTenant(
            tenantA,
            orderB,
            OrderStatus.CANCELLED,
            0L
    );

    assertEquals(0, updatedRows);
}
```

## 16.3 Search/list

```java id="a9miq3"
@Test
void searchOnlyReturnsOrdersForCurrentTenant() {
    UUID tenantA = UUID.randomUUID();
    UUID tenantB = UUID.randomUUID();

    insertOrderForTenant(tenantA);
    insertOrderForTenant(tenantB);

    List<OrderRecord> result = mapper.searchOrders(
            new OrderSearchCriteria(tenantA, null, 20)
    );

    assertEquals(1, result.size());
    assertEquals(tenantA, result.getFirst().tenantId());
}
```

Test matrix:

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Read tenant B order using tenant A | 404/empty |
| Update tenant B order using tenant A | 0 rows / 404 |
| Delete tenant B order using tenant A | 0 rows / forbidden/not found |
| Search with tenant A | Only tenant A rows |
| Count with tenant A | Only tenant A rows |
| Export with tenant A | Only tenant A rows |
| RLS enabled | DB blocks cross-tenant even if query misses filter |
| Same pooled connection after tenant A | Tenant B context not polluted |

---

# 17. SQL Injection Test Matrix

| Attack surface | Test |
|---|---|
| Sort field | `submitted_at desc; drop table orders; --` rejected before SQL |
| Sort direction | `DESC; delete from orders; --` rejected |
| Search text | Treated as value with `#{}`, not SQL |
| Filter enum | Invalid enum rejected by DTO deserialization/validation |
| ID path param | Invalid UUID rejected |
| Pagination size | Max enforced |
| Raw metadata key | Bounded and validated |
| IN list | Size bounded; values bound via `#{}` |
| XML mapper `${}` | Every occurrence reviewed |
| Query error | No SQL detail in API response |

Example:

```java id="5ziesy"
@Test
void shouldRejectInvalidSortField() {
    assertThrows(ValidationException.class, () -> {
        apiMapper.toCriteria(
                new SearchOrderRequest(
                        null,
                        null,
                        "submitted_at desc; drop table orders; --",
                        "DESC",
                        20
                ),
                tenantId
        );
    });
}
```

Better: model sort as enum so malicious string cannot deserialize.

---

# 18. PostgreSQL RLS Test

```java id="22c628"
@Test
void rlsShouldBlockRowsFromOtherTenant() {
    UUID tenantA = UUID.randomUUID();
    UUID tenantB = UUID.randomUUID();

    insertOrderForTenant(tenantB);

    transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        SecuritySqlMapper securityMapper =
                session.getMapper(SecuritySqlMapper.class);

        securityMapper.setCurrentTenant(tenantA);

        OrderSqlMapper orderMapper =
                session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

        List<OrderRecord> records = orderMapper.selectAllWithoutTenantFilter();

        assertTrue(records.isEmpty());

        return null;
    });
}
```

This test intentionally calls unsafe query to verify RLS defense-in-depth.

Checklist:

```text id="x5p9fe"
[ ] RLS test runs under same DB role as app_runtime.
[ ] Test uses pooled connection scenario.
[ ] Tenant context set with SET LOCAL / transaction-local setting.
[ ] Test proves missing tenant filter does not leak data.
```

---

# 19. DB Privilege Test

Use integration test or migration verification script:

```sql id="13pyq4"
SELECT has_table_privilege('app_runtime', 'app.orders', 'SELECT');
SELECT has_table_privilege('app_runtime', 'app.orders', 'INSERT');
SELECT has_table_privilege('app_runtime', 'app.orders', 'UPDATE');
SELECT has_table_privilege('app_runtime', 'app.orders', 'DELETE');
```

Negative expectation:

```sql id="kdem3x"
SELECT rolsuper
FROM pg_roles
WHERE rolname = 'app_runtime';
```

Should be false.

Checklist:

```text id="oyqfme"
[ ] app_runtime is not superuser.
[ ] app_runtime is not schema owner unless intended.
[ ] app_runtime cannot CREATE/DROP table.
[ ] app_runtime only has needed table/function privileges.
[ ] migration role separate.
```

# 20. Jersey/JAX-RS Integration Points

## 20.1 Security context extraction

```java id="5yprnw"
public final class ActorResolver {

    public AuthenticatedActor resolve(SecurityContext securityContext) {
        Principal principal = securityContext.getUserPrincipal();

        if (principal == null) {
            throw new UnauthorizedException();
        }

        return tokenClaimsResolver.resolve(principal);
    }
}
```

## 20.2 Command carries trusted context

```java id="9bvhdx"
public record CreateOrderCommand(
        TenantId tenantId,
        UserId actorUserId,
        UUID customerId,
        List<CreateOrderItemCommand> items,
        String note
) {}
```

## 20.3 API mapper receives trusted context separately

```java id="m0fmt3"
@Mapper(config = ApiMapperConfig.class)
public interface OrderApiMapper {

    @Mapping(target = "tenantId", source = "tenantId")
    @Mapping(target = "actorUserId", source = "actorUserId")
    CreateOrderCommand toCommand(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UserId actorUserId,
            CreateOrderRequest request
    );
}
```

Do not map `tenantId` from request body for normal user-facing commands.

# 21. Security PR Checklist

## 21.1 MyBatis XML

```text id="5rk6r8"
[ ] No new ${} without allow-list justification.
[ ] All user values use #{}.
[ ] Sort columns are enum/server controlled.
[ ] Filter criteria is typed, not raw SQL.
[ ] SELECT columns explicit.
[ ] No SELECT * for sensitive tables.
[ ] Tenant filter present in read/list/update/delete.
[ ] LIMIT present for list/search.
```

## 21.2 Service/repository

```text id="czoe27"
[ ] tenantId derived from authenticated context.
[ ] actorUserId derived from authenticated context.
[ ] Object-level authorization enforced.
[ ] Repository methods require tenant context.
[ ] Updates/deletes include tenant condition.
[ ] Cross-tenant tests updated.
```

## 21.3 DB

```text id="x2f73q"
[ ] Runtime DB role is least privilege.
[ ] Migration role separate.
[ ] RLS considered for high-risk multi-tenant data.
[ ] Sensitive columns access controlled.
[ ] Views/functions do not bypass policy accidentally.
```

## 21.4 Logging/error

```text id="t0wbta"
[ ] No secret/PII raw logs.
[ ] No raw SQL parameters in production logs.
[ ] SQLSTATE logged internally.
[ ] API response uses safe error code/message.
[ ] Correlation ID present.
```

---

# 22. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| `${sort}` dari query param | SQL injection | enum allow-list |
| `WHERE tenant_id = #{request.tenantId}` | tenant spoofing | server-derived tenant |
| Resource langsung panggil mapper | authorization bypass risk | resource → service → repository |
| Query by ID tanpa tenant | cross-tenant data leak | `findByIdForTenant` |
| Update/delete tanpa tenant | cross-tenant mutation | `WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}` |
| Log full SQL params | PII/secret leak | mapper name + duration + redacted fields |
| App DB user superuser | blast radius besar | least privilege runtime role |
| Migration role dipakai runtime | app bisa DDL/drop | separate runtime role |
| RLS dianggap satu-satunya security | policy/config bypass risk | app auth + RLS defense-in-depth |
| Error DB mentah ke client | information disclosure | SQLSTATE translator |

---

# 23. Production Checklist

```text id="2gsy87"
SQL injection
[ ] #{} used for all values.
[ ] ${} only for server-side allow-listed SQL fragments.
[ ] CI grep/review for ${}.
[ ] Malicious sort/filter tests exist.

Tenant isolation
[ ] tenantId server-derived.
[ ] Repository methods require tenantId.
[ ] Read/list/update/delete include tenant filter.
[ ] Cross-tenant read/update/search tests exist.
[ ] Optional RLS evaluated for defense-in-depth.

Authorization
[ ] Object-level permission checked in service/domain.
[ ] List/search visibility rules server-derived.
[ ] Empty permission scope returns empty, not all.

DB privilege
[ ] Runtime DB role least privilege.
[ ] Migration DB role separate.
[ ] PUBLIC/default grants reviewed.
[ ] Function EXECUTE grants explicit.

Logging/error
[ ] SQLSTATE logged.
[ ] SQL/table details not returned to client.
[ ] PII/secrets redacted.
[ ] Correlation ID included.

Testing
[ ] SQL injection test matrix.
[ ] Tenant isolation test matrix.
[ ] RLS test if used.
[ ] DB privilege verification.
[ ] Error response safety tests.
```

# Cheatsheet - MyBatis Repository & Domain Boundary Patterns  
## repository abstraction, persistence record vs domain, rehydration, aggregate loading, anti-corruption layer, mapping boundary

## 1. Introduction

Dalam stack **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis + PostgreSQL**, repository layer adalah batas antara **business/application code** dan **SQL/persistence detail**.

Tujuan utamanya:

```text id="mb-repo-001"
Jersey Resource tidak tahu SQL.
Application Service tidak tahu Mapper XML.
Domain Object tidak tahu MyBatis.
MyBatis Record tidak bocor ke API.
Response DTO tidak bocor dari table schema.
```

MyBatis memang memberi kontrol SQL eksplisit melalui mapper XML dan `resultMap`; dokumentasi MyBatis menyebut `resultMap` sebagai elemen paling kuat sekaligus kompleks untuk memuat object dari database result set. Karena itu, semakin penting untuk memisahkan **persistence shape** dari **domain/API shape** agar perubahan SQL/schema tidak langsung merusak domain dan API contract. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Tujuan | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository interface | Domain-friendly persistence contract | Service tidak tergantung MyBatis | Service langsung panggil mapper XML |
| Repository implementation | Bridge domain ↔ MyBatis | Encapsulate SQL details | Repository jadi business service |
| Persistence record | DB row/projection shape | Stabilkan mapping SQL | Record dipakai sebagai API DTO |
| Domain aggregate | Business state + invariant | Jaga rule bisnis | Domain jadi anemic data holder |
| Rehydration | Load domain dari DB | Restore aggregate secara valid | Constructor bypass invariant sembarangan |
| Persistence mapper | Domain ↔ record | Mapping boundary eksplisit | Mapping tersebar manual di service |
| Aggregate loading | Load root + child | Hindari N+1 dan row explosion | Nested select/list besar |
| Query model | Read projection | Optimalkan read/list/search | Memaksa aggregate untuk semua read |
| Anti-corruption layer | Isolasi external/legacy schema | Lindungi domain model | Domain ikut istilah DB/legacy |
| Error translation | DB/MyBatis error → domain/API error | Error aman dan stabil | SQLSTATE/raw SQL bocor |
| Transaction boundary | Service-level transaction | Atomic use case | Repository commit sendiri |
| Test boundary | Unit + integration | Buktikan mapping/transaction benar | Hanya happy-path resource test |

---

# 4. Layer Responsibility

| Layer | Boleh tahu | Tidak boleh tahu |
|---|---|---|
| Jersey Resource | DTO, validation, service, HTTP status | SQL, MyBatis XML, transaction detail |
| Application Service | command, repository, transaction, domain | JSON parser, SQL column name |
| Domain | business state, invariant, value object | database, MyBatis, HTTP, DTO |
| Repository Interface | domain object, domain ID, query intent | mapper XML, SQLSTATE |
| Repository Implementation | MyBatis mapper, record, transaction session | HTTP response |
| MyBatis Mapper | SQL parameter/result shape | domain behavior |
| Mapper XML | SQL, resultMap, dynamic SQL | API contract |
| OpenAPI | public DTO/error schema | DB columns/internal table |

Rule ringkas:

```text id="mb-repo-003"
Resource handles protocol.
Service handles use case.
Domain handles business rules.
Repository handles persistence abstraction.
MyBatis handles SQL.
PostgreSQL handles data integrity.
```

---

# 5. API DTO vs Command vs Domain vs Persistence Record

## 5.1 API Request DTO

```java id="mb-repo-004"
public record CreateOrderRequest(

        @NotNull
        UUID customerId,

        @NotEmpty
        List<@Valid CreateOrderItemRequest> items,

        @Size(max = 500)
        String note

) {}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-005"
Public HTTP input contract.
Contains validation annotations.
Must not contain DB columns like version, tenant_id, deleted_at.
```

---

## 5.2 Application Command

```java id="mb-repo-006"
public record CreateOrderCommand(
        TenantId tenantId,
        UserId actorUserId,
        UUID customerId,
        List<CreateOrderItemCommand> items,
        String note
) {}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-007"
Use-case input.
Contains trusted context such as tenantId and actorUserId.
Not tied to JSON serialization.
```

---

## 5.3 Domain Aggregate

```java id="mb-repo-008"
public final class Order {

    private final UUID id;
    private final TenantId tenantId;
    private final String orderNumber;
    private final UUID customerId;
    private final List<OrderItem> items;
    private OrderStatus status;
    private Money total;
    private long version;

    private Order(
            UUID id,
            TenantId tenantId,
            String orderNumber,
            UUID customerId,
            List<OrderItem> items,
            OrderStatus status,
            Money total,
            long version
    ) {
        this.id = Objects.requireNonNull(id);
        this.tenantId = Objects.requireNonNull(tenantId);
        this.orderNumber = requireNotBlank(orderNumber);
        this.customerId = Objects.requireNonNull(customerId);
        this.items = List.copyOf(items);
        this.status = Objects.requireNonNull(status);
        this.total = Objects.requireNonNull(total);
        this.version = version;

        validateInvariant();
    }

    public static Order create(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID customerId,
            List<OrderItem> items,
            OrderNumberGenerator orderNumberGenerator
    ) {
        if (items == null || items.isEmpty()) {
            throw new DomainException(
                    "ORDER_ITEMS_REQUIRED",
                    "Order must contain at least one item",
                    DomainErrorCategory.BUSINESS_RULE
            );
        }

        Money total = OrderCalculator.calculateTotal(items);

        return new Order(
                UUID.randomUUID(),
                tenantId,
                orderNumberGenerator.next(),
                customerId,
                items,
                OrderStatus.DRAFT,
                total,
                0L
        );
    }

    public static Order rehydrate(
            UUID id,
            TenantId tenantId,
            String orderNumber,
            UUID customerId,
            List<OrderItem> items,
            OrderStatus status,
            Money total,
            long version
    ) {
        return new Order(
                id,
                tenantId,
                orderNumber,
                customerId,
                items,
                status,
                total,
                version
        );
    }

    public void submit() {
        if (status != OrderStatus.DRAFT) {
            throw new DomainException(
                    "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_SUBMITTED",
                    "Order cannot be submitted in current state",
                    DomainErrorCategory.CONFLICT
            );
        }

        status = OrderStatus.SUBMITTED;
    }

    public void cancel(String reason) {
        if (status == OrderStatus.APPROVED) {
            throw new DomainException(
                    "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED",
                    "Approved order cannot be cancelled",
                    DomainErrorCategory.CONFLICT
            );
        }

        status = OrderStatus.CANCELLED;
    }

    private void validateInvariant() {
        if (items.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Order must contain items");
        }

        if (total.amount().compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) < 0) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Order total cannot be negative");
        }
    }

    private static String requireNotBlank(String value) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Value must not be blank");
        }

        return value;
    }

    public UUID id() {
        return id;
    }

    public TenantId tenantId() {
        return tenantId;
    }

    public String orderNumber() {
        return orderNumber;
    }

    public UUID customerId() {
        return customerId;
    }

    public List<OrderItem> items() {
        return items;
    }

    public OrderStatus status() {
        return status;
    }

    public Money total() {
        return total;
    }

    public long version() {
        return version;
    }
}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-009"
Business state + behavior.
Owns invariant.
Does not know MyBatis, SQL, DTO, HTTP, JSON.
```

## 5.4 MyBatis Persistence Record

```java id="mb-repo-010"
public record OrderRecord(
        UUID id,
        UUID tenantId,
        String orderNumber,
        UUID customerId,
        OrderStatus status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt,
        long version
) {}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-011"
Represents DB row/projection.
Matches mapper XML/resultMap.
May contain fields not exposed in API.
Should not contain business behavior.
```

---

## 5.5 API Response DTO

```java id="mb-repo-012"
public record OrderResponse(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatusDto status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-013"
Public output contract.
Stable for client.
Should not expose DB-specific/internal fields.
```

# 6. Boundary Decision Table

| Question | Put it in |
|---|---|
| “Is customerId required in HTTP request?” | Request DTO + Bean Validation |
| “Can submitted order be cancelled?” | Domain aggregate |
| “Should this use `SELECT FOR UPDATE`?” | Repository/MyBatis implementation |
| “What SQLSTATE maps to duplicate error?” | Persistence exception translator |
| “Should response include `internal_status`?” | API contract decision, usually no |
| “How to calculate total?” | Domain service/value object or aggregate |
| “How to join orders and items?” | MyBatis mapper/repository |
| “How to transform domain result to response?” | MapStruct/API mapper |
| “How to enforce tenant filter?” | Service/repository + optionally PostgreSQL RLS |
| “How to return 409?” | ExceptionMapper |

---

# 7. Repository Interface Pattern

Repository interface should speak **domain language**, not SQL language.

## 7.1 Good Repository Interface

```java id="mb-repo-014"
public interface OrderRepository {

    void save(Order order);

    Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);

    Optional<Order> findByIdForUpdate(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);

    List<Order> findSubmittedOrdersForCustomer(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID customerId,
            int limit
    );

    boolean existsByOrderNumber(TenantId tenantId, String orderNumber);
}
```

Good because:

```text id="mb-repo-015"
[ ] Uses domain terms.
[ ] Requires tenant context.
[ ] Hides MyBatis mapper.
[ ] Hides SQL table/column details.
[ ] Returns domain aggregate where mutation is needed.
```

---

## 7.2 Bad Repository Interface

```java id="mb-repo-016"
public interface OrderRepository {

    List<Map<String, Object>> executeQuery(String sql);

    OrderRecord selectFromOrdersTable(UUID id);

    void updateOrdersStatusColumn(UUID id, String status);

    OrderResponse findResponseById(UUID id);
}
```

Problems:

```text id="mb-repo-017"
[ ] SQL leaks into application layer.
[ ] Persistence record leaks upward.
[ ] API DTO leaks downward.
[ ] No tenant context.
[ ] Repository becomes generic DAO without domain intent.
```

---

# 8. Repository Implementation with MyBatis

```java id="mb-repo-018"
public final class MyBatisOrderRepository implements OrderRepository {

    private final OrderSqlMapper sqlMapper;
    private final OrderPersistenceMapper persistenceMapper;

    public MyBatisOrderRepository(
            SqlSession session,
            OrderPersistenceMapper persistenceMapper
    ) {
        this.sqlMapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);
        this.persistenceMapper = persistenceMapper;
    }

    @Override
    public void save(Order order) {
        OrderRecord existing = sqlMapper.findByIdForTenant(
                order.tenantId().value(),
                order.id()
        );

        if (existing == null) {
            insert(order);
        } else {
            update(order);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId) {
        OrderRecord record = sqlMapper.findByIdForTenant(
                tenantId.value(),
                orderId
        );

        if (record == null) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }

        List<OrderItemRecord> items =
                sqlMapper.findItemsByOrderIdForTenant(
                        tenantId.value(),
                        orderId
                );

        return Optional.of(persistenceMapper.toDomain(record, items));
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<Order> findByIdForUpdate(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID orderId
    ) {
        OrderRecord record = sqlMapper.findByIdForTenantForUpdate(
                tenantId.value(),
                orderId
        );

        if (record == null) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }

        List<OrderItemRecord> items =
                sqlMapper.findItemsByOrderIdForTenant(
                        tenantId.value(),
                        orderId
                );

        return Optional.of(persistenceMapper.toDomain(record, items));
    }

    private void insert(Order order) {
        OrderRecord orderRecord = persistenceMapper.toRecord(order);
        sqlMapper.insertOrder(orderRecord);

        List<OrderItemRecord> itemRecords =
                persistenceMapper.toItemRecords(order);

        for (OrderItemRecord item : itemRecords) {
            sqlMapper.insertOrderItem(item);
        }
    }

    private void update(Order order) {
        OrderRecord orderRecord = persistenceMapper.toRecord(order);

        int rows = sqlMapper.updateOrder(orderRecord);

        if (rows == 0) {
            throw new PersistenceException(
                    "VERSION_CONFLICT",
                    "Resource version conflict",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT
            );
        }
    }

    @Override
    public List<Order> findSubmittedOrdersForCustomer(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID customerId,
            int limit
    ) {
        List<OrderRecord> records =
                sqlMapper.findSubmittedOrdersForCustomer(
                        tenantId.value(),
                        customerId,
                        limit
                );

        if (records.isEmpty()) {
            return List.of();
        }

        List<UUID> orderIds = records.stream()
                .map(OrderRecord::id)
                .toList();

        List<OrderItemRecord> items =
                sqlMapper.findItemsByOrderIdsForTenant(
                        tenantId.value(),
                        orderIds
                );

        Map<UUID, List<OrderItemRecord>> itemsByOrderId =
                items.stream()
                        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(
                                OrderItemRecord::orderId
                        ));

        return records.stream()
                .map(record -> persistenceMapper.toDomain(
                        record,
                        itemsByOrderId.getOrDefault(
                                record.id(),
                                List.of()
                        )
                ))
                .toList();
    }

    @Override
    public boolean existsByOrderNumber(
            TenantId tenantId,
            String orderNumber
    ) {
        return sqlMapper.existsByOrderNumber(
                tenantId.value(),
                orderNumber
        );
    }
}
```

Important:

```text id="mb-repo-019"
Repository implementation may know MyBatis.
Repository interface should not.
Application service should depend on repository interface.
```

# 9. MyBatis Mapper Interface

```java id="mb-repo-020"
public interface OrderSqlMapper {

    OrderRecord findByIdForTenant(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("id") UUID id
    );

    OrderRecord findByIdForTenantForUpdate(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("id") UUID id
    );

    List<OrderItemRecord> findItemsByOrderIdForTenant(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("orderId") UUID orderId
    );

    List<OrderItemRecord> findItemsByOrderIdsForTenant(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("orderIds") List<UUID> orderIds
    );

    void insertOrder(OrderRecord record);

    void insertOrderItem(OrderItemRecord record);

    int updateOrder(OrderRecord record);

    List<OrderRecord> findSubmittedOrdersForCustomer(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("customerId") UUID customerId,
            @Param("limit") int limit
    );

    boolean existsByOrderNumber(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("orderNumber") String orderNumber
    );
}
```

Guideline:

```text id="mb-repo-021"
MyBatis mapper interface may expose SQL operation shape.
Repository hides it from application/domain.
```

# 10. Mapper XML

```xml id="mb-repo-022"
<mapper namespace="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderSqlMapper">

    <resultMap id="OrderRecordResultMap"
               type="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderRecord">
        <id property="id" column="id"/>
        <result property="tenantId" column="tenant_id"/>
        <result property="orderNumber" column="order_number"/>
        <result property="customerId" column="customer_id"/>
        <result property="status" column="status"
                typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.OrderStatusTypeHandler"/>
        <result property="totalAmount" column="total_amount"/>
        <result property="currency" column="currency"/>
        <result property="submittedAt" column="submitted_at"
                typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.InstantTypeHandler"/>
        <result property="version" column="version"/>
    </resultMap>

    <sql id="OrderColumns">
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at,
        version
    </sql>

    <select id="findByIdForTenant" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
        SELECT
            <include refid="OrderColumns"/>
        FROM orders
        WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
          AND id = #{id}
    </select>

    <select id="findByIdForTenantForUpdate"
            resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
        SELECT
            <include refid="OrderColumns"/>
        FROM orders
        WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
          AND id = #{id}
        FOR UPDATE
    </select>

    <insert id="insertOrder"
            parameterType="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderRecord">
        INSERT INTO orders (
            id,
            tenant_id,
            order_number,
            customer_id,
            status,
            total_amount,
            currency,
            submitted_at,
            version
        ) VALUES (
            #{id},
            #{tenantId},
            #{orderNumber},
            #{customerId},
            #{status},
            #{totalAmount},
            #{currency},
            #{submittedAt},
            #{version}
        )
    </insert>

    <update id="updateOrder"
            parameterType="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderRecord">
        UPDATE orders
        SET
            status = #{status},
            total_amount = #{totalAmount},
            currency = #{currency},
            version = version + 1,
            updated_at = now()
        WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
          AND id = #{id}
          AND version = #{version}
    </update>

</mapper>
```

MyBatis mapper XML supports mapped statements like `select`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, SQL fragments, and `resultMap`; this makes mapper XML the right place for SQL shape, not for business workflow. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
