# 11. Persistence Mapper Pattern

MapStruct is useful for structural mapping because it generates type-safe mapper implementations at compile time using normal Java method calls, without reflection. ([mapstruct.org](https://mapstruct.org/documentation/stable/reference/html/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.1 Structural persistence mapping with MapStruct

```java id="mb-repo-023"
@Mapper(config = ApiMapperConfig.class)
public interface OrderPersistenceMapper {

    @Mapping(target = "tenantId", source = "tenantId.value")
    @Mapping(target = "totalAmount", source = "total.amount")
    @Mapping(target = "currency", source = "total.currency")
    OrderRecord toRecord(Order order);

    List<OrderItemRecord> toItemRecords(Order order);

    default Order toDomain(
            OrderRecord record,
            List<OrderItemRecord> itemRecords
    ) {
        List<OrderItem> items = itemRecords.stream()
                .map(this::toDomainItem)
                .toList();

        return Order.rehydrate(
                record.id(),
                new TenantId(record.tenantId()),
                record.orderNumber(),
                record.customerId(),
                items,
                record.status(),
                new Money(record.totalAmount(), record.currency()),
                record.version()
        );
    }

    default OrderItem toDomainItem(OrderItemRecord record) {
        return OrderItem.rehydrate(
                record.id(),
                record.productId(),
                record.quantity(),
                new Money(record.unitPrice(), record.currency())
        );
    }
}
```

## 11.2 When manual mapper is better

Use manual mapper when:

```text id="mb-repo-024"
[ ] Domain rehydration must call factory/rehydrate method.
[ ] Constructor has invariant checks.
[ ] Value object creation can fail.
[ ] Mapping needs domain semantic translation.
[ ] You need careful handling for legacy/null DB values.
```

Example manual mapper:

```java id="mb-repo-025"
public final class OrderPersistenceMapper {

    public OrderRecord toRecord(Order order) {
        return new OrderRecord(
                order.id(),
                order.tenantId().value(),
                order.orderNumber(),
                order.customerId(),
                order.status(),
                order.total().amount(),
                order.total().currency(),
                order.submittedAt(),
                order.version()
        );
    }

    public Order toDomain(
            OrderRecord record,
            List<OrderItemRecord> itemRecords
    ) {
        List<OrderItem> items = itemRecords.stream()
                .map(this::toDomainItem)
                .toList();

        return Order.rehydrate(
                record.id(),
                new TenantId(record.tenantId()),
                record.orderNumber(),
                record.customerId(),
                items,
                record.status(),
                new Money(record.totalAmount(), record.currency()),
                record.version()
        );
    }

    private OrderItem toDomainItem(OrderItemRecord record) {
        return OrderItem.rehydrate(
                record.id(),
                record.productId(),
                record.quantity(),
                new Money(record.unitPrice(), record.currency())
        );
    }
}
```

Decision rule:

```text id="mb-repo-026"
Use MapStruct for straightforward structural mapping.
Use manual mapper for invariant-rich rehydration.
Never let mapper silently bypass important domain rules.
```

---

# 12. Rehydration Pattern

Rehydration adalah proses membuat ulang domain aggregate dari persisted state.

## 12.1 Creation vs Rehydration

| Operation | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| New business object | `Order.create(...)` | Apply creation rules |
| Load from DB | `Order.rehydrate(...)` | Restore known persisted state |
| State transition | `order.submit()` / `order.cancel()` | Apply business transition |
| API response | `OrderResponse` mapping | Public output |

Example:

```java id="mb-repo-027"
Order newOrder = Order.create(
        tenantId,
        customerId,
        items,
        orderNumberGenerator
);

Order existingOrder = Order.rehydrate(
        record.id(),
        new TenantId(record.tenantId()),
        record.orderNumber(),
        record.customerId(),
        items,
        record.status(),
        new Money(record.totalAmount(), record.currency()),
        record.version()
);
```

## 12.2 Rehydration rules

```text id="mb-repo-028"
[ ] Rehydration should not generate new ID.
[ ] Rehydration should not generate new order number.
[ ] Rehydration should not reset version.
[ ] Rehydration should still protect impossible state.
[ ] Rehydration may tolerate legacy state only with explicit migration/compatibility policy.
```

---

# 13. Aggregate Loading Patterns

## 13.1 Aggregate root + child collection

```text id="mb-repo-029"
Order aggregate:
  Order root
    ├─ OrderItem
    ├─ OrderItem
    └─ OrderItem
```

Repository method:

```java id="mb-repo-030"
Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);
```

Implementation options:

| Option | Pattern | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Join nested result | `collection` resultMap | One SQL | Row duplication/resultMap complexity |
| Manual two-query | parent query + child query | Clear and testable | Two SQL |
| Batch child load | parent page + child query by IDs | Avoid N+1 | More code |
| Separate endpoint | parent list, child detail separately | Fast list | More API calls |

---

## 13.2 Detail endpoint

For detail by ID:

```java id="mb-repo-031"
public Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId) {
    OrderRecord order = sqlMapper.findByIdForTenant(
            tenantId.value(),
            orderId
    );

    if (order == null) {
        return Optional.empty();
    }

    List<OrderItemRecord> items =
            sqlMapper.findItemsByOrderIdForTenant(
                    tenantId.value(),
                    orderId
            );

    return Optional.of(persistenceMapper.toDomain(order, items));
}
```

Good because:

```text id="mb-repo-032"
[ ] Easy to reason.
[ ] Easy to test.
[ ] Avoids duplicate parent rows.
[ ] Good for one aggregate by ID.
```

---

## 13.3 List/search endpoint

Do not load full aggregate graph for every list row unless required.

Bad:

```java id="mb-repo-033"
List<Order> orders = repository.searchFullAggregates(criteria);
```

Better read model:

```java id="mb-repo-034"
public record OrderSummaryRecord(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatus status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

Mapper:

```java id="mb-repo-035"
List<OrderSummaryRecord> searchOrderSummaries(OrderSearchCriteria criteria);
```

API response:

```java id="mb-repo-036"
public record OrderSummaryResponse(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatusDto status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

Rule:

```text id="mb-repo-037"
Use full aggregate for commands and detail behavior.
Use read projection for list/search/report.
```

---

# 14. Command vs Query Repository Split

For complex systems, split command and query persistence.

## 14.1 Command repository

```java id="mb-repo-038"
public interface OrderRepository {

    Optional<Order> findByIdForUpdate(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);

    void save(Order order);
}
```

## 14.2 Query repository

```java id="mb-repo-039"
public interface OrderQueryRepository {

    PageResult<OrderSummaryProjection> searchSummaries(
            OrderSearchCriteria criteria
    );

    Optional<OrderDetailProjection> findDetail(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID orderId
    );
}
```

Why split:

```text id="mb-repo-040"
Command side needs domain aggregate and invariants.
Query side needs optimized projection and pagination.
Forcing both through one aggregate model often causes overfetching.
```

---

# 15. Anti-Corruption Layer Pattern

Anti-corruption layer protects your domain model from external/legacy schema.

## 15.1 Legacy table example

Legacy DB:

```text id="mb-repo-041"
LEG_ORD_HDR
  ORD_ID
  CUST_NO
  STAT_CD
  TOT_AMT
  CURR_CD
  CRT_TS
```

Do not let these names infect domain:

Bad domain:

```java id="mb-repo-042"
public final class LegOrdHdr {
    private String statCd;
    private BigDecimal totAmt;
}
```

Better persistence record:

```java id="mb-repo-043"
public record LegacyOrderHeaderRecord(
        String ordId,
        String custNo,
        String statCd,
        BigDecimal totAmt,
        String currCd,
        Instant crtTs
) {}
```

Domain:

```java id="mb-repo-044"
public final class Order {
    private UUID id;
    private UUID customerId;
    private OrderStatus status;
    private Money total;
}
```

Mapper:

```java id="mb-repo-045"
public final class LegacyOrderMapper {

    public Order toDomain(LegacyOrderHeaderRecord record) {
        return Order.rehydrate(
                parseOrderId(record.ordId()),
                resolveCustomerId(record.custNo()),
                mapStatus(record.statCd()),
                new Money(record.totAmt(), record.currCd()),
                0L
        );
    }

    private OrderStatus mapStatus(String statCd) {
        return switch (statCd) {
            case "N" -> OrderStatus.DRAFT;
            case "S" -> OrderStatus.SUBMITTED;
            case "A" -> OrderStatus.APPROVED;
            case "X" -> OrderStatus.CANCELLED;
            default -> OrderStatus.UNKNOWN_LEGACY;
        };
    }
}
```

Rule:

```text id="mb-repo-046"
Legacy terms stay in infrastructure.
Domain uses business language.
Mapping translates between them.
```

---

# 16. Repository and Transaction Boundary

Repository should not own transaction globally unless it is an implementation detail within service transaction.

## 16.1 Recommended

```java id="mb-repo-047"
public OrderResult cancel(CancelOrderCommand command) {
    return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);

        Order order = repository.findByIdForUpdate(
                command.tenantId(),
                command.orderId()
        ).orElseThrow(() -> DomainException.notFound("ORDER_NOT_FOUND"));

        order.cancel(command.reason());

        repository.save(order);

        return OrderResult.from(order);
    });
}
```

## 16.2 Avoid

```java id="mb-repo-048"
public final class MyBatisOrderRepository {

    public void save(Order order) {
        try (SqlSession session = factory.openSession()) {
            mapper.insert(...);
            session.commit();
        }
    }
}
```

Why avoid:

```text id="mb-repo-049"
If one use case needs multiple repositories,
each repository committing independently breaks atomicity.
```

---

# 17. Domain Events and Repository Boundary

If domain emits events, do not publish external events before DB commit.

## 17.1 Domain records events

```java id="mb-repo-050"
public final class Order {

    private final List<DomainEvent> domainEvents = new ArrayList<>();

    public void submit() {
        if (status != OrderStatus.DRAFT) {
            throw new DomainException(
                    "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_SUBMITTED",
                    "Order cannot be submitted in current state",
                    DomainErrorCategory.CONFLICT
            );
        }

        status = OrderStatus.SUBMITTED;

        domainEvents.add(new OrderSubmittedEvent(id, tenantId, Instant.now()));
    }

    public List<DomainEvent> pullDomainEvents() {
        List<DomainEvent> events = List.copyOf(domainEvents);
        domainEvents.clear();
        return events;
    }
}
```

## 17.2 Service saves aggregate + outbox in same transaction

```java id="mb-repo-051"
public OrderResult submit(SubmitOrderCommand command) {
    return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository orderRepository =
                orderRepositoryFactory.create(session);

        OutboxRepository outboxRepository =
                outboxRepositoryFactory.create(session);

        Order order = orderRepository.findByIdForUpdate(
                command.tenantId(),
                command.orderId()
        ).orElseThrow(() -> DomainException.notFound("ORDER_NOT_FOUND"));

        order.submit();

        orderRepository.save(order);

        for (DomainEvent event : order.pullDomainEvents()) {
            outboxRepository.save(event);
        }

        return OrderResult.from(order);
    });
}
```

Rule:

```text id="mb-repo-052"
Domain can create events.
Service persists events transactionally.
Publisher sends events after commit through outbox worker.
```

---

# 18. Error Translation Boundary

## 18.1 Repository should translate persistence errors

```java id="mb-repo-053"
public final class PersistenceExceptionTranslator {

    public RuntimeException translate(RuntimeException exception) {
        SQLException sqlException = findSqlException(exception);

        if (sqlException == null) {
            return new PersistenceException(
                    "PERSISTENCE_ERROR",
                    "Persistence operation failed",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.UNKNOWN,
                    exception
            );
        }

        return switch (sqlException.getSQLState()) {
            case "23505" -> new PersistenceException(
                    "DUPLICATE_RESOURCE",
                    "Resource already exists",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
                    exception
            );
            case "23503" -> new PersistenceException(
                    "REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND",
                    "Referenced resource was not found",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
                    exception
            );
            case "40001", "40P01" -> new PersistenceException(
                    "CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION",
                    "Resource was modified concurrently",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.RETRYABLE_CONFLICT,
                    exception
            );
            default -> new PersistenceException(
                    "PERSISTENCE_ERROR",
                    "Persistence operation failed",
                    PersistenceErrorCategory.UNKNOWN,
                    exception
            );
        };
    }
}
```

## 18.2 Application service should not catch SQL exception directly

Bad:

```java id="mb-repo-054"
try {
    orderSqlMapper.insertOrder(record);
} catch (SQLException exception) {
    return Response.status(500).build();
}
```

Better:

```text id="mb-repo-055"
MyBatis/SQL exception
  → PersistenceExceptionTranslator
  → PersistenceException
  → ExceptionMapper
  → ApiErrorResponse
```

---

# 19. Read Projection Pattern

Not every read needs full domain aggregate.

## 19.1 Projection record

```java id="mb-repo-056"
public record OrderListProjection(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatus status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

## 19.2 Query repository

```java id="mb-repo-057"
public interface OrderQueryRepository {

    List<OrderListProjection> search(OrderSearchCriteria criteria);

    Optional<OrderDetailProjection> findDetail(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UUID orderId
    );
}
```

## 19.3 MyBatis mapper

```java id="mb-repo-058"
public interface OrderQuerySqlMapper {

    List<OrderListProjection> searchOrderList(OrderSearchCriteria criteria);

    OrderDetailProjection findOrderDetail(
            @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
            @Param("id") UUID id
    );
}
```

Rule:

```text id="mb-repo-059"
Use query projections for read-only screens.
Use aggregate loading for behavior-changing commands.
```

---

# 20. Aggregate Boundary Heuristics

Use aggregate when:

```text id="mb-repo-060"
[ ] You need enforce invariant.
[ ] You are changing lifecycle state.
[ ] Multiple child rows must stay consistent.
[ ] Operation needs version/locking.
[ ] Domain method expresses business behavior.
```

Use projection when:

```text id="mb-repo-061"
[ ] Read-only list/search.
[ ] Data comes from multiple aggregates.
[ ] You need only summary fields.
[ ] You need optimized SQL.
[ ] No domain behavior is executed.
```

Avoid:

```text id="mb-repo-062"
Loading full aggregate graph for every list screen.
Using projection for command that must enforce invariant.
```

---

# 21. Mapping Boundary Checklist

## 21.1 API Mapper

DTO ↔ Command/Result.

```java id="mb-repo-063"
@Mapper(config = ApiMapperConfig.class)
public interface OrderApiMapper {

    CreateOrderCommand toCommand(
            TenantId tenantId,
            UserId actorUserId,
            CreateOrderRequest request
    );

    OrderResponse toResponse(OrderResult result);
}
```

## 21.2 Persistence Mapper

Domain ↔ Record.

```java id="mb-repo-064"
public final class OrderPersistenceMapper {

    public OrderRecord toRecord(Order order) {
        ...
    }

    public Order toDomain(
            OrderRecord record,
            List<OrderItemRecord> items
    ) {
        ...
    }
}
```

## 21.3 Never cross these boundaries

```text id="mb-repo-065"
[NO] Resource → OrderSqlMapper
[NO] Resource → OrderRecord
[NO] Domain → OrderRecord
[NO] Domain → SqlSession
[NO] MyBatis XML → API DTO
[NO] OpenAPI → DB column names
```

---

# 22. Common Repository Patterns

## 22.1 Save pattern

```java id="mb-repo-066"
void save(Order order);
```

Good when repository owns insert/update decision.

Caution:

```text id="mb-repo-067"
Needs clear rule:
- Is order new or existing?
- Does version decide update?
- Should duplicate insert become 409?
```

---

## 22.2 Explicit insert/update pattern

```java id="mb-repo-068"
void insert(Order order);

void update(Order order);
```

Good when use case knows lifecycle.

Caution:

```text id="mb-repo-069"
Application service should not become SQL-aware.
```

---

## 22.3 `findByIdForUpdate`

```java id="mb-repo-070"
Optional<Order> findByIdForUpdate(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId);
```

Good for state transition.

Caution:

```text id="mb-repo-071"
Only call inside transaction.
Keep transaction short.
Avoid external calls while row locked.
```

---

## 22.4 `existsBy...`

```java id="mb-repo-072"
boolean existsByOrderNumber(TenantId tenantId, String orderNumber);
```

Useful for early validation.

Caution:

```text id="mb-repo-073"
Do not rely only on exists check for uniqueness.
Still need DB unique constraint.
Race condition can happen between exists and insert.
```

---

## 22.5 Count/search

```java id="mb-repo-074"
PageResult<OrderListProjection> search(OrderSearchCriteria criteria);
```

Caution:

```text id="mb-repo-075"
Count query can be expensive.
Consider cursor pagination or estimated counts for large data.
```

# 23. Testing Strategy

## 23.1 Domain unit test

```java id="mb-repo-076"
@Test
void submittedOrderCannotBeSubmittedAgain() {
    Order order = OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder();

    DomainException exception = assertThrows(
            DomainException.class,
            order::submit
    );

    assertEquals("ORDER_CANNOT_BE_SUBMITTED", exception.code());
}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-077"
Business rule test without DB.
Fast and focused.
```

---

## 23.2 Persistence mapper test

```java id="mb-repo-078"
@Test
void shouldMapOrderToRecordAndBack() {
    Order order = OrderTestFactory.draftOrder();

    OrderRecord record = persistenceMapper.toRecord(order);

    Order rehydrated = persistenceMapper.toDomain(
            record,
            persistenceMapper.toItemRecords(order)
    );

    assertEquals(order.id(), rehydrated.id());
    assertEquals(order.status(), rehydrated.status());
    assertEquals(order.total(), rehydrated.total());
}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-079"
Verify domain ↔ record mapping.
```

---

## 23.3 Repository integration test

```java id="mb-repo-080"
@Test
void shouldSaveAndLoadOrderAggregate() {
    TenantId tenantId = TenantId.random();
    Order order = OrderTestFactory.draftOrder(tenantId);

    transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);
        repository.save(order);
        return null;
    });

    Order loaded = transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);
        return repository.findById(tenantId, order.id()).orElseThrow();
    });

    assertEquals(order.id(), loaded.id());
    assertEquals(order.orderNumber(), loaded.orderNumber());
    assertEquals(order.items().size(), loaded.items().size());
}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-081"
Verify MyBatis XML + resultMap + repository + mapper + PostgreSQL.
```

---

## 23.4 Tenant boundary test

```java id="mb-repo-082"
@Test
void shouldNotLoadOrderFromAnotherTenant() {
    TenantId tenantA = TenantId.random();
    TenantId tenantB = TenantId.random();

    Order orderB = OrderTestFactory.draftOrder(tenantB);
    save(orderB);

    Optional<Order> result = transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository repository = repositoryFactory.create(session);
        return repository.findById(tenantA, orderB.id());
    });

    assertTrue(result.isEmpty());
}
```

Purpose:

```text id="mb-repo-083"
Prevent cross-tenant data leak.
```

---

## 23.5 Query projection test

```java id="mb-repo-084"
@Test
void shouldSearchOrderSummariesWithoutLoadingFullAggregate() {
    TenantId tenantId = TenantId.random();

    save(OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder(tenantId));
    save(OrderTestFactory.cancelledOrder(tenantId));

    List<OrderListProjection> result =
            queryRepository.search(new OrderSearchCriteria(
                    tenantId,
                    OrderStatus.SUBMITTED,
                    20
            ));

    assertEquals(1, result.size());
    assertEquals(OrderStatus.SUBMITTED, result.getFirst().status());
}
```

```text id="mb-repo-085"
Verify read model / projection query.
```

# 24. Review Checklist

## 24.1 Repository interface

```text id="mb-repo-086"
[ ] Uses domain language.
[ ] Requires tenant/security context where needed.
[ ] Does not expose MyBatis mapper.
[ ] Does not expose persistence record unless explicitly query-side.
[ ] Has clear command vs query intent.
[ ] Does not return Map<String,Object>.
```

## 24.2 Repository implementation

```text id="mb-repo-087"
[ ] Uses SqlSession from service transaction.
[ ] Does not commit/rollback independently unless designed.
[ ] Uses persistence mapper.
[ ] Translates persistence exceptions.
[ ] Enforces tenant filter in mapper calls.
[ ] Avoids N+1 for list/search.
```

## 24.3 Domain

```text id="mb-repo-088"
[ ] Domain object has behavior, not only getters/setters.
[ ] Invariants live in domain.
[ ] Domain does not import MyBatis/JAX-RS/Jackson.
[ ] Rehydrate path is explicit.
[ ] Impossible states are rejected or handled intentionally.
```

## 24.4 Persistence record

```text id="mb-repo-089"
[ ] Represents DB row/projection.
[ ] Not exposed in API response.
[ ] Does not contain business behavior.
[ ] Matches mapper XML resultMap.
[ ] Has TypeHandler for custom enum/time/jsonb if needed.
```

## 24.5 Mapping

```text id="mb-repo-090"
[ ] API mapper and persistence mapper are separate.
[ ] Sensitive/internal fields not mapped to response.
[ ] Domain value objects are reconstructed safely.
[ ] MapStruct unmapped target policy catches drift where used.
[ ] Manual mapper used where domain rehydration is semantic.
```

---

# 25. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Resource calls MyBatis mapper directly | HTTP, auth, SQL mixed | Resource → service → repository |
| Repository returns API DTO | API tied to DB query | Query projection → API mapper |
| Domain object has MyBatis annotations/imports | Domain polluted | Separate persistence record |
| `OrderRecord` used as domain | No behavior/invariant | Domain aggregate + mapper |
| Full aggregate for every list | Slow overfetch | Read projection |
| Nested select on large list | N+1 query | Batch child loading |
| Repository commits itself | Broken multi-repository transaction | Service-level transaction |
| Mapper does business decisions | Logic hidden in infrastructure | Domain/service |
| DB enum value crashes `valueOf` unexpectedly | Runtime 500 | TypeHandler + compatibility policy |
| No rehydration method | Constructor misuse | Explicit `rehydrate(...)` |

---

# 26. Practical “Which Model Should I Use?” Guide

```text id="mb-repo-091"
Incoming JSON?
  → Request DTO

Use case input?
  → Command

Business behavior?
  → Domain aggregate/entity/value object

Database row?
  → Persistence record

SQL query result for list/read-only?
  → Query projection

Outgoing JSON?
  → Response DTO

Failure response?
  → ApiErrorResponse

Persistence failure?
  → PersistenceException → ExceptionMapper
```

---

# 27. Production Checklist

```text id="mb-repo-092"
Architecture
[ ] API DTO, command, domain, record, response DTO are separated.
[ ] Resource does not call MyBatis directly.
[ ] Service owns transaction boundary.
[ ] Repository hides MyBatis details.

Domain
[ ] Business invariants live in domain.
[ ] Rehydration explicit.
[ ] Domain has no infrastructure imports.
[ ] State transition methods are tested.

Repository
[ ] Interface uses domain language.
[ ] Methods are tenant-scoped.
[ ] findByIdForUpdate only used inside transaction.
[ ] Save/update checks affected rows for optimistic lock.
[ ] Persistence errors translated.

MyBatis
[ ] Mapper XML resultMap matches record.
[ ] SQL columns explicit.
[ ] No raw user input in ${}.
[ ] List/search avoids N+1.
[ ] Query projections used for read-only screens.

Mapping
[ ] API mapper separate from persistence mapper.
[ ] Sensitive fields are not mapped to response.
[ ] TypeHandler covers enum/time/jsonb.
[ ] Mapper tests exist.

Testing
[ ] Domain unit tests.
[ ] Persistence mapper tests.
[ ] Repository integration tests with PostgreSQL.
[ ] Tenant boundary tests.
[ ] Query projection tests.
[ ] Transaction rollback/conflict tests.
```

# Cheatsheet - PostgreSQL Function / Procedure + MyBatis Deep Dive  
## PL/pgSQL function/procedure, callable statement, result mapping, error mapping, transaction behavior, migration/versioning, integration testing

## 1. Introduction

Di stack **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis + PostgreSQL**, function dan procedure bisa sangat berguna, tapi harus dipakai dengan disiplin. Jangan semua business logic dipindah ke database hanya karena bisa. Gunakan function/procedure untuk kasus yang memang **data-intensive, atomic, reusable, dekat dengan database, atau butuh SQL/PL/pgSQL expressiveness**.

Mental model utamanya:

```text id="pgfunc-001"
PostgreSQL function
  → dipanggil dengan SELECT
  → cocok untuk return scalar/table/query result
  → sering lebih mudah dimapping oleh MyBatis sebagai <select>

PostgreSQL procedure
  → dipanggil dengan CALL
  → cocok untuk operation/side-effect DB-side
  → di MyBatis biasanya pakai statementType="CALLABLE"
```

PostgreSQL documentation menyatakan bahwa function dipanggil dengan `SELECT`, sedangkan procedure dipanggil dengan `CALL`; `CALL` membutuhkan privilege `EXECUTE`, dan transaction control di dalam procedure hanya diperbolehkan dalam kondisi tertentu. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-call.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 2. Diagram

```text id="pgfunc-002"
Jersey Resource
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
Transaction Boundary
  ↓
Repository
  ↓
MyBatis Mapper Interface
  ↓
Mapper XML
  ├─ <select> SELECT my_function(...)
  ├─ <select> SELECT * FROM table_function(...)
  ├─ <update statementType="CALLABLE"> CALL my_procedure(...)
  └─ <select affectData="true"> INSERT/UPDATE ... RETURNING ...
  ↓
PostgreSQL
  ├─ SQL function
  ├─ PL/pgSQL function
  ├─ procedure
  ├─ RAISE EXCEPTION
  ├─ SQLSTATE
  └─ transaction / lock / constraint
```

---

# 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Kapan dipakai | Risiko utama |
|---|---|---|---|
| SQL function | `LANGUAGE sql` | Query wrapper, scalar/table return sederhana | Jadi tempat logic kompleks tersembunyi |
| PL/pgSQL function | `LANGUAGE plpgsql` | Branching, validation DB-side, loops, exception | Business logic split app/DB |
| Table-returning function | `RETURNS TABLE` | Search/reporting projection reusable | Return columns berubah → resultMap drift |
| Procedure | `CREATE PROCEDURE` + `CALL` | DB-side operation/maintenance/batch | Transaction behavior membingungkan |
| MyBatis `<select>` for function | `SELECT fn(...)` | Scalar/table result | Salah resultMap/resultType |
| MyBatis `CALLABLE` | `statementType="CALLABLE"` | Procedure/callable statement | OUT param mapping/provider-specific behavior |
| `RETURNING` mapping | `<select affectData="true">` | Insert/update returning rows | Salah pakai `<insert>` untuk return data |
| Error mapping | `RAISE EXCEPTION`, SQLSTATE | Stable DB-side business/persistence errors | Raw DB message bocor ke API |
| Transaction behavior | app transaction vs procedure transaction | Consistency/rollback | Procedure mencoba commit di transaction block |
| Versioning | function/procedure signature lifecycle | Backward compatibility | Mapper XML rusak saat signature berubah |
| Migration | Flyway/Liquibase repeatable/versioned | Deploy DB code | Replace function breaking old app |
| Integration test | PostgreSQL nyata | Prove behavior | Mock tidak menangkap DB behavior |

---

# 4. Function vs Procedure Decision Table

| Need | Prefer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Return one scalar value | Function | `SELECT calculate_total(...)` simple |
| Return result set/table | Function | `SELECT * FROM search_orders(...)` maps naturally |
| Use in SQL query / join | Function | Function can appear in SQL expression/from clause |
| Perform DB-side operation | Procedure | `CALL close_old_orders(...)` expresses action |
| Need transaction control inside DB code | Procedure, top-level only | PostgreSQL restricts transaction control |
| Called from MyBatis and maps result rows | Function | Easier with `<select resultMap=...>` |
| Called as command with no result | Procedure or function returning void | Procedure clearer for operation |
| Needs stable API contract | Either, but version carefully | Signature is contract |
| Complex business workflow | Usually application service | Keep workflow visible/testable in Java |

PostgreSQL `CREATE FUNCTION` supports table-returning functions via `RETURNS TABLE(...)`, and PostgreSQL docs show `SELECT * FROM function(...)` for table function consumption. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createfunction.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 5. PostgreSQL Function Patterns

## 5.1 Scalar SQL Function

Use when computation is simple and close to data.

```sql id="pgfunc-003"
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION calculate_order_total(p_order_id uuid)
RETURNS numeric
LANGUAGE sql
AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(quantity * unit_price), 0)
    FROM order_items
    WHERE order_id = p_order_id
$$;
```

MyBatis mapper interface:

```java id="pgfunc-004"
public interface OrderFunctionSqlMapper {

    BigDecimal calculateOrderTotal(@Param("orderId") UUID orderId);
}
```

Mapper XML:

```xml id="pgfunc-005"
<select id="calculateOrderTotal" resultType="java.math.BigDecimal">
    SELECT calculate_order_total(#{orderId})
</select>
```

Use for:

```text id="pgfunc-006"
[OK] DB-side aggregate calculation.
[OK] Reusable SQL expression.
[OK] Simple deterministic calculation.
```

Avoid for:

```text id="pgfunc-007"
[NO] Multi-step workflow with external side effects.
[NO] Logic that should be unit-tested as Java domain logic.
[NO] Logic that needs API/security context not present in DB.
```

---

## 5.2 Table-Returning SQL Function

Good for reusable read projection.

```sql id="pgfunc-008"
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION search_order_summaries(
    p_tenant_id uuid,
    p_status text,
    p_limit integer
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    id uuid,
    order_number text,
    status text,
    total_amount numeric,
    currency text,
    submitted_at timestamptz
)
LANGUAGE sql
AS $$
    SELECT
        o.id,
        o.order_number,
        o.status,
        o.total_amount,
        o.currency,
        o.submitted_at
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.tenant_id = p_tenant_id
      AND (p_status IS NULL OR o.status = p_status)
    ORDER BY o.submitted_at DESC, o.id DESC
    LIMIT p_limit
$$;
```

Record:

```java id="pgfunc-009"
public record OrderSummaryRecord(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatus status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

MyBatis resultMap:

```xml id="pgfunc-010"
<resultMap id="OrderSummaryResultMap"
           type="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderSummaryRecord">
    <id property="id" column="id"/>
    <result property="orderNumber" column="order_number"/>
    <result property="status" column="status"
            typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.OrderStatusTypeHandler"/>
    <result property="totalAmount" column="total_amount"/>
    <result property="currency" column="currency"/>
    <result property="submittedAt" column="submitted_at"
            typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.InstantTypeHandler"/>
</resultMap>

<select id="searchOrderSummaries"
        resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at
    FROM search_order_summaries(
        #{tenantId},
        #{status},
        #{limit}
    )
</select>
```

PostgreSQL docs show `RETURNS TABLE(...)` as a way to return multiple columns from a function, and the returned table function is selected from like a relation. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createfunction.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Checklist:

```text id="pgfunc-011"
[ ] Function return columns are explicit.
[ ] MyBatis resultMap matches function output.
[ ] No SELECT * in mapper if output may evolve.
[ ] Function has integration test.
[ ] Function signature/version is migration-governed.
```

---

## 5.3 PL/pgSQL Function with Branching

Use PL/pgSQL when SQL function is not enough.

```sql id="pgfunc-012"
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION can_cancel_order(
    p_order_id uuid
)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_status text;
BEGIN
    SELECT status
    INTO v_status
    FROM orders
    WHERE id = p_order_id;

    IF v_status IS NULL THEN
        RETURN false;
    END IF;

    IF v_status IN ('APPROVED', 'CANCELLED') THEN
        RETURN false;
    END IF;

    RETURN true;
END;
$$;
```

Mapper:

```xml id="pgfunc-013"
<select id="canCancelOrder" resultType="boolean">
    SELECT can_cancel_order(#{orderId})
</select>
```

But ask first:

```text id="pgfunc-014"
Should this rule be in Java domain instead?
```

For cancellation rule specifically, often better:

```text id="pgfunc-015"
Load aggregate → order.cancel(reason) → save.
```

Use DB function for:

```text id="pgfunc-016"
[OK] data-heavy validation
[OK] reusable query logic
[OK] enforcing DB-side invariant close to data
```

Avoid DB function for:

```text id="pgfunc-017"
[NO] core lifecycle rule that Java domain should own
[NO] behavior requiring external service calls
[NO] behavior that must be transparent to app developers
```

---

# 6. PostgreSQL Procedure Patterns

## 6.1 Basic Procedure

```sql id="pgfunc-018"
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE close_old_submitted_orders(
    p_cutoff timestamptz
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    UPDATE orders
    SET
        status = 'CLOSED',
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE status = 'SUBMITTED'
      AND submitted_at < p_cutoff;
END;
$$;
```

MyBatis mapper:

```java id="pgfunc-019"
public interface OrderProcedureSqlMapper {

    void closeOldSubmittedOrders(@Param("cutoff") Instant cutoff);
}
```

Mapper XML:

```xml id="pgfunc-020"
<update id="closeOldSubmittedOrders"
        statementType="CALLABLE">
    CALL close_old_submitted_orders(#{cutoff})
</update>
```

MyBatis supports `statementType` values `STATEMENT`, `PREPARED`, and `CALLABLE`, which map to JDBC `Statement`, `PreparedStatement`, and `CallableStatement`. ([mybatis.org](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 6.2 Procedure with OUT Parameters

PostgreSQL procedure can have output parameters, and `CALL` can return an output row. For MyBatis/JDBC, OUT/INOUT parameters are mapped through parameter properties with `mode=OUT` or `mode=INOUT`. MyBatis documentation states that `mode` can specify `IN`, `OUT`, or `INOUT`, and OUT/INOUT values mutate the passed parameter object property. ([mybatis.org](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Procedure:

```sql id="pgfunc-021"
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE cancel_order_proc(
    IN p_tenant_id uuid,
    IN p_order_id uuid,
    IN p_reason text,
    OUT p_cancelled boolean,
    OUT p_error_code text
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_status text;
BEGIN
    SELECT status
    INTO v_status
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = p_tenant_id
      AND id = p_order_id
    FOR UPDATE;

    IF v_status IS NULL THEN
        p_cancelled := false;
        p_error_code := 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND';
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    IF v_status = 'APPROVED' THEN
        p_cancelled := false;
        p_error_code := 'ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED';
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    UPDATE orders
    SET
        status = 'CANCELLED',
        cancel_reason = p_reason,
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE tenant_id = p_tenant_id
      AND id = p_order_id;

    p_cancelled := true;
    p_error_code := NULL;
END;
$$;
```

Parameter object:

```java id="pgfunc-022"
public final class CancelOrderProcedureParams {

    private UUID tenantId;
    private UUID orderId;
    private String reason;
    private Boolean cancelled;
    private String errorCode;

    public UUID getTenantId() {
        return tenantId;
    }

    public void setTenantId(UUID tenantId) {
        this.tenantId = tenantId;
    }

    public UUID getOrderId() {
        return orderId;
    }

    public void setOrderId(UUID orderId) {
        this.orderId = orderId;
    }

    public String getReason() {
        return reason;
    }

    public void setReason(String reason) {
        this.reason = reason;
    }

    public Boolean getCancelled() {
        return cancelled;
    }

    public void setCancelled(Boolean cancelled) {
        this.cancelled = cancelled;
    }

    public String getErrorCode() {
        return errorCode;
    }

    public void setErrorCode(String errorCode) {
        this.errorCode = errorCode;
    }
}
```

Mapper interface:

```java id="pgfunc-023"
void cancelOrder(CancelOrderProcedureParams params);
```

Mapper XML:

```xml id="pgfunc-024"
<update id="cancelOrder"
        parameterType="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.CancelOrderProcedureParams"
        statementType="CALLABLE">
    CALL cancel_order_proc(
        #{tenantId, mode=IN, jdbcType=OTHER},
        #{orderId, mode=IN, jdbcType=OTHER},
        #{reason, mode=IN, jdbcType=VARCHAR},
        #{cancelled, mode=OUT, jdbcType=BOOLEAN},
        #{errorCode, mode=OUT, jdbcType=VARCHAR}
    )
</update>
```

Caution:

```text id="pgfunc-025"
OUT parameter behavior can be driver/database sensitive.
For PostgreSQL, many teams prefer function returning a row/table if the goal is result mapping.
Use integration tests with real PostgreSQL before standardizing procedure OUT params.
```

---

# 7. Prefer Function Returning Result for MyBatis Mapping

For many app use cases, a function returning table/record is easier than procedure OUT params.

```sql id="pgfunc-026"
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cancel_order_fn(
    p_tenant_id uuid,
    p_order_id uuid,
    p_reason text
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    cancelled boolean,
    error_code text,
    id uuid,
    status text,
    version bigint
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_status text;
BEGIN
    SELECT o.status
    INTO v_status
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.tenant_id = p_tenant_id
      AND o.id = p_order_id
    FOR UPDATE;

    IF v_status IS NULL THEN
        RETURN QUERY
        SELECT false, 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND', NULL::uuid, NULL::text, NULL::bigint;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    IF v_status = 'APPROVED' THEN
        RETURN QUERY
        SELECT false, 'ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED', p_order_id, v_status, NULL::bigint;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    UPDATE orders o
    SET
        status = 'CANCELLED',
        cancel_reason = p_reason,
        version = o.version + 1,
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE o.tenant_id = p_tenant_id
      AND o.id = p_order_id
    RETURNING
        true,
        NULL::text,
        o.id,
        o.status,
        o.version
    INTO cancelled, error_code, id, status, version;

    RETURN NEXT;
END;
$$;
```

Result record:

```java id="pgfunc-027"
public record CancelOrderDbResult(
        Boolean cancelled,
        String errorCode,
        UUID id,
        OrderStatus status,
        Long version
) {}
```

MyBatis:

```xml id="pgfunc-028"
<resultMap id="CancelOrderDbResultMap"
           type="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.CancelOrderDbResult">
    <result property="cancelled" column="cancelled"/>
    <result property="errorCode" column="error_code"/>
    <id property="id" column="id"/>
    <result property="status" column="status"
            typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.OrderStatusTypeHandler"/>
    <result property="version" column="version"/>
</resultMap>

<select id="cancelOrderUsingFunction"
        resultMap="CancelOrderDbResultMap">
    SELECT
        cancelled,
        error_code,
        id,
        status,
        version
    FROM cancel_order_fn(
        #{tenantId},
        #{orderId},
        #{reason}
    )
</select>
```

Interface:

```java id="pgfunc-029"
CancelOrderDbResult cancelOrderUsingFunction(
        @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
        @Param("orderId") UUID orderId,
        @Param("reason") String reason
);
```

Why often better:

```text id="pgfunc-030"
[ ] MyBatis maps result rows naturally.
[ ] Easier to test.
[ ] Easier to version return shape.
[ ] Avoids OUT param surprises.
```

---

# 8. `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ... RETURNING` with MyBatis

PostgreSQL supports `RETURNING` clauses for DML. MyBatis documentation notes that statements returning result sets, such as PostgreSQL `RETURNING`, should be written as `<select>` to map returned data; it also documents `affectData="true"` for data-changing statements that return data. ([mybatis.org](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 8.1 Insert and return row

```xml id="pgfunc-031"
<select id="insertOrderReturning"
        resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap"
        affectData="true"
        flushCache="true">
    INSERT INTO orders (
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at,
        version
    ) VALUES (
        #{id},
        #{tenantId},
        #{orderNumber},
        #{customerId},
        #{status},
        #{totalAmount},
        #{currency},
        #{submittedAt},
        #{version}
    )
    RETURNING
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at,
        version
</select>
```

Mapper:

```java id="pgfunc-032"
OrderRecord insertOrderReturning(OrderRecord record);
```

Use when:

```text id="pgfunc-033"
[OK] DB fills default/generated fields.
[OK] Need inserted row immediately.
[OK] Want one round trip.
```

---

## 8.2 Update and return row

```xml id="pgfunc-034"
<select id="cancelOrderReturning"
        resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap"
        affectData="true"
        flushCache="true">
    UPDATE orders
    SET
        status = 'CANCELLED',
        cancel_reason = #{reason},
        version = version + 1,
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND id = #{orderId}
      AND version = #{expectedVersion}
    RETURNING
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at,
        version
</select>
```

Mapper:

```java id="pgfunc-035"
OrderRecord cancelOrderReturning(
        @Param("tenantId") UUID tenantId,
        @Param("orderId") UUID orderId,
        @Param("reason") String reason,
        @Param("expectedVersion") long expectedVersion
);
```

If no row returned:

```text id="pgfunc-036"
Either not found, tenant mismatch, or version conflict.
Repository must distinguish if needed.
```

---

# 9. Error Handling in PL/pgSQL

PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL supports `RAISE` for errors/messages, and if no SQLSTATE is specified for `RAISE EXCEPTION`, the default SQLSTATE is `P0001` (`raise_exception`). ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/plpgsql-errors-and-messages.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 9.1 Raise custom error

```sql id="pgfunc-037"
RAISE EXCEPTION 'Order cannot be cancelled'
    USING
        ERRCODE = 'P0001',
        DETAIL = 'Approved order cannot be cancelled',
        HINT = 'Refresh order state';
```

But for application mapping, avoid parsing text:

```text id="pgfunc-038"
Do not parse message text.
Use SQLSTATE and/or structured return error_code.
```

PostgreSQL error codes are five-character SQLSTATE codes, and applications should usually test error code rather than textual message because codes are more stable and not localized. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 9.2 Custom SQLSTATE strategy

PostgreSQL allows custom SQLSTATE values other than `00000`; use a consistent internal convention if you choose this route. Prefer documenting a registry.

```sql id="pgfunc-039"
RAISE EXCEPTION 'Order cannot be cancelled'
    USING ERRCODE = 'P1001';
```

Java translator:

```java id="pgfunc-040"
return switch (sqlException.getSQLState()) {
    case "P1001" -> new PersistenceException(
            "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED",
            "Order cannot be cancelled in current state",
            PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
            original
    );
    case "23505" -> new PersistenceException(
            "DUPLICATE_RESOURCE",
            "Resource already exists",
            PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT,
            original
    );
    default -> unknown(original);
};
```

Caution:

```text id="pgfunc-041"
[ ] Custom SQLSTATE must be documented.
[ ] Do not overload same SQLSTATE for unrelated errors.
[ ] Prefer structured function result for expected business outcomes.
[ ] Use exceptions for exceptional cases, not normal branch flow.
```

---

# 10. Expected Business Outcome vs Exception

| Situation | Prefer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Order not found in cancel command | Domain exception or structured DB result | Expected business failure |
| Order cannot be cancelled | Domain exception or structured DB result | Expected business rule |
| Duplicate key | SQLSTATE translation | DB integrity conflict |
| Deadlock | SQLSTATE + retry | Infrastructure concurrency |
| Invalid function argument due to bug | Exception | Should be fixed |
| Procedure internal invariant breach | Exception with SQLSTATE | Unexpected or critical |

Rule:

```text id="pgfunc-042"
Expected business branch should usually be explicit result.
Unexpected DB failure should be exception.
```

---

# 11. Transaction Behavior

## 11.1 Procedure transaction control

PostgreSQL procedure transaction control has restrictions. `CALL` inside a transaction block prevents the called procedure from executing transaction control statements; transaction control is only possible from top-level `CALL` or certain nested `CALL`/`DO` cases without intervening commands. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-call.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com), [postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/plpgsql-transactions.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Implication for Jersey/MyBatis:

```text id="pgfunc-043"
If application service already opens transaction:
  procedure should not COMMIT/ROLLBACK internally.

If procedure needs transaction control:
  do not wrap it in app transaction.
  call it as top-level operation with explicit operational design.
```

## 11.2 Recommended default

```text id="pgfunc-044"
Default for microservice:
  Java application service owns transaction.
  Procedure/function participates in that transaction.
  DB code does not COMMIT/ROLLBACK internally.
```

Why:

```text id="pgfunc-045"
[ ] Easier rollback.
[ ] Service can coordinate multiple repositories.
[ ] Outbox can be saved in same transaction.
[ ] Testing is clearer.
```

---

# 12. Repository Pattern for Function/Procedure

## 12.1 Keep function/procedure behind repository

Bad:

```java id="pgfunc-046"
@POST
@Path("/{id}/cancel")
public Response cancel(@PathParam("id") UUID id) {
    sqlMapper.cancelOrderUsingFunction(...);
    return Response.ok().build();
}
```

Better:

```java id="pgfunc-047"
public final class OrderService {

    public OrderResult cancel(CancelOrderCommand command) {
        return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderRepository repository =
                    orderRepositoryFactory.create(session);

            return repository.cancelUsingDbFunction(
                    command.tenantId(),
                    command.orderId(),
                    command.reason()
            );
        });
    }
}
```

Repository:

```java id="pgfunc-048"
public OrderResult cancelUsingDbFunction(
        TenantId tenantId,
        UUID orderId,
        String reason
) {
    CancelOrderDbResult result = sqlMapper.cancelOrderUsingFunction(
            tenantId.value(),
            orderId,
            reason
    );

    if (result == null || !Boolean.TRUE.equals(result.cancelled())) {
        throw mapCancelFailure(result);
    }

    return new OrderResult(
            result.id(),
            result.status(),
            result.version()
    );
}
```

Mapping failure:

```java id="pgfunc-049"
private RuntimeException mapCancelFailure(CancelOrderDbResult result) {
    String code = result == null
            ? "ORDER_CANCEL_FAILED"
            : result.errorCode();

    return switch (code) {
        case "ORDER_NOT_FOUND" -> new DomainException(
                "ORDER_NOT_FOUND",
                "Order was not found",
                DomainErrorCategory.NOT_FOUND
        );
        case "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED" -> new DomainException(
                "ORDER_CANNOT_BE_CANCELLED",
                "Order cannot be cancelled in current state",
                DomainErrorCategory.CONFLICT
        );
        default -> new PersistenceException(
                "PERSISTENCE_ERROR",
                "Persistence operation failed",
                PersistenceErrorCategory.UNKNOWN
        );
    };
}
```

---

# 13. Function/Procedure Versioning

Function/procedure signature is a contract.

## 13.1 Breaking changes

```text id="pgfunc-050"
[BREAKING] Rename function.
[BREAKING] Remove parameter.
[BREAKING] Change parameter type.
[BREAKING] Change return column name.
[BREAKING] Change return column type.
[BREAKING] Remove return column used by resultMap.
[BREAKING] Change error_code values.
```

## 13.2 Safer versioning

```sql id="pgfunc-051"
CREATE FUNCTION search_order_summaries_v1(...)
RETURNS TABLE (...);

CREATE FUNCTION search_order_summaries_v2(...)
RETURNS TABLE (...);
```

Mapper XML:

```xml id="pgfunc-052"
<select id="searchOrderSummariesV1" resultMap="OrderSummaryV1ResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM search_order_summaries_v1(
        #{tenantId},
        #{status},
        #{limit}
    )
</select>

<select id="searchOrderSummariesV2" resultMap="OrderSummaryV2ResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        reference_number,
        status,
        priority
    FROM search_order_summaries_v2(
        #{tenantId},
        #{status},
        #{priority},
        #{limit}
    )
</select>
```

Use versioned functions when:

```text id="pgfunc-053"
[ ] Old app version may still run.
[ ] Rolling deploy means v1 and v2 app coexist.
[ ] Rollback app version must remain possible.
[ ] Return shape changes.
```

---

# 14. Migration Strategy

## 14.1 Versioned migration for table/function contract changes

```text id="pgfunc-054"
V202607130001__create_order_functions.sql
V202607130002__create_cancel_order_fn_v2.sql
V202607130003__switch_mapper_to_v2.sql
V202607130004__drop_cancel_order_fn_v1.sql
```

## 14.2 Repeatable migrations for replaceable views/functions

Example Flyway:

```text id="pgfunc-055"
R__order_functions.sql
```

Caution:

```text id="pgfunc-056"
Repeatable function replacement is convenient,
but can break old app during rolling deploy if signature/return shape changes.
```

Safer:

```text id="pgfunc-057"
Use repeatable migrations for non-breaking body changes.
Use versioned new function name for breaking signature/return changes.
```

---

# 15. PostgreSQL Function Volatility / Security Notes

For functions, PostgreSQL supports attributes like volatility classification and security behavior in `CREATE FUNCTION`. Treat these as production design decisions, not decoration. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createfunction.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Practical guidance:

```text id="pgfunc-058"
[ ] Use correct volatility category when defining function.
[ ] Avoid SECURITY DEFINER unless truly needed.
[ ] If using SECURITY DEFINER, lock down search_path.
[ ] Grant EXECUTE explicitly.
[ ] Avoid giving app runtime broad privileges just to call one function.
```

Security-definer functions can be dangerous if search path and privileges are not controlled. Keep function ownership and grants explicit.

---

# 16. MyBatis Mapping Patterns

## 16.1 Scalar return

```xml id="pgfunc-059"
<select id="calculateOrderTotal" resultType="java.math.BigDecimal">
    SELECT calculate_order_total(#{orderId})
</select>
```

## 16.2 Table return with resultMap

```xml id="pgfunc-060"
<select id="searchOrderSummaries" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at
    FROM search_order_summaries(
        #{tenantId},
        #{status},
        #{limit}
    )
</select>
```

## 16.3 Procedure call with no result

```xml id="pgfunc-061"
<update id="closeOldSubmittedOrders"
        statementType="CALLABLE"
        timeout="30">
    CALL close_old_submitted_orders(#{cutoff})
</update>
```

## 16.4 Procedure call with OUT params

```xml id="pgfunc-062"
<update id="cancelOrder"
        parameterType="CancelOrderProcedureParams"
        statementType="CALLABLE">
    CALL cancel_order_proc(
        #{tenantId, mode=IN, jdbcType=OTHER},
        #{orderId, mode=IN, jdbcType=OTHER},
        #{reason, mode=IN, jdbcType=VARCHAR},
        #{cancelled, mode=OUT, jdbcType=BOOLEAN},
        #{errorCode, mode=OUT, jdbcType=VARCHAR}
    )
</update>
```

## 16.5 DML returning row

```xml id="pgfunc-063"
<select id="updateOrderReturning"
        resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap"
        affectData="true"
        flushCache="true">
    UPDATE orders
    SET status = #{status}
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND id = #{id}
    RETURNING
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        customer_id,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at,
        version
</select>
```

MyBatis documentation specifically notes that PostgreSQL `RETURNING`-style statements should be written as `<select>` if they return result sets. ([mybatis.org](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 17. Error Mapping Matrix

| DB-side signal | Where produced | MyBatis receives | Java mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RETURN error_code` | function result | result row | map to DomainException |
| `RAISE EXCEPTION ERRCODE 'P1001'` | PL/pgSQL | SQLException SQLSTATE | PersistenceExceptionTranslator |
| unique violation `23505` | constraint | SQLException SQLSTATE | `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE` |
| FK violation `23503` | constraint | SQLException SQLSTATE | `REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| deadlock `40P01` | DB concurrency | SQLException SQLSTATE | retryable conflict |
| serialization `40001` | isolation conflict | SQLException SQLSTATE | retryable conflict |

Preferred pattern:

```text id="pgfunc-064"
Expected business failure:
  structured result error_code

Unexpected/infrastructure failure:
  SQLSTATE exception translation
```

---

# 18. Integration Testing

Function/procedure must be tested with real PostgreSQL.

## 18.1 Testcontainers skeleton

```java id="pgfunc-065"
@Testcontainers
class OrderFunctionMapperIT {

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
            new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16")
                    .withDatabaseName("app_test")
                    .withUsername("test")
                    .withPassword("test");

    private static SqlSessionFactory sqlSessionFactory;

    @BeforeAll
    static void setup() {
        DataSource dataSource = buildDataSource(postgres);
        runMigrations(dataSource);
        sqlSessionFactory = buildSqlSessionFactory(dataSource);
    }

    @Test
    void shouldCalculateOrderTotal() {
        UUID orderId = insertOrderWithItems();

        try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession()) {
            OrderFunctionSqlMapper mapper =
                    session.getMapper(OrderFunctionSqlMapper.class);

            BigDecimal total = mapper.calculateOrderTotal(orderId);

            assertEquals(new BigDecimal("100.00"), total);
        }
    }

    @Test
    void shouldSearchOrderSummariesUsingFunction() {
        UUID tenantId = insertTenantWithOrders();

        try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession()) {
            OrderFunctionSqlMapper mapper =
                    session.getMapper(OrderFunctionSqlMapper.class);

            List<OrderSummaryRecord> records =
                    mapper.searchOrderSummaries(
                            tenantId,
                            OrderStatus.SUBMITTED,
                            20
                    );

            assertFalse(records.isEmpty());
        }
    }
}
```

## 18.2 Procedure test

```java id="pgfunc-066"
@Test
void shouldCloseOldSubmittedOrders() {
    Instant cutoff = Instant.parse("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z");

    UUID oldOrder = insertSubmittedOrderBefore(cutoff);
    UUID newOrder = insertSubmittedOrderAfter(cutoff);

    try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession(false)) {
        OrderProcedureSqlMapper mapper =
                session.getMapper(OrderProcedureSqlMapper.class);

        mapper.closeOldSubmittedOrders(cutoff);
        session.commit();
    }

    assertEquals(OrderStatus.CLOSED, findStatus(oldOrder));
    assertEquals(OrderStatus.SUBMITTED, findStatus(newOrder));
}
```

# 19. Test Matrix

| Pattern | Test |
|---|---|
| Scalar function | Input → expected scalar |
| Table function | Result columns map to record |
| PL/pgSQL branch | Each branch returns expected result |
| Procedure side effect | Rows changed correctly |
| OUT params | Parameter object mutated correctly |
| DML returning | Returned row mapped correctly |
| Error code result | Expected error_code maps to domain error |
| RAISE SQLSTATE | SQLSTATE translator maps correctly |
| Transaction rollback | Procedure/function changes rollback with app transaction |
| Procedure transaction control | Test top-level vs app transaction behavior if used |
| Versioned function | v1 and v2 coexist during migration |
| Security grants | runtime role has only EXECUTE needed |
| Tenant isolation | function/procedure includes tenant scope |
| Performance | EXPLAIN for function body/query where needed |

# 20. Security Checklist

```text id="pgfunc-067"
[ ] Function/procedure parameters use #{...}.
[ ] No user input goes into ${...}.
[ ] tenant_id is server-derived.
[ ] Function/procedure filters by tenant where needed.
[ ] Runtime role has EXECUTE only where needed.
[ ] SECURITY DEFINER avoided unless required.
[ ] SECURITY DEFINER uses safe search_path if used.
[ ] Function/procedure does not expose internal table details in error.
[ ] Error text not parsed by application.
```

---

# 21. Review Checklist

## 21.1 Design

```text id="pgfunc-068"
[ ] Is DB function/procedure actually justified?
[ ] Could this be simpler in Java service/domain?
[ ] Is this data-heavy enough to live in DB?
[ ] Is the signature stable?
[ ] Is return shape stable?
[ ] Is tenant/security context handled?
```

## 21.2 MyBatis

```text id="pgfunc-069"
[ ] Function returning rows uses <select>.
[ ] PostgreSQL RETURNING uses <select affectData="true">.
[ ] Procedure uses statementType="CALLABLE" when appropriate.
[ ] OUT params have mode/jdbcType.
[ ] resultMap matches return columns.
[ ] TypeHandler applied for enum/time/jsonb.
```

## 21.3 Transaction

```text id="pgfunc-070"
[ ] App service owns transaction by default.
[ ] Procedure does not COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside app transaction.
[ ] Long-running procedure has timeout strategy.
[ ] Locking behavior documented.
[ ] Retry behavior documented for SQLSTATE 40001/40P01.
```

## 21.4 Migration

```text id="pgfunc-071"
[ ] New function/procedure migration included.
[ ] Breaking signature change uses versioned function name.
[ ] Old app compatibility considered.
[ ] Rollback/forward-fix plan exists.
[ ] Integration tests run from empty DB and upgraded DB.
```

---

# 22. Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Semua business logic pindah ke PL/pgSQL | Java domain kehilangan rule | Domain/service for workflow |
| Function return `SELECT *` | resultMap drift | Explicit columns |
| Procedure commits inside service transaction | Runtime error/transaction confusion | App owns transaction |
| Parse DB error message text | Fragile/localization issue | SQLSTATE/error_code |
| Replace function signature in-place | Rolling deploy break | Versioned function |
| Function ignores tenant_id | Cross-tenant leak | Tenant parameter + filter/RLS |
| OUT param without integration test | Driver/runtime surprise | Test with PostgreSQL |
| `SECURITY DEFINER` casually | Privilege escalation risk | Avoid or harden |
| Raw SQL fragment in function params | SQL injection | Typed parameters |
| Procedure used for UI request long job | Request timeout/lock | Async job/batch worker |
