# Cheatsheet - JSONB / Advanced PostgreSQL Types with MyBatis  
## JSONB, array, enum, range type, TypeHandler, indexing, query pattern, schema governance, integration testing

## 1. Introduction

PostgreSQL punya tipe data yang kaya: `jsonb`, array, enum, range/multirange, UUID, temporal, numeric, dan user-defined types. Di stack **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis**, tipe-tipe ini berguna, tetapi harus dipakai dengan governance yang jelas.

Tujuan seri ini:

```text id="pgadv-001"
[ ] Memakai tipe PostgreSQL advanced tanpa membocorkan detail DB ke API.
[ ] Memetakan tipe advanced ke Java dengan TypeHandler yang jelas.
[ ] Memilih index yang cocok untuk JSONB/array/range.
[ ] Menjaga schema governance agar JSONB tidak menjadi “schema liar”.
[ ] Menambahkan integration test karena behavior-nya PostgreSQL-specific.
```

PostgreSQL mendokumentasikan `json` dan `jsonb` sebagai tipe JSON native; `jsonb` menyimpan data dalam format decomposed binary sehingga input sedikit lebih lambat, tetapi pemrosesan jauh lebih cepat dan mendukung indexing. PostgreSQL juga menyediakan array multidimensi, range/multirange, enum, dan tipe native lain yang bisa dipakai bila sesuai kebutuhan. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-json.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 2. Diagram

```text id="pgadv-002"
Jersey API DTO
  ↓
Bean Validation
  ↓
Application Command / Domain
  ↓
Repository Boundary
  ↓
Persistence Record
  ↓
MyBatis TypeHandler
  ├─ JsonNode / Map / Value Object ↔ jsonb
  ├─ List<String> / String[] ↔ text[]
  ├─ Java enum ↔ text / PostgreSQL enum
  ├─ Range value object ↔ tstzrange / int4range / daterange
  └─ Instant / BigDecimal / UUID ↔ PostgreSQL native type
  ↓
Mapper XML
  ├─ resultMap
  ├─ typeHandler
  ├─ JSONB operators
  ├─ array operators
  ├─ range operators
  └─ index-aware SQL
  ↓
PostgreSQL
```

---

# 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Kapan dipakai | Risiko utama |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSONB storage | `jsonb` column | Flexible metadata, external payload, event payload | Menjadi schema liar |
| JSONB query | `@>`, `?`, `->`, `->>` | Search by JSON key/value | Index tidak sesuai operator |
| JSONB TypeHandler | Java ↔ `jsonb` | `JsonNode`, `Map`, typed value object | JSON parse error runtime |
| Array type | `text[]`, `uuid[]`, etc. | Small tag/list value | Normalization/relational constraint lemah |
| Array query | `ANY`, `&&`, `@>` | Tag overlap/contains | Index/operator mismatch |
| Enum type | text + check / PG enum / lookup table | Status/category | Evolution sulit |
| Range type | `daterange`, `tstzrange`, `int4range` | Validity period, booking, price period | Bound semantics salah |
| Range index | GiST / SP-GiST | Overlap/contains query | Full scan jika salah index |
| TypeHandler | Custom conversion | Advanced type mapping | MyBatis tidak tahu DB type otomatis |
| Schema governance | JSON schema/versioning | Data quality | Unknown JSON shape |
| Index governance | GIN/GiST/expression/partial index | Performance | Index bloat/write overhead |
| Integration test | PostgreSQL nyata | Validate mapping/query/index | Mock tidak cukup |

MyBatis `TypeHandler` dipakai untuk mengubah Java type ke/dari JDBC type. Dokumentasi MyBatis menekankan bahwa MyBatis tidak selalu menginspeksi metadata database untuk menentukan tipe kolom, sehingga type handler kadang harus disebut eksplisit pada parameter/result mapping agar tepat. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/configuration.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 4. JSONB: Kapan Dipakai dan Kapan Tidak

## 4.1 Cocok untuk JSONB

```text id="pgadv-003"
[OK] Metadata yang optional dan berubah-ubah.
[OK] Payload eksternal yang perlu disimpan apa adanya.
[OK] Event/outbox payload.
[OK] Audit snapshot.
[OK] Feature flags/config kecil.
[OK] Projection tambahan yang tidak selalu dipakai.
```

## 4.2 Hindari JSONB untuk

```text id="pgadv-004"
[NO] Core business fields yang wajib.
[NO] Field yang selalu difilter/join/agregasi.
[NO] Data yang perlu foreign key.
[NO] Data yang butuh strong relational constraints.
[NO] Field yang menjadi API contract utama.
[NO] Pengganti desain schema karena malas migration.
```

Rule praktis:

```text id="pgadv-005"
Jika field menjadi wajib, sering dicari, sering diurutkan, atau perlu constraint,
promote dari JSONB ke kolom typed.
```

---

# 5. JSONB Column Design

## 5.1 Table

```sql id="pgadv-006"
CREATE TABLE orders (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    order_number text NOT NULL,
    status text NOT NULL,
    metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Checklist:

```text id="pgadv-007"
[ ] DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb jika object metadata.
[ ] DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb jika array payload.
[ ] NOT NULL jika app tidak ingin null ambiguity.
[ ] CHECK jsonb_typeof(metadata) = 'object' jika object wajib.
[ ] Size/shape governance di aplikasi.
```

Example constraint:

```sql id="pgadv-008"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD CONSTRAINT orders_metadata_is_object
CHECK (jsonb_typeof(metadata) = 'object');
```

---

# 6. JSONB Java Representation

## 6.1 `JsonNode`

Good for flexible but structured processing.

```java id="pgadv-009"
public record OrderMetadataRecord(
        UUID orderId,
        JsonNode metadata
) {}
```

Use when:

```text id="pgadv-010"
[OK] Need tree access.
[OK] Need preserve JSON shape.
[OK] Need partial dynamic structure.
```

## 6.2 `Map<String, Object>`

Use carefully.

```java id="pgadv-011"
public record OrderMetadataRecord(
        UUID orderId,
        Map<String, Object> metadata
) {}
```

Risk:

```text id="pgadv-012"
[ ] Numeric type ambiguity: Integer/Long/Double/BigDecimal.
[ ] Nested type unchecked.
[ ] Harder schema governance.
```

## 6.3 Typed value object

Best for governed JSONB.

```java id="pgadv-013"
public record OrderMetadata(
        String sourceSystem,
        String externalReference,
        Map<String, String> attributes
) {}
```

Use when:

```text id="pgadv-014"
[OK] JSON shape is known.
[OK] You want validation.
[OK] You want versioned metadata schema.
```

---

# 7. JSONB TypeHandler with `JsonNode`

PostgreSQL JDBC supports Java access through standard JDBC, and PostgreSQL-specific objects can be represented using `PGobject` for non-standard types such as `jsonb`. Use the official pgJDBC driver and integration tests because behavior is driver/database-specific. ([pgJDBC](https://jdbc.postgresql.org/documentation/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```java id="pgadv-015"
public final class JsonNodeJsonbTypeHandler
        extends BaseTypeHandler<JsonNode> {

    private static final ObjectMapper OBJECT_MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

    @Override
    public void setNonNullParameter(
            PreparedStatement ps,
            int i,
            JsonNode parameter,
            JdbcType jdbcType
    ) throws SQLException {
        PGobject jsonb = new PGobject();
        jsonb.setType("jsonb");
        jsonb.setValue(parameter.toString());
        ps.setObject(i, jsonb);
    }

    @Override
    public JsonNode getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            String columnName
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnName));
    }

    @Override
    public JsonNode getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    @Override
    public JsonNode getNullableResult(
            CallableStatement cs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(cs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    private JsonNode parse(String value) throws SQLException {
        if (value == null) {
            return null;
        }

        try {
            return OBJECT_MAPPER.readTree(value);
        } catch (JsonProcessingException exception) {
            throw new SQLException("Invalid jsonb value", exception);
        }
    }
}
```

MyBatis config:

```xml id="pgadv-016"
<typeHandlers>
    <typeHandler handler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.JsonNodeJsonbTypeHandler"/>
</typeHandlers>
```

ResultMap:

```xml id="pgadv-017"
<result property="metadata"
        column="metadata"
        typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.JsonNodeJsonbTypeHandler"/>
```

Parameter:

```xml id="pgadv-018"
#{metadata,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.JsonNodeJsonbTypeHandler}
```

---

# 8. JSONB TypeHandler with Typed Value Object

```java id="pgadv-019"
public record OrderMetadata(
        String sourceSystem,
        String externalReference,
        Map<String, String> attributes
) {}
```

```java id="pgadv-020"
public final class OrderMetadataJsonbTypeHandler
        extends BaseTypeHandler<OrderMetadata> {

    private static final ObjectMapper OBJECT_MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

    @Override
    public void setNonNullParameter(
            PreparedStatement ps,
            int i,
            OrderMetadata parameter,
            JdbcType jdbcType
    ) throws SQLException {
        try {
            PGobject jsonb = new PGobject();
            jsonb.setType("jsonb");
            jsonb.setValue(OBJECT_MAPPER.writeValueAsString(parameter));
            ps.setObject(i, jsonb);
        } catch (JsonProcessingException exception) {
            throw new SQLException("Failed to serialize order metadata", exception);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public OrderMetadata getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            String columnName
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnName));
    }

    @Override
    public OrderMetadata getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    @Override
    public OrderMetadata getNullableResult(
            CallableStatement cs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(cs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    private OrderMetadata parse(String value) throws SQLException {
        if (value == null) {
            return null;
        }

        try {
            return OBJECT_MAPPER.readValue(value, OrderMetadata.class);
        } catch (JsonProcessingException exception) {
            throw new SQLException("Failed to deserialize order metadata", exception);
        }
    }
}
```

Use typed handler when JSONB is not truly arbitrary.

---

# 9. JSONB Query Patterns

PostgreSQL provides JSON and JSONB operators/functions; `jsonb` supports containment and existence operators such as `@>`, `?`, `?|`, `?&`, and path extraction operators. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-json.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 9.1 Containment query

```xml id="pgadv-021"
<select id="findByMetadataContains" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        status,
        metadata
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND metadata @> #{metadataFilter,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.JsonNodeJsonbTypeHandler}
    ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Filter JSON:

```json id="pgadv-022"
{
  "sourceSystem": "CRM"
}
```

## 9.2 Extract JSON text key

```xml id="pgadv-023"
<select id="findByExternalReference" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        status,
        metadata
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND metadata ->> 'externalReference' = #{externalReference}
</select>
```

## 9.3 Key existence

```xml id="pgadv-024"
<select id="findOrdersWithMetadataKey" resultMap="OrderRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_number,
        status,
        metadata
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND metadata ? #{key}
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Caution:

```text id="pgadv-025"
JSONB key names in SQL should be controlled.
Do not allow arbitrary user-provided JSON path to become raw SQL.
Values still use #{}.
```

---

# 10. JSONB Indexing

PostgreSQL documentation states GIN indexes can efficiently search keys or key/value pairs within many `jsonb` documents. The two common operator classes are default `jsonb_ops` and `jsonb_path_ops`; the latter supports fewer operators but can be smaller and faster for containment-heavy workloads. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-json.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 10.1 General GIN index

```sql id="pgadv-026"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_metadata_gin
ON orders
USING gin (metadata);
```

Good for general JSONB key/value search.

## 10.2 Path ops for containment-heavy query

```sql id="pgadv-027"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_metadata_path_ops
ON orders
USING gin (metadata jsonb_path_ops);
```

Good for:

```text id="pgadv-028"
metadata @> '{"sourceSystem": "CRM"}'
```

## 10.3 Expression index for common key

```sql id="pgadv-029"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_metadata_external_reference
ON orders ((metadata ->> 'externalReference'));
```

Query:

```sql id="pgadv-030"
WHERE metadata ->> 'externalReference' = ?
```

## 10.4 Partial expression index

```sql id="pgadv-031"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_crm_external_reference
ON orders ((metadata ->> 'externalReference'))
WHERE metadata ->> 'sourceSystem' = 'CRM';
```

Index checklist:

```text id="pgadv-032"
[ ] Which JSONB operator does query use?
[ ] Does chosen GIN operator class support that operator?
[ ] Is expression index better for one hot key?
[ ] Is partial index useful for one source/type?
[ ] Does EXPLAIN prove index usage?
[ ] Is write overhead acceptable?
```

---

# 11. Array Types

PostgreSQL allows columns to be defined as arrays of built-in or user-defined base types, including enum and composite types. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/arrays.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.1 Table

```sql id="pgadv-033"
CREATE TABLE products (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    sku text NOT NULL,
    tags text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
```

Use arrays for:

```text id="pgadv-034"
[OK] Small tags.
[OK] Simple labels.
[OK] No per-item metadata.
[OK] No FK needed per item.
```

Prefer join table for:

```text id="pgadv-035"
[NO] Tags need owner/metadata.
[NO] Tags need FK/reference.
[NO] Frequent analytics on tag rows.
[NO] Large/unbounded list.
```

---

## 11.2 Array TypeHandler for `List<String>`

```java id="pgadv-036"
public final class StringListArrayTypeHandler
        extends BaseTypeHandler<List<String>> {

    @Override
    public void setNonNullParameter(
            PreparedStatement ps,
            int i,
            List<String> parameter,
            JdbcType jdbcType
    ) throws SQLException {
        Array array = ps.getConnection()
                .createArrayOf("text", parameter.toArray(String[]::new));
        ps.setArray(i, array);
    }

    @Override
    public List<String> getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            String columnName
    ) throws SQLException {
        return toList(rs.getArray(columnName));
    }

    @Override
    public List<String> getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return toList(rs.getArray(columnIndex));
    }

    @Override
    public List<String> getNullableResult(
            CallableStatement cs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return toList(cs.getArray(columnIndex));
    }

    private List<String> toList(Array array) throws SQLException {
        if (array == null) {
            return List.of();
        }

        String[] values = (String[]) array.getArray();
        return List.of(values);
    }
}
```

ResultMap:

```xml id="pgadv-037"
<result property="tags"
        column="tags"
        typeHandler="com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.StringListArrayTypeHandler"/>
```

Parameter:

```xml id="pgadv-038"
#{tags,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.StringListArrayTypeHandler}
```

---

# 12. Array Query Patterns

## 12.1 Contains array

```xml id="pgadv-039"
<select id="findProductsContainingTags" resultMap="ProductRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        sku,
        tags
    FROM products
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND tags @> #{tags,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.StringListArrayTypeHandler}
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

## 12.2 Overlap array

```xml id="pgadv-040"
<select id="findProductsOverlappingTags" resultMap="ProductRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        sku,
        tags
    FROM products
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND tags && #{tags,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.StringListArrayTypeHandler}
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

## 12.3 Any value

```xml id="pgadv-041"
<select id="findProductsByTag" resultMap="ProductRecordResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        sku,
        tags
    FROM products
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND #{tag} = ANY(tags)
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Index:

```sql id="pgadv-042"
CREATE INDEX idx_products_tags_gin
ON products
USING gin (tags);
```

# 13. Enum Types

## 13.1 Option A - text + check constraint

```sql id="pgadv-043"
CREATE TABLE orders (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    status text NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT orders_status_check
    CHECK (status IN ('DRAFT', 'SUBMITTED', 'APPROVED', 'CANCELLED'))
);
```

Pros:

```text id="pgadv-044"
[OK] Easier to add/remove values through constraint migration.
[OK] Simpler JDBC mapping as string.
[OK] Operationally flexible.
```

Cons:

```text id="pgadv-045"
[NO] Less type-specific than PostgreSQL enum.
```

## 13.2 Option B - PostgreSQL enum

```sql id="pgadv-046"
CREATE TYPE order_status AS ENUM (
    'DRAFT',
    'SUBMITTED',
    'APPROVED',
    'CANCELLED'
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    status order_status NOT NULL
);
```

Pros:

```text id="pgadv-047"
[OK] Strong DB type.
[OK] Clear allowed values at type level.
```

Cons:

```text id="pgadv-048"
[NO] Evolution/removal/rollback more complicated.
[NO] Java TypeHandler often needed.
```

PostgreSQL enum types are ordered lists of labels created with `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM`; enum labels are case-sensitive and have ordering based on creation order. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 13.3 Option C - lookup table

```sql id="pgadv-049"
CREATE TABLE order_status_lookup (
    code text PRIMARY KEY,
    display_name text NOT NULL,
    active boolean NOT NULL
);
```

Use when:

```text id="pgadv-050"
[OK] Status values have metadata.
[OK] Admin/config can manage values.
[OK] Need localization/display names.
[OK] Need lifecycle of code values.
```

---

# 14. Enum TypeHandler

```java id="pgadv-051"
public final class OrderStatusTypeHandler
        extends BaseTypeHandler<OrderStatus> {

    @Override
    public void setNonNullParameter(
            PreparedStatement ps,
            int i,
            OrderStatus parameter,
            JdbcType jdbcType
    ) throws SQLException {
        ps.setString(i, parameter.name());
    }

    @Override
    public OrderStatus getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            String columnName
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnName));
    }

    @Override
    public OrderStatus getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    @Override
    public OrderStatus getNullableResult(
            CallableStatement cs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(cs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    private OrderStatus parse(String value) throws SQLException {
        if (value == null) {
            return null;
        }

        try {
            return OrderStatus.valueOf(value);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException exception) {
            throw new SQLException("Unknown order status: " + value, exception);
        }
    }
}
```

For PostgreSQL enum, you may need explicit cast in SQL:

```xml id="pgadv-052"
UPDATE orders
SET status = #{status}::order_status
WHERE id = #{id}
```

or TypeHandler with `PGobject` type matching the enum.

Governance rule:

```text id="pgadv-053"
Adding DB enum/status value requires:
[ ] DB migration.
[ ] Java enum update.
[ ] TypeHandler test.
[ ] Domain transition review.
[ ] API DTO enum review.
[ ] OpenAPI update if exposed.
```

# 15. Range Types

PostgreSQL range types represent a range of values with lower/upper bounds. Built-in range types include `int4range`, `int8range`, `numrange`, `tsrange`, `tstzrange`, and `daterange`; PostgreSQL also has multirange types. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Use range types for:

```text id="pgadv-054"
[OK] Effective date period.
[OK] Booking/reservation windows.
[OK] Price validity period.
[OK] Subscription active period.
[OK] Non-overlap constraints.
```

---

## 15.1 Table with `tstzrange`

```sql id="pgadv-055"
CREATE TABLE price_rules (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    product_id uuid NOT NULL,
    price numeric NOT NULL,
    currency text NOT NULL,
    valid_period tstzrange NOT NULL
);
```

Example insert:

```sql id="pgadv-056"
INSERT INTO price_rules (
    id,
    tenant_id,
    product_id,
    price,
    currency,
    valid_period
) VALUES (
    gen_random_uuid(),
    :tenant_id,
    :product_id,
    100.00,
    'USD',
    tstzrange('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2026-02-01T00:00:00Z', '[)')
);
```

`[)` means:

```text id="pgadv-057"
inclusive lower bound
exclusive upper bound
```

This is often best for time intervals because adjacent ranges do not overlap.

---

## 15.2 Java Range Value Object

```java id="pgadv-058"
public record InstantRange(
        Instant startInclusive,
        Instant endExclusive
) {
    public InstantRange {
        Objects.requireNonNull(startInclusive);
        Objects.requireNonNull(endExclusive);

        if (!startInclusive.isBefore(endExclusive)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "startInclusive must be before endExclusive"
            );
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 15.3 Simple Range TypeHandler via text representation

```java id="pgadv-059"
public final class InstantRangeTstzRangeTypeHandler
        extends BaseTypeHandler<InstantRange> {

    private static final DateTimeFormatter FORMATTER =
            DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT;

    @Override
    public void setNonNullParameter(
            PreparedStatement ps,
            int i,
            InstantRange parameter,
            JdbcType jdbcType
    ) throws SQLException {
        PGobject range = new PGobject();
        range.setType("tstzrange");
        range.setValue(toPostgresRange(parameter));
        ps.setObject(i, range);
    }

    @Override
    public InstantRange getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            String columnName
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnName));
    }

    @Override
    public InstantRange getNullableResult(
            ResultSet rs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(rs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    @Override
    public InstantRange getNullableResult(
            CallableStatement cs,
            int columnIndex
    ) throws SQLException {
        return parse(cs.getString(columnIndex));
    }

    private String toPostgresRange(InstantRange range) {
        return "["
                + FORMATTER.format(range.startInclusive())
                + ","
                + FORMATTER.format(range.endExclusive())
                + ")";
    }

    private InstantRange parse(String value) throws SQLException {
        if (value == null) {
            return null;
        }

        // Production code should use a robust parser for quoted bounds,
        // infinity, empty ranges, spaces, and time zone variants.
        if (!value.startsWith("[") || !value.endsWith(")")) {
            throw new SQLException("Unsupported tstzrange format: " + value);
        }

        String body = value.substring(1, value.length() - 1);
        String[] parts = body.split(",", 2);

        if (parts.length != 2) {
            throw new SQLException("Invalid tstzrange value: " + value);
        }

        return new InstantRange(
                Instant.parse(parts[0].replace("\"", "")),
                Instant.parse(parts[1].replace("\"", ""))
        );
    }
}
```

Caution:

```text id="pgadv-060"
Range text parsing is tricky.
For production, test:
[ ] inclusive/exclusive bounds
[ ] empty range
[ ] unbounded range
[ ] quoted timestamp
[ ] timezone variants
```

---

# 16. Range Query Patterns

## 16.1 Contains timestamp

```xml id="pgadv-061"
<select id="findActivePriceRule" resultMap="PriceRuleResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        product_id,
        price,
        currency,
        valid_period
    FROM price_rules
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND product_id = #{productId}
      AND valid_period @> #{at}
    LIMIT 1
</select>
```

## 16.2 Overlaps period

```xml id="pgadv-062"
<select id="findOverlappingRules" resultMap="PriceRuleResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        tenant_id,
        product_id,
        price,
        currency,
        valid_period
    FROM price_rules
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND product_id = #{productId}
      AND valid_period && #{period,typeHandler=com.company.app.infrastructure.mybatis.typehandler.InstantRangeTstzRangeTypeHandler}
</select>
```

## 16.3 Prevent overlap with exclusion constraint

```sql id="pgadv-063"
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;

ALTER TABLE price_rules
ADD CONSTRAINT price_rules_no_overlap
EXCLUDE USING gist (
    tenant_id WITH =,
    product_id WITH =,
    valid_period WITH &&
);
```

PostgreSQL range types support indexing, and GiST/SP-GiST indexes can support range operations such as overlap/contains; exclusion constraints are commonly used to prevent overlapping ranges. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 17. Range Indexing

```sql id="pgadv-064"
CREATE INDEX idx_price_rules_valid_period_gist
ON price_rules
USING gist (valid_period);
```

Composite with equality fields may need extension/opclass strategy:

```sql id="pgadv-065"
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;

CREATE INDEX idx_price_rules_tenant_product_period_gist
ON price_rules
USING gist (
    tenant_id,
    product_id,
    valid_period
);
```

Checklist:

```text id="pgadv-066"
[ ] Query uses range operators supported by index.
[ ] EXPLAIN verifies GiST/SP-GiST usage.
[ ] Bound convention is standardized, e.g. [).
[ ] Non-overlap constraints tested.
[ ] Timezone handling is explicit.
```

# 18. UUID, Numeric, Temporal Quick Policy

## 18.1 UUID

Use PostgreSQL `uuid` and Java `UUID`.

```sql id="pgadv-067"
id uuid PRIMARY KEY
```

```java id="pgadv-068"
UUID id
```

## 18.2 Money / Decimal

Use PostgreSQL `numeric` and Java `BigDecimal`.

```sql id="pgadv-069"
total_amount numeric(18, 2) NOT NULL
```

```java id="pgadv-070"
BigDecimal totalAmount
```

## 18.3 Time

Use `timestamptz` for absolute event timestamps and Java `Instant`/`OffsetDateTime`.

```sql id="pgadv-071"
created_at timestamptz NOT NULL
```

```java id="pgadv-072"
Instant createdAt
```

These are not “advanced” but should be standardized with advanced type handling to avoid subtle drift.

# 19. Schema Governance for JSONB

JSONB governance checklist:

```text id="pgadv-073"
[ ] Column purpose documented.
[ ] JSON shape documented if not arbitrary.
[ ] Required keys validated in app or DB.
[ ] JSON schema version stored if shape evolves.
[ ] Max payload size enforced at API/service.
[ ] Hot keys promoted to typed columns if needed.
[ ] Indexes match actual query operators.
[ ] OpenAPI does not blindly expose internal JSONB.
```

## 19.1 Metadata schema version

```json id="pgadv-074"
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "sourceSystem": "CRM",
  "externalReference": "CRM-123",
  "attributes": {
    "campaign": "Q3"
  }
}
```

## 19.2 Promotion pattern

If JSONB key becomes core:

```text id="pgadv-075"
metadata.sourceSystem
  ↓
add source_system column
  ↓
backfill from metadata
  ↓
dual write
  ↓
switch query to typed column
  ↓
optionally keep/remove JSON key
```

Migration:

```sql id="pgadv-076"
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD COLUMN source_system text;

UPDATE orders
SET source_system = metadata ->> 'sourceSystem'
WHERE source_system IS NULL
  AND metadata ? 'sourceSystem';

CREATE INDEX idx_orders_source_system
ON orders (tenant_id, source_system);
```

---

# 20. API Boundary Policy

Do not expose DB advanced type directly unless it is intentionally part of public contract.

## 20.1 Bad response

```java id="pgadv-077"
public record OrderResponse(
        UUID id,
        JsonNode metadata
) {}
```

Maybe okay for admin/internal, but dangerous for public API.

## 20.2 Better public response

```java id="pgadv-078"
public record OrderResponse(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        String sourceSystem,
        String externalReference
) {}
```

Mapping:

```java id="pgadv-079"
public OrderResponse toResponse(OrderResult result) {
    OrderMetadata metadata = result.metadata();

    return new OrderResponse(
            result.id(),
            result.orderNumber(),
            metadata.sourceSystem(),
            metadata.externalReference()
    );
}
```

Rule:

```text id="pgadv-080"
PostgreSQL advanced type is persistence detail.
API exposes stable DTO fields.
```

# 21. Integration Test Matrix

| Type | Test |
|---|---|
| JSONB TypeHandler | Insert JsonNode → select → same JSON |
| JSONB typed object | Serialize/deserialize OrderMetadata |
| JSONB containment | `metadata @> ...` returns expected rows |
| JSONB expression key | `metadata ->> key` query works |
| JSONB index | EXPLAIN for critical query |
| Array TypeHandler | List<String> round-trip |
| Array overlap | `tags && ?` query works |
| Array contains | `tags @> ?` query works |
| Enum TypeHandler | Java enum ↔ DB value |
| Unknown enum | Fails safely / compatibility policy |
| Range TypeHandler | InstantRange round-trip |
| Range contains | `valid_period @> timestamp` |
| Range overlap | `valid_period && period` |
| Exclusion constraint | overlapping range rejected |
| SQLSTATE mapping | constraint errors mapped |
| Migration | JSONB key promotion/backfill tested |

# 22. Example JSONB Test

```java id="pgadv-081"
@Test
void shouldRoundTripJsonbMetadata() {
    UUID orderId = UUID.randomUUID();

    JsonNode metadata = objectMapper.createObjectNode()
            .put("sourceSystem", "CRM")
            .put("externalReference", "CRM-123");

    try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession(false)) {
        OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

        mapper.insertOrderMetadata(orderId, metadata);

        JsonNode loaded = mapper.findMetadata(orderId);

        assertEquals("CRM", loaded.get("sourceSystem").asText());
        assertEquals("CRM-123", loaded.get("externalReference").asText());

        session.rollback();
    }
}
```

# 24. Review Checklist

## 24.1 JSONB

```text id="pgadv-083"
[ ] JSONB use case justified.
[ ] Shape/version documented.
[ ] Required keys validated.
[ ] Hot query keys indexed or promoted.
[ ] JSONB TypeHandler tested.
[ ] API does not expose internal JSON blindly.
```

## 24.2 Array

```text id="pgadv-084"
[ ] Array is small/bounded.
[ ] No per-item FK/metadata needed.
[ ] TypeHandler tested.
[ ] GIN index considered for contains/overlap.
[ ] Empty/null array semantics clear.
```

## 24.3 Enum

```text id="pgadv-085"
[ ] Strategy chosen: text+check, PG enum, or lookup table.
[ ] Java enum updated.
[ ] API enum reviewed.
[ ] Unknown/future values handled intentionally.
[ ] Migration/rollback considered.
```

## 24.4 Range

```text id="pgadv-086"
[ ] Bound convention standardized, usually [).
[ ] Timezone clear.
[ ] TypeHandler parser tested.
[ ] GiST/SP-GiST index considered.
[ ] Exclusion constraint used for non-overlap if needed.
```

## 24.5 MyBatis

```text id="pgadv-087"
[ ] TypeHandler specified where needed.
[ ] resultMap explicit.
[ ] No raw user input in JSON path/SQL fragment.
[ ] Integration test uses PostgreSQL.
[ ] SQLSTATE translation covers constraints.
```

# 25. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Semua field masuk JSONB | Hilang constraint/index/clarity | Typed columns untuk core fields |
| Public API expose raw JSONB | API contract tidak stabil | Response DTO typed |
| Query JSONB hot key tanpa index | Slow query | Expression/GIN index |
| Array untuk data relasional kompleks | Constraint lemah | Join table |
| PostgreSQL enum untuk status sering berubah | Migration sulit | text + check / lookup |
| Range pakai start/end biasa tanpa constraint | Overlap bug | Range type + exclusion constraint |
| TypeHandler tanpa test | Runtime mapping failure | PostgreSQL integration test |
| Parse range text asal-asalan | Edge case bug | Robust parser + tests |
| `${jsonPath}` dari client | SQL injection | allow-list paths |
| JSONB jadi migration avoidance | Data quality turun | Schema governance |

# Seri 5/9 - Outbox Pattern with MyBatis + PostgreSQL  
## transactional outbox, event table design, idempotency, retry, polling worker, Kafka/RabbitMQ publishing, cleanup, observability, contract testing

## 1. Introduction

**Transactional outbox** adalah pattern untuk memastikan perubahan database dan event/message yang mewakili perubahan itu tidak saling inkonsisten.

Masalah klasik:

```text id="outbox-001"
Order berhasil disimpan ke PostgreSQL
  ↓
Aplikasi crash sebelum publish event ke Kafka/RabbitMQ
  ↓
Service lain tidak pernah tahu order dibuat
```

Atau sebaliknya:

```text id="outbox-002"
Event berhasil dipublish
  ↓
Database transaction rollback
  ↓
Consumer menerima event untuk data yang sebenarnya tidak pernah committed
```

Outbox menyelesaikan ini dengan menulis **business data** dan **event outbox row** dalam **satu transaksi database**. Setelah commit, worker terpisah membaca outbox dan publish ke broker. Debezium juga mendeskripsikan outbox pattern sebagai cara menghindari inkonsistensi antara state internal service di database dan event yang dikonsumsi service lain. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 2. Mental Model

```text id="outbox-003"
Application transaction:
  INSERT/UPDATE business table
  INSERT outbox_event
  COMMIT

After commit:
  Outbox worker polls outbox_event
  Publishes event to Kafka/RabbitMQ
  Marks event as published or schedules retry
```

Key rule:

```text id="outbox-004"
Never publish external message inside database transaction
unless you have a very explicit distributed transaction design.

Default microservice pattern:
  DB transaction writes outbox.
  Worker publishes after commit.
```

---

# 3. Diagram

```text id="outbox-005"
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Jersey Resource                            │
│                                                              │
│  POST /orders                                                 │
│  @Valid CreateOrderRequest                                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Application Service                        │
│                                                              │
│  transactionManager.inTransaction(...)                        │
│    ├─ orderRepository.save(order)                             │
│    └─ outboxRepository.save(OrderCreatedEvent)                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PostgreSQL Transaction                     │
│                                                              │
│  orders                                                       │
│  order_items                                                  │
│  outbox_events                                                │
│                                                              │
│  COMMIT atomically                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Outbox Worker                              │
│                                                              │
│  SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED                            │
│  publish to Kafka/RabbitMQ                                    │
│  mark PUBLISHED / retry                                       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Message Broker                             │
│                                                              │
│  Kafka topic / RabbitMQ exchange                              │
│  Consumers                                                    │
│  Idempotent processing                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

PostgreSQL `SKIP LOCKED` cocok untuk workflow seperti queue table karena row yang sedang locked oleh worker lain akan dilewati, sehingga beberapa worker bisa mengambil batch berbeda tanpa saling menunggu; dokumentasi PostgreSQL juga mengingatkan bahwa ini menghasilkan view yang tidak konsisten sehingga tidak cocok untuk general-purpose read biasa. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 4. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Tujuan | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transactional outbox | Write business data + event row in one DB transaction | Avoid DB/event inconsistency | Publish event langsung lalu DB rollback |
| Outbox table design | Store event envelope/payload/status | Durable event buffer | Payload tidak versioned |
| Event envelope | eventId, aggregateId, type, version, timestamp | Consumer contract | Consumer tidak bisa dedupe |
| Idempotency | eventId/idempotency key | Safe retry/duplicate handling | Consumer double-process |
| Polling worker | Claim pending rows | Async publish | Multiple worker publish same row |
| `SKIP LOCKED` | Concurrent row claiming | Parallel workers | Dipakai untuk read biasa |
| Retry policy | retry_count, next_attempt_at, error | Recover transient broker failure | Infinite tight retry loop |
| Dead letter | status `FAILED` / DLQ topic | Manual recovery | Poison event menghambat batch |
| Broker publish | Kafka/RabbitMQ | Deliver event | No confirm/ack semantics |
| Mark published | Update outbox status | Prevent repeated publish | Crash after publish before mark |
| Cleanup/archive | Retention policy | Keep table small | Delete too early |
| Observability | metrics/logs/traces | Debug pipeline | “event hilang” tanpa evidence |
| Contract testing | event schema fixtures | Stable consumers | Event shape berubah diam-diam |

---

# 5. Outbox Table Design

## 5.1 Recommended table

```sql id="outbox-006"
CREATE TABLE outbox_events (
    id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,

    aggregate_type text NOT NULL,
    aggregate_id uuid NOT NULL,

    event_type text NOT NULL,
    event_version integer NOT NULL,

    event_key text NOT NULL,
    payload jsonb NOT NULL,
    headers jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,

    status text NOT NULL,
    retry_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    max_retry_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,

    next_attempt_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    locked_by text,
    locked_at timestamptz,

    published_at timestamptz,
    last_error text,

    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

    CONSTRAINT outbox_events_status_check
    CHECK (status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'PUBLISHED', 'FAILED'))
);
```

## 5.2 Indexes

```sql id="outbox-007"
CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_pending_ready
ON outbox_events (
    status,
    next_attempt_at,
    created_at,
    id
)
WHERE status = 'PENDING';

CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_aggregate
ON outbox_events (
    aggregate_type,
    aggregate_id,
    created_at
);

CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_published_cleanup
ON outbox_events (
    published_at
)
WHERE status = 'PUBLISHED';
```

Design notes:

```text id="outbox-008"
id             → eventId, stable dedupe key
event_key      → broker partition/routing key
event_type     → consumer contract type
event_version  → schema evolution
payload        → event body
headers        → correlationId, causationId, trace context, content type
status         → worker lifecycle
next_attempt_at→ retry schedule
```

# 7. Write Business Data + Outbox in Same Transaction

## 7.1 Domain event

```java id="outbox-013"
public interface DomainEvent {
    UUID eventId();
    UUID aggregateId();
    String aggregateType();
    String eventType();
    int eventVersion();
    Instant occurredAt();
}
```

```java id="outbox-014"
public record OrderSubmittedEvent(
        UUID eventId,
        UUID tenantId,
        UUID aggregateId,
        String orderNumber,
        UUID customerId,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant occurredAt
) implements DomainEvent {

    @Override
    public String aggregateType() {
        return "Order";
    }

    @Override
    public String eventType() {
        return "OrderSubmitted";
    }

    @Override
    public int eventVersion() {
        return 1;
    }
}
```

## 7.2 Service transaction

```java id="outbox-015"
public final class OrderService {

    private final TransactionManager transactionManager;
    private final OrderRepositoryFactory orderRepositoryFactory;
    private final OutboxRepositoryFactory outboxRepositoryFactory;

    public OrderResult submit(SubmitOrderCommand command) {
        return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderRepository orderRepository =
                    orderRepositoryFactory.create(session);

            OutboxRepository outboxRepository =
                    outboxRepositoryFactory.create(session);

            Order order = orderRepository.findByIdForUpdate(
                    command.tenantId(),
                    command.orderId()
            ).orElseThrow(() -> DomainException.notFound("ORDER_NOT_FOUND"));

            order.submit(command.actorUserId());

            orderRepository.save(order);

            for (DomainEvent event : order.pullDomainEvents()) {
                outboxRepository.save(event, command.correlationId());
            }

            return OrderResult.from(order);
        });
    }
}
```

Critical rule:

```text id="outbox-016"
orderRepository.save(order)
outboxRepository.save(event)

Both inside same SqlSession / same DB transaction.
```

# 8. Outbox Repository with MyBatis

## 8.1 Repository interface

```java id="outbox-017"
public interface OutboxRepository {

    void save(DomainEvent event, String correlationId);

    List<OutboxEventRecord> claimPendingBatch(
            String workerId,
            int batchSize,
            Instant now
    );

    void markPublished(UUID eventId, Instant publishedAt);

    void markRetry(
            UUID eventId,
            int retryCount,
            Instant nextAttemptAt,
            String lastError
    );

    void markFailed(
            UUID eventId,
            int retryCount,
            String lastError
    );
}
```

## 8.2 Implementation

```java id="outbox-018"
public final class MyBatisOutboxRepository implements OutboxRepository {

    private final OutboxSqlMapper sqlMapper;
    private final OutboxEventMapper eventMapper;

    public MyBatisOutboxRepository(
            SqlSession session,
            OutboxEventMapper eventMapper
    ) {
        this.sqlMapper = session.getMapper(OutboxSqlMapper.class);
        this.eventMapper = eventMapper;
    }

    @Override
    public void save(DomainEvent event, String correlationId) {
        OutboxEventRecord record =
                eventMapper.toOutboxRecord(event, correlationId);

        sqlMapper.insert(record);
    }

    @Override
    public List<OutboxEventRecord> claimPendingBatch(
            String workerId,
            int batchSize,
            Instant now
    ) {
        return sqlMapper.claimPendingBatch(workerId, batchSize, now);
    }

    @Override
    public void markPublished(UUID eventId, Instant publishedAt) {
        sqlMapper.markPublished(eventId, publishedAt);
    }

    @Override
    public void markRetry(
            UUID eventId,
            int retryCount,
            Instant nextAttemptAt,
            String lastError
    ) {
        sqlMapper.markRetry(
                eventId,
                retryCount,
                nextAttemptAt,
                truncate(lastError)
        );
    }

    @Override
    public void markFailed(
            UUID eventId,
            int retryCount,
            String lastError
    ) {
        sqlMapper.markFailed(
                eventId,
                retryCount,
                truncate(lastError)
        );
    }

    private String truncate(String value) {
        if (value == null) {
            return null;
        }

        return value.length() <= 2000
                ? value
                : value.substring(0, 2000);
    }
}
```

# 11. Claim Pending Batch with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`

## 11.1 Atomic claim using CTE

```xml id="outbox-022"
<select id="claimPendingBatch"
        resultMap="OutboxEventResultMap">
    WITH candidates AS (
        SELECT id
        FROM outbox_events
        WHERE status = 'PENDING'
          AND next_attempt_at &lt;= #{now}
        ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC
        LIMIT #{batchSize}
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
    )
    UPDATE outbox_events e
    SET
        status = 'PROCESSING',
        locked_by = #{workerId},
        locked_at = #{now},
        updated_at = #{now}
    FROM candidates c
    WHERE e.id = c.id
    RETURNING
        e.id,
        e.tenant_id,
        e.aggregate_type,
        e.aggregate_id,
        e.event_type,
        e.event_version,
        e.event_key,
        e.payload,
        e.headers,
        e.status,
        e.retry_count,
        e.max_retry_count,
        e.next_attempt_at,
        e.locked_by,
        e.locked_at,
        e.published_at,
        e.last_error,
        e.created_at,
        e.updated_at
</select>
```

This is intentionally `<select>` because PostgreSQL `UPDATE ... RETURNING` returns rows. MyBatis documents that data-changing statements returning rows, such as PostgreSQL `RETURNING`, should be written as `<select>` so returned data can be mapped. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-update.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.2 Why this pattern

```text id="outbox-023"
[ ] Claim and mark PROCESSING atomically.
[ ] Multiple workers can run concurrently.
[ ] Locked rows are skipped.
[ ] Returned rows are exactly the claimed rows.
```

# 13. Outbox Worker Flow

```text id="outbox-027"
loop:
  claim batch in short DB transaction
  for each event:
      publish to broker
      if success:
          mark PUBLISHED
      if failure and retry_count < max:
          mark PENDING with next_attempt_at
      if failure and retry_count >= max:
          mark FAILED
  sleep/backoff if no events
```

Important transaction boundary:

```text id="outbox-028"
Claim batch transaction:
  short

Publish:
  outside DB transaction

Mark status:
  short transaction per event or small batch
```

Do not keep DB row locked while waiting for Kafka/RabbitMQ network calls.

---

# 14. Worker Java Skeleton

```java id="outbox-029"
public final class OutboxWorker implements Runnable {

    private final String workerId;
    private final TransactionManager transactionManager;
    private final OutboxRepositoryFactory repositoryFactory;
    private final EventPublisher eventPublisher;
    private final Clock clock;

    private final int batchSize = 50;

    @Override
    public void run() {
        while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) {
            List<OutboxEventRecord> events = claimBatch();

            if (events.isEmpty()) {
                sleepQuietly(Duration.ofSeconds(1));
                continue;
            }

            for (OutboxEventRecord event : events) {
                publishOne(event);
            }
        }
    }

    private List<OutboxEventRecord> claimBatch() {
        return transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OutboxRepository repository =
                    repositoryFactory.create(session);

            return repository.claimPendingBatch(
                    workerId,
                    batchSize,
                    Instant.now(clock)
            );
        });
    }

    private void publishOne(OutboxEventRecord event) {
        try {
            eventPublisher.publish(event);

            transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
                OutboxRepository repository =
                        repositoryFactory.create(session);

                repository.markPublished(
                        event.id(),
                        Instant.now(clock)
                );

                return null;
            });

        } catch (Exception exception) {
            handlePublishFailure(event, exception);
        }
    }

    private void handlePublishFailure(
            OutboxEventRecord event,
            Exception exception
    ) {
        int nextRetryCount = event.retryCount() + 1;

        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OutboxRepository repository =
                    repositoryFactory.create(session);

            if (nextRetryCount >= event.maxRetryCount()) {
                repository.markFailed(
                        event.id(),
                        nextRetryCount,
                        exception.getMessage()
                );
            } else {
                repository.markRetry(
                        event.id(),
                        nextRetryCount,
                        calculateNextAttempt(nextRetryCount),
                        exception.getMessage()
                );
            }

            return null;
        });
    }

    private Instant calculateNextAttempt(int retryCount) {
        long delaySeconds = Math.min(300, retryCount * retryCount * 5L);
        return Instant.now(clock).plusSeconds(delaySeconds);
    }

    private void sleepQuietly(Duration duration) {
        try {
            Thread.sleep(duration.toMillis());
        } catch (InterruptedException exception) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
    }
}
```

# 15. Publishing to Kafka

## 15.1 Publisher interface

```java id="outbox-030"
public interface EventPublisher {

    void publish(OutboxEventRecord event) throws Exception;
}
```

## 15.2 Kafka publisher concept

```java id="outbox-031"
public final class KafkaOutboxPublisher implements EventPublisher {

    private final KafkaProducer<String, String> producer;
    private final ObjectMapper objectMapper;
    private final String topic;

    @Override
    public void publish(OutboxEventRecord event) throws Exception {
        ProducerRecord<String, String> record =
                new ProducerRecord<>(
                        topic,
                        event.eventKey(),
                        objectMapper.writeValueAsString(event.payload())
                );

        record.headers().add("eventId", event.id().toString().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        record.headers().add("eventType", event.eventType().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        record.headers().add("eventVersion", String.valueOf(event.eventVersion()).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        record.headers().add("correlationId", extractHeader(event, "correlationId"));

        producer.send(record).get();
    }

    private byte[] extractHeader(OutboxEventRecord event, String name) {
        JsonNode value = event.headers().get(name);
        return value == null
                ? new byte[0]
                : value.asText().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }
}
```

Kafka’s producer config documentation states that idempotence is enabled by default unless conflicting configs are set; still, the outbox pattern should assume downstream consumers may see duplicates because the worker can crash after publish but before marking the row as `PUBLISHED`. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/41/configuration/producer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Kafka producer guidance:

```text id="outbox-032"
[ ] Use eventId as header.
[ ] Use aggregateId/orderId or tenant+aggregate as key for ordering.
[ ] Enable/keep idempotent producer configuration.
[ ] Use acks=all where durability matters.
[ ] Define retry/delivery timeout carefully.
[ ] Consumers must be idempotent.
```

---

# 16. Publishing to RabbitMQ

RabbitMQ publisher confirms are designed for reliable publishing; when confirms are enabled, the broker asynchronously confirms that it has taken care of published messages. ([RabbitMQ](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/confirms?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Conceptual publisher:

```java id="outbox-033"
public final class RabbitMqOutboxPublisher implements EventPublisher {

    private final Channel channel;
    private final String exchange;
    private final ObjectMapper objectMapper;

    @Override
    public void publish(OutboxEventRecord event) throws Exception {
        AMQP.BasicProperties properties =
                new AMQP.BasicProperties.Builder()
                        .messageId(event.id().toString())
                        .type(event.eventType())
                        .contentType("application/json")
                        .headers(Map.of(
                                "eventVersion", event.eventVersion(),
                                "correlationId", headerText(event, "correlationId")
                        ))
                        .deliveryMode(2)
                        .build();

        channel.basicPublish(
                exchange,
                event.eventKey(),
                true,
                properties,
                objectMapper.writeValueAsBytes(event.payload())
        );

        channel.waitForConfirmsOrDie(5_000);
    }

    private String headerText(OutboxEventRecord event, String name) {
        JsonNode value = event.headers().get(name);
        return value == null ? "" : value.asText();
    }
}
```

RabbitMQ guidance:

```text id="outbox-034"
[ ] Use persistent messages where durability matters.
[ ] Use durable exchange/queue.
[ ] Enable publisher confirms.
[ ] Use messageId = eventId.
[ ] Consumers must dedupe by messageId/eventId.
```

---

# 17. Crash Window and Duplicate Reality

Important failure scenario:

```text id="outbox-035"
Worker publishes event successfully
  ↓
Worker crashes before markPublished
  ↓
Event remains PROCESSING or gets reset to PENDING
  ↓
Worker publishes same event again
```

Therefore:

```text id="outbox-036"
Outbox gives at-least-once delivery by default.
Consumers must be idempotent.
```

Exactly-once end-to-end is not achieved just by an outbox table. Kafka has idempotent and transactional producer features, but outbox-to-broker-to-consumer systems still need explicit duplicate handling across service boundaries. KafkaProducer documentation describes idempotent and transactional producer modes, but these do not remove the need to design idempotent consumers when using a database outbox worker. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/23/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/KafkaProducer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 18. Consumer Idempotency Pattern

## 18.1 Processed event table

```sql id="outbox-037"
CREATE TABLE processed_events (
    consumer_name text NOT NULL,
    event_id uuid NOT NULL,
    processed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (consumer_name, event_id)
);
```

## 18.2 Consumer transaction

```text id="outbox-038"
Consumer receives event
  ↓
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO processed_events(consumer_name, event_id)
  If duplicate key:
      already processed → ack and skip
  Apply business effect
COMMIT
  ↓
ack broker message
```

Consumer pseudo-code:

```java id="outbox-039"
public void handle(OrderSubmittedEvent event) {
    transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        ProcessedEventRepository processed =
                processedEventRepositoryFactory.create(session);

        if (!processed.tryMarkProcessing("billing-service", event.eventId())) {
            return null;
        }

        billingRepository.createInvoiceFromOrder(event);

        return null;
    });
}
```

Database uniqueness is the dedupe guard.

# 19. Reset Stuck PROCESSING Events

Worker can crash after claiming rows. Add recovery.

## 19.1 Reset query

```xml id="outbox-040"
<update id="resetStuckProcessingEvents">
    UPDATE outbox_events
    SET
        status = 'PENDING',
        locked_by = NULL,
        locked_at = NULL,
        next_attempt_at = now(),
        updated_at = now(),
        last_error = 'Reset stuck PROCESSING event'
    WHERE status = 'PROCESSING'
      AND locked_at &lt; now() - interval '5 minutes'
</update>
```

Checklist:

```text id="outbox-041"
[ ] processing timeout > expected publish duration.
[ ] reset job logs count.
[ ] reset job metric exists.
[ ] event remains idempotent because duplicate publish can happen.
```

---

# 20. Retry Policy

## 20.1 Backoff

```text id="outbox-042"
retry 1 → 5s
retry 2 → 20s
retry 3 → 45s
retry 4 → 80s
retry 5 → 125s
cap    → 5m / 15m / custom
```

Add jitter to avoid thundering herd.

## 20.2 Retryable vs non-retryable

| Failure | Retry? |
|---|---:|
| Broker temporarily unavailable | Yes |
| Publish timeout | Yes |
| Network interruption | Yes |
| Serialization bug | Usually no, mark failed |
| Unknown event type mapping bug | No until deploy fix |
| Payload too large | No or manual remediation |
| Auth/permission error to broker | Usually no until config fixed |

## 20.3 Retry fields

```text id="outbox-043"
retry_count
max_retry_count
next_attempt_at
last_error
status
```

---

# 21. Dead Letter / Failed Events

When max retry exhausted:

```text id="outbox-044"
status = FAILED
last_error = truncated diagnostic
```

Operational options:

```text id="outbox-045"
[ ] Manual replay after fix.
[ ] Move to broker DLQ if publish partially succeeds.
[ ] Admin endpoint/tool to requeue failed event.
[ ] Alert when FAILED count > 0.
```

Requeue SQL:

```sql id="outbox-046"
UPDATE outbox_events
SET
    status = 'PENDING',
    retry_count = 0,
    next_attempt_at = now(),
    last_error = NULL,
    updated_at = now()
WHERE id = :event_id
  AND status = 'FAILED';
```

---

# 22. Cleanup / Archive

Outbox table can grow fast.

## 22.1 Delete published events after retention

```sql id="outbox-047"
DELETE FROM outbox_events
WHERE status = 'PUBLISHED'
  AND published_at < now() - interval '14 days';
```

For high-volume table, batch:

```sql id="outbox-048"
WITH batch AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM outbox_events
    WHERE status = 'PUBLISHED'
      AND published_at < now() - interval '14 days'
    ORDER BY published_at ASC
    LIMIT 1000
)
DELETE FROM outbox_events e
USING batch b
WHERE e.id = b.id;
```

PostgreSQL’s `UPDATE` docs mention batching with ordered subqueries and notes that `SKIP LOCKED` can prevent multiple commands from updating the same row when lock contention is a concern. The same operational mindset applies to cleanup jobs: batch work, avoid long locks, and test with real data volume. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-update.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 22.2 Archive before delete

```text id="outbox-049"
PUBLISHED old events
  ↓
copy to outbox_events_archive
  ↓
delete from hot outbox_events
```

Checklist:

```text id="outbox-050"
[ ] Retention policy defined.
[ ] Compliance/audit needs reviewed.
[ ] Cleanup batched.
[ ] Index supports cleanup query.
[ ] FAILED events not deleted automatically.
```

---

# 23. CDC Alternative: Debezium Outbox Event Router

Instead of polling worker, another production-grade option is:

```text id="outbox-051"
Application writes outbox_events
  ↓
Debezium PostgreSQL connector reads WAL changes
  ↓
Outbox Event Router transforms rows into Kafka messages
```

Debezium’s Outbox Event Router is specifically designed to capture changes in an outbox table and route them as event messages, reducing the need to build your own polling publisher. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Decision table:

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Polling worker | Simple, app-controlled, broker-agnostic | Need build retry/claim/publish logic |
| Debezium CDC | Low app polling overhead, WAL-based, strong Kafka fit | Infra complexity, Kafka/Connect operations |
| Direct publish in transaction | Simple code | Unsafe without distributed transaction |
| Broker transaction only | Helps broker side | Still not atomic with DB commit |

---

# 24. Event Ordering

Ordering is subtle.

## 24.1 Per aggregate ordering

If events for same aggregate must be ordered:

```text id="outbox-052"
event_key = aggregate_id
```

Kafka uses key-based partitioning; same key usually goes to same partition, preserving order within that partition. For RabbitMQ, routing/queue design must preserve the ordering expectation.

## 24.2 Outbox ordering query

```sql id="outbox-053"
ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC
```

But with multiple workers and `SKIP LOCKED`:

```text id="outbox-054"
Global strict ordering is not guaranteed.
Per-aggregate ordering requires extra design.
```

Options:

```text id="outbox-055"
[ ] Partition workers by aggregate hash.
[ ] Use event_key consistently.
[ ] Avoid parallel publishing for same aggregate.
[ ] Consumer handles version/order checks.
[ ] Store aggregate_version in event.
```

Add field:

```sql id="outbox-056"
ALTER TABLE outbox_events
ADD COLUMN aggregate_version bigint;
```

Consumer can ignore stale/out-of-order event if aggregate version already processed.

# 27. Example Integration Test: Commit/Rollback

```java id="outbox-065"
@Test
void shouldCommitBusinessDataAndOutboxTogether() {
    UUID orderId = UUID.randomUUID();

    transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderRepository orderRepository =
                orderRepositoryFactory.create(session);
        OutboxRepository outboxRepository =
                outboxRepositoryFactory.create(session);

        Order order = OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder(orderId);
        orderRepository.save(order);

        outboxRepository.save(
                new OrderSubmittedEvent(
                        UUID.randomUUID(),
                        order.tenantId().value(),
                        order.id(),
                        order.orderNumber(),
                        order.customerId(),
                        order.total().amount(),
                        order.total().currency(),
                        Instant.now()
                ),
                "req-test"
        );

        return null;
    });

    assertTrue(orderExists(orderId));
    assertEquals(1, countOutboxEventsForAggregate(orderId));
}
```

```java id="outbox-066"
@Test
void shouldRollbackBusinessDataAndOutboxTogether() {
    UUID orderId = UUID.randomUUID();

    assertThrows(RuntimeException.class, () -> {
        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderRepository orderRepository =
                    orderRepositoryFactory.create(session);
            OutboxRepository outboxRepository =
                    outboxRepositoryFactory.create(session);

            Order order = OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder(orderId);
            orderRepository.save(order);

            outboxRepository.save(
                    OrderTestEvents.submitted(order),
                    "req-test"
            );

            throw new RuntimeException("simulate failure");
        });
    });

    assertFalse(orderExists(orderId));
    assertEquals(0, countOutboxEventsForAggregate(orderId));
}
```

# 28. Example Integration Test: Concurrent Claim

```java id="outbox-067"
@Test
void twoWorkersShouldNotClaimSameEvent() throws Exception {
    insertPendingOutboxEvents(100);

    ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2);

    Future<List<UUID>> workerA = executor.submit(() -> claimIds("worker-a", 50));
    Future<List<UUID>> workerB = executor.submit(() -> claimIds("worker-b", 50));

    Set<UUID> a = new HashSet<>(workerA.get());
    Set<UUID> b = new HashSet<>(workerB.get());

    Set<UUID> intersection = new HashSet<>(a);
    intersection.retainAll(b);

    assertTrue(intersection.isEmpty());
}
```

# 29. Schema Evolution

Event payload is a contract.

## 29.1 Compatible changes

```text id="outbox-068"
[OK] Add optional field.
[OK] Add new event type.
[OK] Add optional header.
[OK] Add nullable metadata.
```

## 29.2 Breaking changes

```text id="outbox-069"
[BREAKING] Remove field.
[BREAKING] Rename field.
[BREAKING] Change field type.
[BREAKING] Change enum meaning.
[BREAKING] Change event key semantics.
[BREAKING] Change required header.
```

## 29.3 Versioning

```text id="outbox-070"
OrderSubmitted.v1
OrderSubmitted.v2
```

Outbox fields:

```text id="outbox-071"
event_type = OrderSubmitted
event_version = 1
headers.schema = OrderSubmitted.v1
```

---

# 30. API / Domain Boundary

Do not create outbox event directly from API DTO.

Bad:

```java id="outbox-072"
outboxRepository.saveFromRequest(createOrderRequest);
```

Better:

```text id="outbox-073"
Request DTO
  → Command
  → Domain aggregate changes
  → Domain event
  → Outbox event mapper
```

Reason:

```text id="outbox-074"
API request is user intent.
Domain event is committed business fact.
```

Example:

```text id="outbox-075"
CreateOrderRequest
  ≠ OrderCreatedEvent

Request may fail validation/domain rule.
Event should exist only after domain state changes.
```

---

# 31. Security Considerations

```text id="outbox-076"
[ ] Do not put secrets/tokens in payload.
[ ] Minimize PII in events.
[ ] Use event-specific DTO, not full entity snapshot by default.
[ ] Apply tenant/security classification.
[ ] Consider encryption/tokenization for sensitive payloads.
[ ] Ensure broker ACLs restrict topic/exchange access.
[ ] Avoid logging full payload.
```

Payload design:

```text id="outbox-077"
Prefer:
  IDs, status, amount, public business fields

Avoid:
  full address, raw identity documents, payment data, tokens
```

# 32. Review Checklist

## 32.1 Transaction

```text id="outbox-078"
[ ] Business data and outbox row are written in same transaction.
[ ] No broker publish inside transaction.
[ ] Rollback removes both business and outbox changes.
[ ] Outbox repository uses same SqlSession.
```

## 32.2 Event design

```text id="outbox-079"
[ ] eventId exists.
[ ] eventType stable.
[ ] eventVersion explicit.
[ ] eventKey defined.
[ ] aggregateId present.
[ ] payload schema documented.
[ ] correlationId propagated.
```

## 32.3 Worker

```text id="outbox-080"
[ ] Claim query uses SKIP LOCKED or equivalent safe concurrency.
[ ] Publish is outside claim transaction.
[ ] Mark published/retry/failed robustly.
[ ] Stuck PROCESSING reset exists.
[ ] Retry has backoff and max count.
```

## 32.4 Broker

```text id="outbox-081"
[ ] Kafka producer durability/idempotence reviewed, or RabbitMQ publisher confirms used.
[ ] Consumer idempotency required.
[ ] messageId/eventId propagated.
[ ] Topic/exchange/routing key documented.
```

## 32.5 Ops

```text id="outbox-082"
[ ] Metrics exist for pending/failed/oldest age.
[ ] Alerts exist.
[ ] Cleanup/retention defined.
[ ] Manual requeue process exists.
```

# 33. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Publish event before DB commit | Event for rolled-back data | Write outbox in DB transaction |
| Publish event after DB commit in same request only | Crash loses event | Durable outbox row |
| Keep DB lock while publishing | Long locks/pool exhaustion | Claim short, publish outside |
| Mark published before broker ack | Event lost if publish failed | Mark after confirmed publish |
| No consumer idempotency | Duplicate side effects | processed_events table |
| No retry/backoff | Event stuck or retry storm | retry_count + next_attempt_at |
| Delete outbox immediately | Audit/debug impossible | retention policy |
| Full entity snapshot event | Sensitive data leak | event-specific payload |
| No schema version | Consumer breakage | event_version/schema header |
| No stuck reset | PROCESSING rows forever | reset job |

## 1. Introduction

Untuk stack **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis + PostgreSQL**, test yang hanya mock repository tidak cukup. Banyak bug production muncul di area yang hanya bisa terlihat saat SQL benar-benar dieksekusi:

```text id="mbtest-001"

resultMap drift
TypeHandler gagal
migration tidak cocok dengan mapper
SQLSTATE tidak diterjemahkan
rollback tidak terjadi
tenant filter lupa
locking/deadlock behavior salah
Jersey error contract berubah
```

Testcontainers berguna karena menyediakan dependency nyata yang ephemeral untuk integration test, termasuk database seperti PostgreSQL. Ini cocok untuk memastikan MyBatis XML, migration, TypeHandler, SQLSTATE, constraint, dan transaction behavior berjalan di PostgreSQL asli, bukan simulasi. ([Testcontainers](https://testcontainers.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 6. Testcontainers PostgreSQL Base Class

```java id="mbtest-006"
@Testcontainers
public abstract class PostgreSqlIntegrationTestBase {

    @Container
    protected static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES =
            new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16")
                    .withDatabaseName("app_test")
                    .withUsername("test")
                    .withPassword("test");

    protected static DataSource dataSource;
    protected static SqlSessionFactory sqlSessionFactory;
    protected static TransactionManager transactionManager;

    @BeforeAll
    static void beforeAll() {
        dataSource = buildDataSource(POSTGRES);
        runMigrations(dataSource);
        sqlSessionFactory = buildSqlSessionFactory(dataSource);

        transactionManager = new TransactionManager(
                new MyBatisSqlSessionFactory(sqlSessionFactory),
                new PersistenceExceptionTranslator()
        );
    }

    private static DataSource buildDataSource(
            PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres
    ) {
        HikariConfig config = new HikariConfig();
        config.setJdbcUrl(postgres.getJdbcUrl());
        config.setUsername(postgres.getUsername());
        config.setPassword(postgres.getPassword());
        config.setMaximumPoolSize(5);
        config.setConnectionTimeout(2_000);
        config.setPoolName("test-pool");

        return new HikariDataSource(config);
    }

    private static void runMigrations(DataSource dataSource) {
        Flyway.configure()
                .dataSource(dataSource)
                .locations("classpath:db/migration")
                .cleanDisabled(false)
                .load()
                .migrate();
    }

    private static SqlSessionFactory buildSqlSessionFactory(
            DataSource dataSource
    ) {
        try (InputStream inputStream =
                     Resources.getResourceAsStream("mybatis/mybatis-config.xml")) {

            XMLConfigBuilder parser = new XMLConfigBuilder(inputStream);
            Configuration configuration = parser.parse();

            Environment environment = new Environment(
                    "test",
                    new JdbcTransactionFactory(),
                    dataSource
            );

            configuration.setEnvironment(environment);

            return new SqlSessionFactoryBuilder().build(configuration);

        } catch (IOException exception) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Failed to build SqlSessionFactory",
                    exception
            );
        }
    }
}
```

MyBatis Java API menjelaskan bahwa `SqlSession` adalah interface utama untuk menjalankan command, memperoleh mapper, dan mengelola transaksi; `SqlSession` dibuat oleh `SqlSessionFactory`. Ini alasan integration test perlu membangun `SqlSessionFactory` realistis, bukan hanya mock mapper interface. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/java-api.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 7. Migration Test

## 7.1 Flyway migration from empty database

```java id="mbtest-007"
@Test
void shouldApplyAllFlywayMigrationsFromEmptyDatabase() {
    Flyway flyway = Flyway.configure()
            .dataSource(dataSource)
            .locations("classpath:db/migration")
            .cleanDisabled(false)
            .load();

    flyway.clean();
    MigrateResult result = flyway.migrate();

    assertTrue(result.migrationsExecuted >= 0);
}
```

Flyway `validate` membandingkan migration yang sudah diterapkan dengan migration yang tersedia dan gagal jika ada perbedaan seperti nama, type, atau checksum. Itu membuatnya berguna sebagai gate sebelum deploy atau sebelum test integration berjalan. ([Redgate Documentation](https://documentation.red-gate.com/fd/validate-277578898.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 7.2 Liquibase validate/update equivalent

```java id="mbtest-008"
@Test
void shouldValidateLiquibaseChangelog() throws Exception {
    try (Connection connection = dataSource.getConnection()) {
        Database database = DatabaseFactory.getInstance()
                .findCorrectDatabaseImplementation(
                        new JdbcConnection(connection)
                );

        Liquibase liquibase = new Liquibase(
                "db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yaml",
                new ClassLoaderResourceAccessor(),
                database
        );

        liquibase.validate();
    }
}
```

Liquibase `validate` mengecek changelog dan menemukan potensi error syntax/behavior Liquibase yang bisa membuat `update` gagal, tetapi dokumentasinya juga menegaskan bahwa validasi ini tidak menjamin SQL di dalam changelog pasti benar saat deployment; karena itu tetap perlu menjalankan update/migration ke PostgreSQL test database. ([docs.liquibase.com](https://docs.liquibase.com/secure/reference-guide-5-2/database-inspection-change-tracking-and-utility-commands/validate?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Tujuan: menangkap masalah namespace, statement id, type alias, type handler, resultMap, dan XML syntax sebelum runtime production.

# 9. resultMap Test

MyBatis documentation menyebut `resultMap` sebagai elemen paling penting dan kuat untuk memetakan `ResultSet` ke object. Karena itu, setiap query penting perlu test yang membuktikan column alias dan mapping benar. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```java id="mbtest-011"
class OrderResultMapIT extends PostgreSqlIntegrationTestBase {

    @Test
    void shouldMapOrderRecordFromResultMap() {
        UUID tenantId = UUID.randomUUID();
        UUID orderId = UUID.randomUUID();

        insertOrderFixture(
                tenantId,
                orderId,
                "ORD-001",
                "SUBMITTED",
                new BigDecimal("100.00"),
                "USD"
        );

        try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession()) {
            OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

            OrderRecord record = mapper.findByIdForTenant(
                    tenantId,
                    orderId
            );

            assertNotNull(record);
            assertEquals(orderId, record.id());
            assertEquals(tenantId, record.tenantId());
            assertEquals("ORD-001", record.orderNumber());
            assertEquals(OrderStatus.SUBMITTED, record.status());
            assertEquals(new BigDecimal("100.00"), record.totalAmount());
            assertEquals("USD", record.currency());
        }
    }
}
```

# 11. Repository Integration Test

## 11.1 Save and load aggregate

```java id="mbtest-016"
class OrderRepositoryIT extends PostgreSqlIntegrationTestBase {

    private final OrderPersistenceMapper persistenceMapper =
            new OrderPersistenceMapper();

    @Test
    void shouldSaveAndLoadOrderAggregate() {
        TenantId tenantId = TenantId.random();
        Order order = OrderTestFactory.draftOrder(tenantId);

        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderRepository repository = new MyBatisOrderRepository(
                    session,
                    persistenceMapper
            );

            repository.save(order);
            return null;
        });

        Order loaded = transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderRepository repository = new MyBatisOrderRepository(
                    session,
                    persistenceMapper
            );

            return repository.findById(tenantId, order.id())
                    .orElseThrow();
        });

        assertEquals(order.id(), loaded.id());
        assertEquals(order.tenantId(), loaded.tenantId());
        assertEquals(order.items().size(), loaded.items().size());
        assertEquals(order.total(), loaded.total());
    }
}
```
