# 13. SQLSTATE Error Translation Tests

PostgreSQL assigns five-character SQLSTATE codes to server messages, and official docs recommend testing error code rather than textual error message because codes are more stable and not affected by localization. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 13.1 Unique violation

```java id="mbtest-020"
@Test
void shouldTranslateUniqueViolationToDuplicateResource() {
    UUID tenantId = UUID.randomUUID();
    String orderNumber = "ORD-DUP-001";

    insertOrderFixture(tenantId, UUID.randomUUID(), orderNumber);

    RuntimeException exception = assertThrows(RuntimeException.class, () -> {
        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

            mapper.insertOrder(TestRecords.orderRecord(
                    tenantId,
                    UUID.randomUUID(),
                    orderNumber
            ));

            return null;
        });
    });

    PersistenceException translated =
            assertInstanceOf(PersistenceException.class, exception);

    assertEquals("DUPLICATE_RESOURCE", translated.code());
    assertEquals(PersistenceErrorCategory.CONFLICT, translated.category());
}
```

## 13.2 Foreign key violation

```java id="mbtest-021"
@Test
void shouldTranslateForeignKeyViolation() {
    UUID tenantId = UUID.randomUUID();
    UUID missingCustomerId = UUID.randomUUID();

    PersistenceException exception = assertThrows(
            PersistenceException.class,
            () -> transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
                OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

                mapper.insertOrder(TestRecords.orderRecordWithCustomer(
                        tenantId,
                        missingCustomerId
                ));

                return null;
            })
    );

    assertEquals("REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND", exception.code());
}
```

## 13.3 SQLSTATE mapping table

| SQLSTATE | Test scenario | Expected API/domain code |
|---|---|---|
| `23505` | duplicate unique key | `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE` |
| `23503` | missing FK | `REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| `23514` | check constraint fail | `CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` |
| `40001` | serialization failure | `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` / retry |
| `40P01` | deadlock | `DEADLOCK_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` / retry |
| `57014` | query timeout/cancel | `QUERY_TIMEOUT` |

# 15. Optimistic Locking Test

```java id="mbtest-025"
@Test
void shouldRejectStaleVersionUpdate() {
    TenantId tenantId = TenantId.random();
    Order order = OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder(tenantId);
    save(order);

    int firstUpdate = transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

        return mapper.updateStatusForTenant(
                tenantId.value(),
                order.id(),
                OrderStatus.APPROVED,
                order.version()
        );
    });

    int secondUpdate = transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
        OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

        return mapper.updateStatusForTenant(
                tenantId.value(),
                order.id(),
                OrderStatus.CANCELLED,
                order.version()
        );
    });

    assertEquals(1, firstUpdate);
    assertEquals(0, secondUpdate);
}
```

Repository should translate `0 rows updated` into:

```text id="mbtest-026"
VERSION_CONFLICT → HTTP 409
```

# 16. Pessimistic Lock / `NOWAIT` Test

PostgreSQL `FOR UPDATE` locks selected rows against concurrent updates; `NOWAIT` reports an error instead of waiting if row cannot be locked, while `SKIP LOCKED` skips rows that cannot be locked and is suitable for queue-like workloads rather than general-purpose reads. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```java id="mbtest-027"
@Test
void shouldFailFastWhenRowIsLockedWithNowait() throws Exception {
    TenantId tenantId = TenantId.random();
    Order order = OrderTestFactory.submittedOrder(tenantId);
    save(order);

    ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2);
    CountDownLatch rowLocked = new CountDownLatch(1);
    CountDownLatch releaseLock = new CountDownLatch(1);

    Future<?> locker = executor.submit(() -> {
        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

            mapper.findByIdForTenantForUpdate(
                    tenantId.value(),
                    order.id()
            );

            rowLocked.countDown();
            await(releaseLock);

            return null;
        });
    });

    rowLocked.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);

    assertThrows(PersistenceException.class, () -> {
        transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
            OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

            mapper.findByIdForTenantForUpdateNowait(
                    tenantId.value(),
                    order.id()
            );

            return null;
        });
    });

    releaseLock.countDown();
    locker.get(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
}
```

---

# 17. `SKIP LOCKED` Worker Claim Test

Useful for outbox/job queues.

```java id="mbtest-028"
@Test
void twoWorkersShouldNotClaimSameOutboxEvents() throws Exception {
    insertPendingOutboxEvents(100);

    ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2);

    Future<List<UUID>> workerA = executor.submit(() ->
            claimOutboxIds("worker-a", 50)
    );

    Future<List<UUID>> workerB = executor.submit(() ->
            claimOutboxIds("worker-b", 50)
    );

    Set<UUID> claimedByA = new HashSet<>(workerA.get());
    Set<UUID> claimedByB = new HashSet<>(workerB.get());

    Set<UUID> intersection = new HashSet<>(claimedByA);
    intersection.retainAll(claimedByB);

    assertTrue(intersection.isEmpty());
}
```

PostgreSQL docs explicitly mention `SKIP LOCKED` as useful to avoid lock contention with multiple consumers accessing a queue-like table, while warning it gives an inconsistent view and is not suitable for general-purpose work. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 21. Test Data Strategy

## 21.1 Deterministic fixtures

```java id="mbtest-037"
public final class TestIds {

    public static final UUID TENANT_A =
            UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1");

    public static final UUID TENANT_B =
            UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000b1");

    public static final Instant FIXED_NOW =
            Instant.parse("2026-07-13T10:15:30Z");

    private TestIds() {}
}
```

## 21.2 Avoid unstable data in golden tests

Avoid:

```text id="mbtest-038"
UUID.randomUUID()
Instant.now()
unordered list
database-generated order without ORDER BY
locale-dependent formatting
timezone-dependent output
```

Use:

```text id="mbtest-039"
fixed UUID
fixed Instant
ORDER BY deterministic
Clock injection
explicit Locale/ZoneOffset.UTC
```

# 22. Database Cleanup Strategy

Options:

| Strategy | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| One container per class | Isolated enough | Slower |
| One container per suite + cleanup | Faster | Cleanup discipline needed |
| Transaction rollback per test | Fast | Does not test commit behavior |
| Truncate tables before each test | Simple | Must respect FK order |
| Schema per test | Strong isolation | More setup |
| Fresh DB per test | Very isolated | Slowest |

Practical recommendation:

```text id="mbtest-040"
Use shared PostgreSQL container per test suite/class.
Run migration once.
Use deterministic cleanup/truncate for repository tests.
Use explicit commit tests where transaction behavior matters.
```

Example cleanup:

```java id="mbtest-041"
@BeforeEach
void cleanup() {
    JdbcTemplate jdbc = new JdbcTemplate(dataSource);

    jdbc.execute("""
            TRUNCATE TABLE
                outbox_events,
                order_items,
                orders,
                customers
            RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE
            """);
}
```

# 24. Test Matrix by Layer

| Layer | Tests |
|---|---|
| Domain | invariant, state transition, event creation |
| API mapper | request DTO → command, result → response |
| Persistence mapper | domain ↔ record |
| MyBatis config | config loads, mapper proxies available |
| Mapper XML | statement smoke tests |
| resultMap | fixture row → record |
| TypeHandler | enum/time/jsonb/array/range round-trip |
| Repository | save/load/update/search |
| Transaction | rollback, optimistic conflict |
| PostgreSQL constraints | unique/FK/check/exclusion |
| SQLSTATE | translation to stable code |
| Security | tenant isolation, SQL injection sort/filter |
| Outbox | atomic write, claim, retry, duplicate |
| Jersey | status code, error body, correlation ID |
| Contract | golden response, OpenAPI examples |

---

# 25. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Hanya mock mapper | SQL/XML tidak pernah dites | PostgreSQL integration test |
| Pakai H2 untuk PostgreSQL behavior | false confidence | Testcontainers PostgreSQL |
| Migration tidak dites dari nol | deploy gagal | migrate empty DB in CI |
| resultMap tidak dites | null/field mismatch runtime | fixture row → mapper select |
| No rollback test | partial commit unnoticed | forced exception rollback test |
| No SQLSTATE test | raw DB error leaks | constraint-triggered test |
| No tenant test | cross-tenant leak | tenant A/B tests |
| Concurrency tidak dites | lost update/deadlock | optimistic/lock tests |
| Golden file pakai random time | flaky | fixed Clock/UUID |
| JerseyTest tanpa ExceptionMapper | test tidak represent production | register full ResourceConfig |

# Seri 7/9 - MyBatis Observability & Troubleshooting  
## SQL logging aman, slow query, correlation ID, metrics, pg_stat_statements, pg_locks, HikariCP metrics, incident playbook, production debugging

## 1. Introduction

Di production, masalah MyBatis + PostgreSQL sering muncul sebagai gejala umum:

```text id="obs-001"
API lambat
DB timeout
connection pool penuh
deadlock
query tiba-tiba lambat
tenant data leak dicurigai
outbox menumpuk
event tidak terkirim
rollback tidak terjadi
error 500 tanpa konteks
```

Observability yang baik harus bisa menjawab:

```text id="obs-002"
Request mana yang bermasalah?
Mapper method apa yang lambat?
SQLSTATE apa yang terjadi?
Pool penuh atau query lambat?
DB menunggu lock atau I/O?
Query plan berubah atau index tidak kepakai?
Outbox tertahan di PENDING/PROCESSING/FAILED?
```

MyBatis menyediakan logging lewat internal log factory yang mendelegasikan ke implementasi seperti SLF4J, Commons Logging, Log4j2, atau JDK logging. Untuk production Java modern, arahkan MyBatis ke SLF4J lalu kontrol level/logger dari logging framework aplikasi. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/logging.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 2. Observability Diagram

```text id="obs-003"
HTTP Request
  │
  ├─ X-Correlation-Id
  ├─ tenantId
  ├─ actorUserId
  └─ endpoint template
       │
       ▼
Jersey Filter
  ├─ generate/validate correlationId
  ├─ put MDC
  └─ echo response header
       │
       ▼
Resource → Service → Repository
  ├─ log use-case result
  ├─ measure duration
  ├─ capture domain/API error code
  └─ propagate correlationId
       │
       ▼
MyBatis / PostgreSQL
  ├─ mapper method
  ├─ SQL duration
  ├─ rows affected/returned
  ├─ SQLSTATE
  ├─ transaction duration
  └─ pool acquisition duration
       │
       ▼
PostgreSQL Diagnostics
  ├─ pg_stat_activity
  ├─ pg_locks
  ├─ pg_stat_statements
  ├─ EXPLAIN ANALYZE
  └─ DB logs
```

# 3. Decomposition Map

| Area | Tujuan | Data penting | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correlation ID | Trace satu request | `correlationId`, `requestId` | Log tidak bisa dihubungkan |
| MDC logging | Inject context ke semua log | tenant, actor, endpoint | MDC tidak dibersihkan |
| Safe SQL logging | Debug query tanpa leak | mapper, duration, rows, SQLSTATE | PII/secret bocor |
| MyBatis logging | Observe SQL layer | logger name, statement | TRACE aktif di production |
| Repository metrics | Ukur method persistence | method, duration, status | Tidak tahu query mana lambat |
| HikariCP metrics | Pool health | active/idle/pending/acquire time | Pool exhaustion tidak terlihat |
| PostgreSQL activity | Active session/query | state, wait_event, query age | “DB lambat” tanpa bukti |
| Lock diagnostics | Blocking/blocker | `pg_locks`, `pg_stat_activity` | Deadlock/lock wait samar |
| pg_stat_statements | Top query aggregate | calls, total time, mean time | Query hot tidak diketahui |
| Query plan | Explain slow query | seq scan, index scan, buffers | Index tidak kepakai |
| SQLSTATE telemetry | Error classification | 23505, 40P01, 57014 | Semua jadi 500 |
| Outbox observability | Event pipeline health | pending, failed, oldest age | Event stuck diam-diam |
| Incident playbook | Debug cepat | symptom → checks | Trial-error saat outage |

PostgreSQL `pg_stat_statements` menyediakan statistik planning dan execution untuk semua SQL statement yang dijalankan server, sehingga sangat berguna untuk melihat query paling mahal berdasarkan total time, mean time, calls, dan rows. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgstatstatements.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 4. Correlation ID di Jersey/JAX-RS

## 4.1 Request filter

```java id="obs-004"
@Provider
@Priority(Priorities.AUTHENTICATION)
public final class CorrelationIdRequestFilter
        implements ContainerRequestFilter {

    public static final String HEADER = "X-Correlation-Id";
    public static final String PROPERTY = "correlationId";

    @Override
    public void filter(ContainerRequestContext requestContext) {
        String incoming = requestContext.getHeaderString(HEADER);

        String correlationId = isValid(incoming)
                ? incoming
                : UUID.randomUUID().toString();

        requestContext.setProperty(PROPERTY, correlationId);
        MDC.put(PROPERTY, correlationId);
    }

    private boolean isValid(String value) {
        return value != null
                && value.length() <= 100
                && value.matches("[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+");
    }
}
```

## 4.2 Response filter

```java id="obs-005"
@Provider
public final class CorrelationIdResponseFilter
        implements ContainerResponseFilter {

    @Override
    public void filter(
            ContainerRequestContext requestContext,
            ContainerResponseContext responseContext
    ) {
        Object correlationId =
                requestContext.getProperty(CorrelationIdRequestFilter.PROPERTY);

        if (correlationId != null) {
            responseContext.getHeaders().putSingle(
                    CorrelationIdRequestFilter.HEADER,
                    correlationId.toString()
            );
        }

        MDC.remove(CorrelationIdRequestFilter.PROPERTY);
    }
}
```

Checklist:

```text id="obs-006"
[ ] Accept incoming correlation ID only if valid.
[ ] Generate if missing/invalid.
[ ] Put into MDC.
[ ] Echo in response.
[ ] Remove MDC in response filter/finally.
[ ] Include in ApiErrorResponse.
```

# 6. Safe SQL Logging Policy

## 6.1 Jangan log ini

```text id="obs-010"
[NO] password
[NO] access token
[NO] refresh token
[NO] Authorization header
[NO] full KTP/passport/national ID
[NO] full card/payment data
[NO] full customer address
[NO] raw request body for sensitive endpoint
[NO] raw SQL parameters containing PII
[NO] full exception stack to client
```

## 6.2 Boleh log ini

```text id="obs-011"
[OK] mapper method
[OK] statement id
[OK] duration
[OK] row count
[OK] SQLSTATE
[OK] correlation ID
[OK] tenant hash
[OK] aggregate ID if not sensitive
[OK] API error code
```

## 6.3 Production default

```text id="obs-012"
Production:
  log mapper method + duration + SQLSTATE + row count.
  avoid raw SQL parameter logging.

Local/dev:
  SQL logging can be more verbose.
  still avoid secrets and tokens.
```

MyBatis can log statement details through configured logging implementation, but you should avoid enabling verbose SQL/parameter logs broadly in production because logs become a data exfiltration surface and can be very noisy. The official MyBatis logging page documents how logging delegates to implementations and can be configured via `logImpl`. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/logging.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 7. MyBatis Logging Configuration

## 7.1 mybatis-config.xml

```xml id="obs-013"
<configuration>
    <settings>
        <setting name="logImpl" value="SLF4J"/>
    </settings>
</configuration>
```

MyBatis supports `logImpl` values such as `SLF4J`, `LOG4J2`, `JDK_LOGGING`, `COMMONS_LOGGING`, `STDOUT_LOGGING`, and `NO_LOGGING`; `LOG4J` is deprecated. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/logging.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 7.2 Logback example

```xml id="obs-014"
<configuration>
    <appender name="JSON" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder"/>
    </appender>

    <logger name="com.company.app.infrastructure" level="INFO"/>
    <logger name="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderSqlMapper" level="WARN"/>

    <!-- Local only, avoid production TRACE unless debugging narrowly -->
    <logger name="org.apache.ibatis" level="WARN"/>

    <root level="INFO">
        <appender-ref ref="JSON"/>
    </root>
</configuration>
```

## 7.3 Targeted mapper logging

Untuk debugging sementara:

```xml id="obs-015"
<logger name="com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderSqlMapper" level="DEBUG"/>
```

Rule:

```text id="obs-016"
Enable detailed mapper logging:
  [OK] temporarily
  [OK] for one mapper
  [OK] in lower environment
  [OK] with redaction

Avoid:
  [NO] global TRACE in production
  [NO] long-lived parameter logging
```

# 8. Repository Timing Wrapper

Karena MyBatis raw logging bisa terlalu detail, sering lebih aman ukur di repository.

```java id="obs-017"
public final class ObservedOrderRepository implements OrderRepository {

    private final OrderRepository delegate;
    private final MeterRegistry meterRegistry;

    public ObservedOrderRepository(
            OrderRepository delegate,
            MeterRegistry meterRegistry
    ) {
        this.delegate = delegate;
        this.meterRegistry = meterRegistry;
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<Order> findById(TenantId tenantId, UUID orderId) {
        long started = System.nanoTime();

        try {
            return delegate.findById(tenantId, orderId);
        } finally {
            recordDuration("findById", started);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void save(Order order) {
        long started = System.nanoTime();

        try {
            delegate.save(order);
        } finally {
            recordDuration("save", started);
        }
    }

    private void recordDuration(String method, long startedNanos) {
        long durationNanos = System.nanoTime() - startedNanos;

        meterRegistry.timer(
                "repository.duration",
                "repository", "OrderRepository",
                "method", method
        ).record(durationNanos, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);

        long durationMs = TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toMillis(durationNanos);

        if (durationMs > 500) {
            log.warn(
                    "repository.slow repository={} method={} durationMs={} correlationId={}",
                    "OrderRepository",
                    method,
                    durationMs,
                    MDC.get("correlationId")
            );
        }
    }
}
```

Metric labels should be low-cardinality:

```text id="obs-018"
Good:
  repository=OrderRepository
  method=findById
  outcome=success/failure

Bad:
  orderId=...
  customerId=...
  rawSql=...
```

# 9. HikariCP Metrics

HikariCP exposes metrics integrations through its metrics packages and APIs; the current HikariCP Javadocs include packages such as `com.zaxxer.hikari.metrics`, `metrics.dropwizard`, and related metrics support. ([Javadoc](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.zaxxer/HikariCP/latest/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 9.1 Important pool metrics

```text id="obs-019"
hikaricp.connections.active
hikaricp.connections.idle
hikaricp.connections.pending
hikaricp.connections.max
hikaricp.connections.min
hikaricp.connections.acquire
hikaricp.connections.timeout
hikaricp.connections.creation
hikaricp.connections.usage
```

Exact metric names depend on your metrics integration, framework, and registry naming convention.

## 9.2 What they mean

| Metric | Meaning | Incident clue |
|---|---|---|
| active connections | currently checked out | high active + high latency |
| idle connections | available in pool | zero idle for long time can be pressure |
| pending threads | waiting for connection | pool exhaustion |
| acquire time | time to obtain connection | DB/pool contention |
| usage time | connection held duration | long transaction/query |
| timeout count | failed to get connection | API failures likely |
| max pool | configured cap | compare with DB capacity |

## 9.3 Hikari config hints

```java id="obs-020"
HikariConfig config = new HikariConfig();

config.setPoolName("order-service-pool");
config.setMaximumPoolSize(20);
config.setMinimumIdle(5);
config.setConnectionTimeout(2_000);
config.setValidationTimeout(1_000);
config.setMaxLifetime(1_800_000);
config.setLeakDetectionThreshold(10_000);
```

`leakDetectionThreshold` is useful as a temporary diagnostic guard, but do not treat it as a replacement for proper session/transaction closure.

# 10. PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity

`pg_stat_activity` is part of PostgreSQL’s cumulative statistics system and shows one row per server process with current activity, state, wait event, query, and timing information. The PostgreSQL monitoring stats documentation covers these views and their role in observing server activity. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 10.1 Active long-running queries

```sql id="obs-021"
SELECT
    pid,
    usename,
    application_name,
    state,
    wait_event_type,
    wait_event,
    now() - query_start AS query_age,
    now() - xact_start AS transaction_age,
    left(query, 1000) AS query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state <> 'idle'
ORDER BY query_age DESC;
```

## 10.2 Idle in transaction

```sql id="obs-022"
SELECT
    pid,
    usename,
    application_name,
    state,
    now() - xact_start AS transaction_age,
    now() - state_change AS idle_age,
    left(query, 1000) AS last_query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'idle in transaction'
ORDER BY transaction_age DESC;
```

Interpretation:

```text id="obs-023"
idle in transaction:
  connection is open
  transaction still active
  locks may be held
  vacuum cleanup can be affected
  app likely forgot commit/rollback/close or is doing long work inside transaction
```

---

# 11. PostgreSQL pg_locks

`pg_locks` provides a global view of locks in the database cluster, not just locks in the current database. It can be joined with `pg_stat_activity` to identify blocking and waiting sessions. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/view-pg-locks.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.1 Lock wait query

```sql id="obs-024"
SELECT
    blocked.pid AS blocked_pid,
    blocked_activity.usename AS blocked_user,
    blocked_activity.application_name AS blocked_app,
    now() - blocked_activity.query_start AS blocked_duration,
    left(blocked_activity.query, 500) AS blocked_query,

    blocking.pid AS blocking_pid,
    blocking_activity.usename AS blocking_user,
    blocking_activity.application_name AS blocking_app,
    now() - blocking_activity.query_start AS blocking_duration,
    left(blocking_activity.query, 500) AS blocking_query
FROM pg_locks blocked
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocked_activity
    ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked.pid
JOIN pg_locks blocking
    ON blocking.locktype = blocked.locktype
   AND blocking.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.database
   AND blocking.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.relation
   AND blocking.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.page
   AND blocking.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.tuple
   AND blocking.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.virtualxid
   AND blocking.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.transactionid
   AND blocking.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.classid
   AND blocking.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.objid
   AND blocking.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.objsubid
   AND blocking.pid <> blocked.pid
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocking_activity
    ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking.pid
WHERE NOT blocked.granted
  AND blocking.granted
ORDER BY blocked_duration DESC;
```

## 11.2 Simple lock summary

```sql id="obs-025"
SELECT
    locktype,
    mode,
    granted,
    count(*) AS count
FROM pg_locks
GROUP BY locktype, mode, granted
ORDER BY count DESC;
```

Use cases:

```text id="obs-026"
[ ] Identify blocker.
[ ] Detect idle transaction holding lock.
[ ] See lock mode.
[ ] Correlate lock wait with application request.
```

# 12. pg_stat_statements

## 12.1 Top total time queries

```sql id="obs-027"
SELECT
    calls,
    total_exec_time,
    mean_exec_time,
    max_exec_time,
    rows,
    left(query, 1000) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

## 12.2 Top mean time queries

```sql id="obs-028"
SELECT
    calls,
    mean_exec_time,
    max_exec_time,
    rows,
    left(query, 1000) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE calls > 10
ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

## 12.3 High call count queries

```sql id="obs-029"
SELECT
    calls,
    mean_exec_time,
    total_exec_time,
    rows,
    left(query, 1000) AS query
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY calls DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

`pg_stat_statements` is an extension, so it must be installed and configured by a database administrator or platform team; it tracks normalized statements and aggregates execution statistics. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgstatstatements.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 13. EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE Workflow

When a query is slow:

```text id="obs-030"
1. Identify mapper method.
2. Capture normalized SQL.
3. Reproduce with representative parameters.
4. Run EXPLAIN.
5. Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) in safe environment.
6. Compare estimated vs actual rows.
7. Check index usage.
8. Review query shape/index/statistics.
```

Example:

```sql id="obs-031"
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    status,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'
  AND status = 'SUBMITTED'
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Use caution: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes the query. For write statements, run inside transaction and rollback in a safe environment.

# 14. SQLSTATE Metrics

PostgreSQL error codes are stable SQLSTATE values; application code should classify errors using SQLSTATE rather than parsing message text. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgstatstatements.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Track:

```text id="obs-032"
db.errors.total{sqlstate="23505",code="DUPLICATE_RESOURCE"}
db.errors.total{sqlstate="23503",code="REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND"}
db.errors.total{sqlstate="40P01",code="DEADLOCK_DETECTED"}
db.errors.total{sqlstate="40001",code="SERIALIZATION_FAILURE"}
db.errors.total{sqlstate="57014",code="QUERY_TIMEOUT"}
```

Translator logging:

```java id="obs-033"
private PersistenceException translateSqlException(
        SQLException sqlException,
        RuntimeException original
) {
    String sqlState = sqlException.getSQLState();

    log.warn(
            "db.error sqlState={} correlationId={} message={}",
            sqlState,
            MDC.get("correlationId"),
            safeMessage(sqlException)
    );

    meterRegistry.counter(
            "db.errors",
            "sqlstate", sqlState == null ? "unknown" : sqlState
    ).increment();

    return switch (sqlState) {
        case "23505" -> duplicate(original);
        case "23503" -> referenceNotFound(original);
        case "40P01" -> deadlock(original);
        case "40001" -> serializationFailure(original);
        case "57014" -> queryTimeout(original);
        default -> unknown(original);
    };
}
```

# 15. Outbox Observability

Outbox-specific metrics:

```text id="obs-034"
outbox.events.pending.count
outbox.events.processing.count
outbox.events.published.count
outbox.events.failed.count
outbox.oldest.pending.age.seconds
outbox.publish.duration
outbox.publish.failures
outbox.retry.count
outbox.stuck.processing.count
outbox.claim.batch.size
```

Queries:

```sql id="obs-035"
SELECT
    status,
    count(*) AS count
FROM outbox_events
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY status;
```

```sql id="obs-036"
SELECT
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - min(created_at)) AS oldest_pending_age_seconds
FROM outbox_events
WHERE status = 'PENDING';
```

```sql id="obs-037"
SELECT
    id,
    event_type,
    retry_count,
    next_attempt_at,
    left(last_error, 500) AS last_error
FROM outbox_events
WHERE status = 'FAILED'
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Alert conditions:

```text id="obs-038"
[ ] FAILED count > 0.
[ ] Oldest pending age > SLA.
[ ] Pending count increasing for N minutes.
[ ] PROCESSING older than worker timeout.
[ ] Publish failure rate high.
```

# 16. Dashboard Layout

A practical dashboard for MyBatis + PostgreSQL:

```text id="obs-039"
API Health
  - request rate
  - p95/p99 latency
  - 4xx/5xx rate
  - error codes

Persistence Health
  - repository duration p95/p99
  - slow repository methods
  - DB error count by SQLSTATE
  - transaction duration

Connection Pool
  - active/idle/pending connections
  - acquire duration
  - timeout count
  - usage duration

PostgreSQL
  - active sessions
  - idle in transaction
  - lock waits
  - top pg_stat_statements
  - deadlocks/timeouts

Outbox
  - pending/failed count
  - oldest pending age
  - publish success/failure
  - retry rate
```

# 17. Troubleshooting Playbook: API Latency High

## Symptom

```text id="obs-040"
p95/p99 API latency naik
```

## Check sequence

```text id="obs-041"
1. Which endpoint?
2. Which correlation IDs?
3. Is time spent before DB or in repository?
4. Is Hikari pending > 0?
5. Are active connections maxed?
6. Any slow mapper/repository logs?
7. pg_stat_activity: long active queries?
8. pg_stat_activity: wait_event lock or IO?
9. pg_stat_statements: top query changed?
10. EXPLAIN slow query.
```

SQL:

```sql id="obs-042"
SELECT
    pid,
    application_name,
    state,
    wait_event_type,
    wait_event,
    now() - query_start AS age,
    left(query, 1000) AS query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state <> 'idle'
ORDER BY age DESC;
```

Likely causes:

```text id="obs-043"
[ ] Query plan regression.
[ ] Missing index.
[ ] Connection pool exhaustion.
[ ] Lock wait.
[ ] DB CPU/IO saturation.
[ ] External call inside transaction.
[ ] Large response serialization.
```

---

# 18. Troubleshooting Playbook: Pool Exhaustion

## Symptom

```text id="obs-044"
Hikari pending threads > 0
connection acquire timeout
API 503/500
```

## Check

```text id="obs-045"
[ ] active connections near max?
[ ] idle connections zero?
[ ] usage duration high?
[ ] long transactions?
[ ] idle in transaction?
[ ] slow queries?
[ ] connection leaks?
[ ] pod count × pool max > DB max_connections?
```

DB query:

```sql id="obs-046"
SELECT
    application_name,
    state,
    count(*) AS count
FROM pg_stat_activity
GROUP BY application_name, state
ORDER BY application_name, state;
```

App review:

```text id="obs-047"
[ ] SqlSession always closed?
[ ] transactionManager uses try-with-resources?
[ ] no streaming response holding connection?
[ ] no long report query using OLTP pool?
[ ] no remote call inside transaction?
```

Do not blindly increase pool size. If the database is saturated, bigger pools can increase contention and latency.

---

# 19. Troubleshooting Playbook: Lock Wait / Deadlock

## Symptom

```text id="obs-048"
Queries hang
lock_timeout
deadlock SQLSTATE 40P01
```

## Check blockers

```sql id="obs-049"
SELECT
    blocked.pid AS blocked_pid,
    now() - blocked_activity.query_start AS blocked_age,
    left(blocked_activity.query, 500) AS blocked_query,
    blocking.pid AS blocking_pid,
    now() - blocking_activity.query_start AS blocking_age,
    left(blocking_activity.query, 500) AS blocking_query
FROM pg_locks blocked
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocked_activity ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked.pid
JOIN pg_locks blocking
    ON blocking.locktype = blocked.locktype
   AND blocking.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.database
   AND blocking.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.relation
   AND blocking.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.page
   AND blocking.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.tuple
   AND blocking.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.transactionid
   AND blocking.pid <> blocked.pid
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking.pid
WHERE NOT blocked.granted
  AND blocking.granted;
```

Fix patterns:

```text id="obs-050"
[ ] Keep transactions short.
[ ] Lock rows in deterministic order.
[ ] Add missing index so UPDATE/SELECT FOR UPDATE touches fewer rows.
[ ] Avoid external calls inside transaction.
[ ] Use lock_timeout.
[ ] Retry SQLSTATE 40P01 only when operation is safe/idempotent.
```

---

# 20. Troubleshooting Playbook: Slow Query

## Symptom

```text id="obs-051"
Specific mapper method is slow.
```

## Steps

```text id="obs-052"
1. Identify mapper statement id.
2. Capture representative parameters.
3. Run query in staging/prod read replica if allowed.
4. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS).
5. Check actual vs estimated rows.
6. Check index usage.
7. Check sort/hash memory.
8. Check row count returned.
9. Check table stats freshness.
10. Review query design.
```

Common fixes:

```text id="obs-053"
[ ] Add/adjust composite index.
[ ] Replace OFFSET pagination with cursor.
[ ] Add LIMIT.
[ ] Avoid leading wildcard LIKE.
[ ] Avoid function on indexed column in WHERE unless expression index exists.
[ ] Split list and detail query.
[ ] Use read projection instead of full aggregate.
[ ] Reduce JSONB dynamic queries or add expression index.
```

---

# 21. Troubleshooting Playbook: Too Many 409 Conflicts

## Symptom

```text id="obs-054"
VERSION_CONFLICT / CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION spike
```

Check:

```text id="obs-055"
[ ] Is this expected user concurrency?
[ ] Is client retrying aggressively?
[ ] Is there a hot row/resource?
[ ] Did a batch job touch many same rows?
[ ] Are aggregate version updates too broad?
[ ] Are locks ordered consistently?
```

Possible fixes:

```text id="obs-056"
[ ] Better UX: refresh and retry.
[ ] Queue updates per aggregate.
[ ] Narrow update statement.
[ ] Use pessimistic lock for specific state transition.
[ ] Use idempotency key for repeated command.
```

---

# 22. Troubleshooting Playbook: Outbox Stuck

## Symptom

```text id="obs-057"
Pending grows, events not published.
```

Check:

```sql id="obs-058"
SELECT status, count(*)
FROM outbox_events
GROUP BY status;
```

```sql id="obs-059"
SELECT
    id,
    event_type,
    retry_count,
    next_attempt_at,
    locked_by,
    locked_at,
    left(last_error, 500) AS last_error
FROM outbox_events
WHERE status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'FAILED')
ORDER BY created_at ASC
LIMIT 100;
```

Likely causes:

```text id="obs-060"
[ ] Worker not running.
[ ] Broker unavailable.
[ ] Poison event serialization failure.
[ ] Stuck PROCESSING rows after worker crash.
[ ] next_attempt_at far in future due retry bug.
[ ] Claim query index missing.
```

Fix:

```text id="obs-061"
[ ] Restart worker.
[ ] Check broker auth/network.
[ ] Reset stuck PROCESSING rows.
[ ] Mark poison event FAILED.
[ ] Requeue after deploy fix.
[ ] Add alert on oldest pending age.
```

---

# 23. Troubleshooting Playbook: Data Leak Suspicion

## Symptom

```text id="obs-062"
User reports seeing other tenant/customer data.
```

Immediate checks:

```text id="obs-063"
[ ] Identify correlationId/request.
[ ] Check endpoint and mapper method.
[ ] Review SQL for tenant filter.
[ ] Check request did not supply tenantId body/query.
[ ] Check service derived tenant from auth context.
[ ] Check list/count/export query uses same visibility rules.
[ ] Check RLS if enabled.
```

Queries:

```sql id="obs-064"
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    count(*)
FROM orders
WHERE id = :reported_order_id
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```

Code grep:

```bash id="obs-065"
grep -R "findById(" src/main/java
grep -R "tenant_id" src/main/resources/mybatis
grep -R "\${" src/main/resources/mybatis
```

Fix pattern:

```text id="obs-066"
[ ] Repository methods require TenantId.
[ ] Mapper statement names include ForTenant.
[ ] Update/delete WHERE includes tenant_id.
[ ] Add cross-tenant regression tests.
[ ] Consider PostgreSQL RLS for defense-in-depth.
```

---

# 24. Production Logging Levels

Recommended defaults:

| Logger | Production default | Temporary debug |
|---|---:|---:|
| application service | INFO | DEBUG |
| repository timing | INFO/WARN slow | DEBUG |
| MyBatis framework | WARN | DEBUG |
| specific mapper | WARN | DEBUG/TRACE narrowly |
| SQL parameters | OFF | local only |
| PostgreSQL JDBC | WARN | DEBUG if diagnosing |
| HikariCP | INFO/WARN | DEBUG during pool issue |

Rule:

```text id="obs-067"
Debug narrowly, temporarily, and with redaction.
After incident, remove noisy logs or lower level.
```

---

# 25. Error Response Observability

A production error response should contain enough for support but not enough to leak internals.

```json id="obs-068"
{
  "code": "QUERY_TIMEOUT",
  "message": "Database query timed out",
  "correlationId": "req-123",
  "errors": []
}
```

Internal log:

```text id="obs-069"
level=WARN
event=api.error
code=QUERY_TIMEOUT
httpStatus=504
correlationId=req-123
sqlState=57014
repository=OrderRepository
method=search
durationMs=5000
```

Do not return:

```text id="obs-070"
[NO] raw SQL
[NO] table/column names
[NO] DB username
[NO] JDBC URL
[NO] stack trace
[NO] constraint detail if sensitive
```

---

# 26. Observability Test Ideas

```text id="obs-071"
[ ] Correlation ID is generated if missing.
[ ] Correlation ID is echoed if valid.
[ ] Invalid correlation ID is replaced.
[ ] ApiErrorResponse includes correlationId.
[ ] MDC is cleared between requests.
[ ] Slow repository call emits metric/log.
[ ] SQLSTATE translator increments metric.
[ ] Outbox failure increments failure metric.
[ ] Tenant ID is not logged raw if policy says hash.
```

Example JerseyTest:

```java id="obs-072"
@Test
void shouldEchoCorrelationId() {
    Response response = target("/orders")
            .request()
            .header("X-Correlation-Id", "req-test-123")
            .get();

    assertEquals("req-test-123",
            response.getHeaderString("X-Correlation-Id"));
}
```

# 27. Production Runbook Template

For each incident, capture:

```text id="obs-073"
Incident:
  start time:
  affected endpoint:
  symptoms:
  correlation IDs:
  api error codes:
  SQLSTATE:
  mapper/repository:
  Hikari metrics:
  pg_stat_activity:
  pg_locks:
  pg_stat_statements:
  EXPLAIN findings:
  mitigation:
  root cause:
  follow-up tests:
  follow-up dashboard/alert:
```

This turns one production issue into regression protection.

# 28. Review Checklist

## 28.1 Logging

```text id="obs-074"
[ ] Correlation ID included.
[ ] No raw secrets/PII.
[ ] Error logs have API code and SQLSTATE.
[ ] Slow query logs have mapper method and duration.
[ ] MDC cleaned up.
```

## 28.2 Metrics

```text id="obs-075"
[ ] API latency/error metrics.
[ ] Repository duration metrics.
[ ] DB error count by SQLSTATE.
[ ] Hikari active/idle/pending/acquire metrics.
[ ] Outbox pending/failed/oldest age.
```

## 28.3 PostgreSQL diagnostics

```text id="obs-076"
[ ] pg_stat_statements available if allowed.
[ ] pg_stat_activity access/runbook available.
[ ] pg_locks blocker query documented.
[ ] EXPLAIN workflow documented.
```

## 28.4 Security

```text id="obs-077"
[ ] SQL parameters not broadly logged.
[ ] Tenant/user identifiers hashed if required.
[ ] Error response does not leak DB internals.
[ ] Debug logs are temporary and scoped.
```

---

# 29. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| No correlation ID | Sulit trace request | Request/response filter + MDC |
| Global MyBatis TRACE in prod | PII leak/noise | Targeted temporary mapper debug |
| Log raw SQL params | Sensitive data leak | mapper + duration + SQLSTATE |
| No Hikari metrics | Pool issue tidak terlihat | expose pool metrics |
| No pg_stat_statements | Top query tidak diketahui | enable if allowed |
| No lock playbook | Deadlock debugging lambat | pg_locks + pg_stat_activity query |
| Semua DB error jadi 500 | Root cause kabur | SQLSTATE mapping |
| No outbox metrics | Event stuck diam-diam | pending/failed/oldest age |
| Increase pool blindly | DB makin saturasi | diagnose query/lock/transaction |
| No post-incident tests | Issue berulang | regression test + alert |

Saya lanjutkan **seri 8/9**: **MyBatis Performance Tuning & Query Review**. Ini akan fokus ke query plan, index-aware SQL, pagination, batch, fetch size, pool sizing, dynamic SQL review, dan checklist performa PostgreSQL.

# Seri 8/9 - MyBatis Performance Tuning & Query Review  
## query plan, index-aware SQL, pagination, batch, fetch size, connection pool sizing, MyBatis dynamic SQL review, PostgreSQL performance checklist

## 1. Introduction

Di aplikasi **Jersey/JAX-RS + MyBatis + PostgreSQL**, performa biasanya ditentukan oleh kombinasi:

```text id="perf-001"
API design
  ↓
query shape
  ↓
MyBatis mapper XML
  ↓
parameter binding
  ↓
PostgreSQL planner statistics
  ↓
index design
  ↓
transaction duration
  ↓
connection pool pressure
  ↓
serialization/response size
```

MyBatis memang “SQL-first”: SQL ada di mapper XML dan MyBatis berusaha “stay out of your way”, sehingga performa sangat bergantung pada kualitas SQL, `resultMap`, dynamic SQL, dan cara query dipanggil dari repository/service. MyBatis mapper XML juga menyediakan atribut seperti `timeout`, `fetchSize`, `resultSetType`, dan `resultOrdered` pada statement tertentu yang bisa memengaruhi behavior query. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

PostgreSQL sendiri membuat query plan untuk setiap query; `EXPLAIN` dipakai untuk melihat plan yang dipilih planner, sedangkan `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` menjalankan query dan menampilkan runtime aktual. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/using-explain.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 2. Performance Mental Model

```text id="perf-002"
Fast endpoint =
  bounded request
  + bounded query
  + selective WHERE
  + deterministic ORDER BY
  + proper index
  + small result set
  + short transaction
  + enough pool capacity
  + no accidental N+1
```

Rule utama:

```text id="perf-003"
Jangan mulai tuning dari pool size.
Mulai dari:
  1. query shape
  2. EXPLAIN plan
  3. index alignment
  4. row count
  5. transaction duration
  6. pool pressure
```

Connection pool yang lebih besar tidak otomatis membuat sistem lebih cepat. Jika bottleneck ada di query lambat, lock, atau DB CPU/IO, menambah pool bisa menambah concurrency dan memperburuk contention.

---

# 3. Diagram

```text id="perf-004"
Jersey Resource
  ↓
DTO Validation
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
Repository
  ↓
MyBatis Mapper Method
  ↓
Mapper XML
  ├─ SELECT explicit columns
  ├─ WHERE indexed/selective
  ├─ ORDER BY deterministic
  ├─ LIMIT bounded
  ├─ no unsafe ${}
  ├─ fetchSize / timeout if needed
  └─ resultMap / projection
       ↓
PostgreSQL Planner
  ├─ statistics
  ├─ index choice
  ├─ join strategy
  ├─ sort/hash
  └─ execution plan
       ↓
Runtime Metrics
  ├─ query duration
  ├─ rows returned
  ├─ lock wait
  ├─ pool wait
  └─ SQLSTATE
```

---

# 4. Decomposition Map

| Area | Skill/domain | Tujuan | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Query shape | SELECT/WHERE/JOIN/ORDER/LIMIT | SQL predictable | query terlalu luas |
| `EXPLAIN` | planner analysis | tahu plan | tuning berdasarkan feeling |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` | runtime analysis | actual row/time/buffer | dipakai sembarangan di write query |
| Index-aware SQL | align WHERE/ORDER BY dengan index | avoid full scan/sort | index tidak kepakai |
| Composite index | multi-column access path | optimize filter + order | urutan kolom salah |
| Partial index | index subset data | kecil dan spesifik | predicate tidak match query |
| Expression index | index expression | JSONB/lower/date expression | query expression tidak identik |
| Pagination | offset vs cursor | bounded list | offset besar lambat |
| Batch operations | bulk insert/update | reduce roundtrip | batch terlalu besar |
| `fetchSize` | row fetching hint | stream-ish large read | load semua ke memory |
| MyBatis `ExecutorType.BATCH` | JDBC batch | efficient repeated update | flush/commit salah |
| Dynamic SQL review | `if/where/set/foreach` | flexible but safe | branch tidak dites |
| Result projection | summary/detail split | reduce overfetch | full aggregate list |
| Connection pool | Hikari sizing/timeout | stable concurrency | pool exhaustion |
| Transaction duration | short DB work | reduce lock/pool hold | remote call in transaction |
| Observability | metrics/logs/pg stats | root cause | no evidence |

---

# 5. Query Review Baseline

Setiap mapper `SELECT` production perlu dicek dengan checklist ini:

```text id="perf-005"
[ ] SELECT column eksplisit, bukan SELECT *.
[ ] WHERE selalu punya tenant/security scope jika multi-tenant.
[ ] WHERE memakai filter yang selektif.
[ ] ORDER BY deterministic.
[ ] LIMIT ada untuk list/search.
[ ] OFFSET besar dihindari untuk data besar.
[ ] JOIN tidak menyebabkan row explosion.
[ ] resultMap/projection sesuai kebutuhan.
[ ] Tidak ada raw user input di ${}.
[ ] Query punya test dengan PostgreSQL.
[ ] Query kritikal sudah dicek EXPLAIN.
```

Bad:

```xml id="perf-006"
<select id="searchOrders" resultType="OrderRecord">
    SELECT *
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = #{status}
</select>
```

Better:

```xml id="perf-007"
<select id="searchOrders" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND status = #{status}
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

---

# 6. EXPLAIN Workflow

## 6.1 Basic EXPLAIN

```sql id="perf-008"
EXPLAIN
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    status,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'
  AND status = 'SUBMITTED'
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Use this to inspect planned shape before execution.

## 6.2 EXPLAIN ANALYZE BUFFERS

```sql id="perf-009"
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    status,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'
  AND status = 'SUBMITTED'
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` actually executes the statement, so use caution for data-changing statements; PostgreSQL’s documentation explicitly notes that `ANALYZE` causes execution. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/sql-explain.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 6.3 What to inspect

```text id="perf-010"
[ ] Actual time.
[ ] Actual rows.
[ ] Estimated rows vs actual rows.
[ ] Seq Scan vs Index Scan.
[ ] Index Cond vs Filter.
[ ] Sort node.
[ ] Buffers hit/read.
[ ] Rows removed by filter.
[ ] Nested Loop with unexpectedly high row count.
[ ] Planning time vs execution time.
```

Large mismatch between estimated and actual rows often means statistics/index/query shape needs review.

---

# 7. Planner Statistics

PostgreSQL planner relies on statistics to estimate selectivity of `WHERE` clauses; those statistics are updated by `ANALYZE` or `VACUUM ANALYZE`. If statistics are stale or insufficient, the planner can choose a bad plan. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.5/planner-stats.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Useful maintenance command:

```sql id="perf-011"
ANALYZE orders;
```

For skewed columns, consider higher statistics target:

```sql id="perf-012"
ALTER TABLE orders
ALTER COLUMN status SET STATISTICS 1000;

ANALYZE orders;
```

Review triggers:

```text id="perf-013"
[ ] Query plan changed after large data load.
[ ] Estimated rows far from actual rows.
[ ] New status/tenant distribution skew.
[ ] Big backfill/migration ran recently.
[ ] New index added but not chosen.
```

---

# 8. Index-Aware SQL

## 8.1 Query

```sql id="perf-014"
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    status,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND status = ?
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT ?;
```

Index candidate:

```sql id="perf-015"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted_id
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    status,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
);
```

Why this shape:

```text id="perf-016"
tenant_id, status = equality filters
submitted_at DESC, id DESC = sort + cursor order
```

PostgreSQL multicolumn indexes are most effective when query predicates align with leading index columns; the docs explain behavior around equality constraints on leading columns and how remaining columns are used. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-multicolumn.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 8.2 ORDER BY and index

PostgreSQL can use a B-tree index to return rows in sorted order and avoid a separate sort step; B-tree is the index type that can produce sorted output. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-ordering.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Query:

```sql id="perf-017"
SELECT
    id,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Index:

```sql id="perf-018"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_submitted_id
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
);
```

Checklist:

```text id="perf-019"
[ ] ORDER BY includes deterministic tie-breaker.
[ ] Index order matches common query order.
[ ] LIMIT is present.
[ ] EXPLAIN confirms index scan or useful plan.
```

---

# 9. Composite Index Decision

## 9.1 Equality + range + order

Query:

```sql id="perf-020"
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND status = ?
  AND submitted_at >= ?
  AND submitted_at < ?
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT ?;
```

Index candidate:

```sql id="perf-021"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted_id
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    status,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
);
```

Rule of thumb:

```text id="perf-022"
Common composite index shape:
  equality filters first
  then range/order column
  then tie-breaker/order column
```

But always validate with `EXPLAIN`, because actual data distribution matters.

---

# 10. Partial Index

Use partial index when query mostly targets one subset.

Example: most searches only process active/submitted orders.

```sql id="perf-023"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_submitted_tenant_submitted_id
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
)
WHERE status = 'SUBMITTED';
```

Query must match predicate:

```sql id="perf-024"
SELECT
    id,
    order_number,
    submitted_at
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND status = 'SUBMITTED'
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Good for:

```text id="perf-025"
[OK] status-specific hot path.
[OK] soft-delete filter: deleted_at IS NULL.
[OK] queue table: status = 'PENDING'.
[OK] smaller index with high selectivity.
```

Caution:

```text id="perf-026"
[ ] Predicate must match query.
[ ] Too many partial indexes increase write overhead.
[ ] Review with EXPLAIN.
```

---

# 11. Expression Index

Useful when query filters on expression.

## 11.1 Case-insensitive search

Query:

```sql id="perf-027"
SELECT
    id,
    customer_number,
    display_name
FROM customers
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND lower(email) = lower(?);
```

Index:

```sql id="perf-028"
CREATE INDEX idx_customers_tenant_lower_email
ON customers (
    tenant_id,
    lower(email)
);
```

## 11.2 JSONB key

Query:

```sql id="perf-029"
SELECT
    id,
    order_number
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND metadata ->> 'externalReference' = ?;
```

Index:

```sql id="perf-030"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_external_reference
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    (metadata ->> 'externalReference')
);
```

Checklist:

```text id="perf-031"
[ ] Query expression exactly matches index expression.
[ ] Use expression index only for hot expressions.
[ ] Validate with EXPLAIN.
```

---

# 12. Covering Index / INCLUDE

When you want index to contain extra columns for read-heavy query:

```sql id="perf-032"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted_include
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    status,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
)
INCLUDE (
    order_number,
    total_amount,
    currency
);
```

Use carefully:

```text id="perf-033"
[OK] read-heavy summary query
[OK] avoid table heap visit in some cases
[OK] stable small included columns

[NO] many wide columns
[NO] frequently updated included columns
[NO] replacing proper data modeling
```

---

# 13. Pagination Performance

## 13.1 Offset pagination

```xml id="perf-034"
<select id="searchOrdersOffset" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
    OFFSET #{offset}
</select>
```

Good for:

```text id="perf-035"
[OK] small datasets
[OK] admin screens
[OK] page number UX
[OK] low write churn
```

Risk:

```text id="perf-036"
[NO] large offset gets slower
[NO] data changes can cause duplicate/missing rows
[NO] needs count query if UI shows total pages
```

## 13.2 Cursor/keyset pagination

```xml id="perf-037"
<select id="searchOrdersCursor" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    <where>
        tenant_id = #{tenantId}

        <if test="status != null">
            AND status = #{status}
        </if>

        <if test="cursorSubmittedAt != null and cursorId != null">
            AND (
                submitted_at &lt; #{cursorSubmittedAt}
                OR (
                    submitted_at = #{cursorSubmittedAt}
                    AND id &lt; #{cursorId}
                )
            )
        </if>
    </where>
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Index:

```sql id="perf-038"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tenant_status_submitted_id
ON orders (
    tenant_id,
    status,
    submitted_at DESC,
    id DESC
);
```

Good for:

```text id="perf-039"
[OK] large data
[OK] infinite scroll/feed
[OK] high write concurrency
[OK] stable next-page navigation
```

---

# 14. Count Query Strategy

Bad for huge filtered data if done on every request:

```sql id="perf-040"
SELECT count(*)
FROM orders
WHERE tenant_id = ?
  AND status = ?;
```

Options:

```text id="perf-041"
1. Do not show exact total.
2. Show “hasNext” by fetching limit + 1 rows.
3. Cache counts for slow-changing dashboards.
4. Use summary table/materialized view for reporting.
5. Run exact count async.
```

Pattern:

```java id="perf-042"
List<OrderSummaryRecord> rows = mapper.search(criteria.withLimit(size + 1));

boolean hasNext = rows.size() > size;

List<OrderSummaryRecord> pageRows = hasNext
        ? rows.subList(0, size)
        : rows;
```

---

# 15. Avoid N+1 Query

Bad list flow:

```text id="perf-043"
search 100 orders
  ↓
for each order:
  select items
  select customer
  select latest payment
```

This can become hundreds of SQL statements for one API call.

Better:

```text id="perf-044"
1. Query parent page.
2. Extract parent IDs.
3. Batch load children with WHERE order_id IN (...)
4. Group in Java.
```

Mapper:

```xml id="perf-045"
<select id="findItemsByOrderIds"
        resultMap="OrderItemResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_id,
        product_id,
        quantity,
        unit_price,
        currency
    FROM order_items
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND order_id IN
      <foreach collection="orderIds"
               item="orderId"
               open="("
               separator=","
               close=")">
          #{orderId}
      </foreach>
    ORDER BY order_id, created_at, id
</select>
```

MyBatis dynamic SQL supports `foreach` for collection iteration, commonly used for `IN` lists. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Checklist:

```text id="perf-046"
[ ] Limit parent page size.
[ ] Bound IN list size.
[ ] Index child table on tenant_id + order_id.
[ ] Test empty list.
[ ] Avoid one child query per parent.
```

---

# 16. Result Projection vs Aggregate Loading

For list/search, prefer projection.

Bad:

```java id="perf-047"
List<Order> orders = repository.searchFullAggregates(criteria);
```

Better:

```java id="perf-048"
public record OrderSummaryRecord(
        UUID id,
        String orderNumber,
        OrderStatus status,
        BigDecimal totalAmount,
        String currency,
        Instant submittedAt
) {}
```

Mapper:

```xml id="perf-049"
<select id="searchOrderSummaries" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Rule:

```text id="perf-050"
Command/update/detail behavior:
  load aggregate.

List/search/read-only:
  use projection.
```

---

# 17. MyBatis Statement Attributes

MyBatis `<select>` supports attributes including `timeout`, `fetchSize`, `resultSetType`, and others. `timeout` controls how many seconds the driver waits for database response, while `fetchSize` is a driver hint for batch row retrieval. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Example:

```xml id="perf-051"
<select id="exportOrders"
        resultMap="OrderExportResultMap"
        timeout="60"
        fetchSize="500"
        resultSetType="FORWARD_ONLY">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        total_amount,
        currency,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
      AND submitted_at &gt;= #{from}
      AND submitted_at &lt; #{to}
    ORDER BY submitted_at ASC, id ASC
</select>
```

Use for:

```text id="perf-052"
[OK] export/report query
[OK] large but bounded read
[OK] cursor-style processing
```

Avoid:

```text id="perf-053"
[NO] synchronous huge export endpoint
[NO] loading millions of rows into List
[NO] long-running transaction in OLTP path
```

---

# 18. Cursor / Streaming Read

MyBatis Java API includes cursor-style selection through `selectCursor`, and MyBatis documentation notes `Cursor` implements `Closeable`, so it should be closed after use. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/java-api.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Pattern:

```java id="perf-054"
try (SqlSession session = sqlSessionFactory.openSession();
     Cursor<OrderExportRecord> cursor =
             session.selectCursor(
                     "com.company.app.infrastructure.order.OrderSqlMapper.exportOrders",
                     criteria
             )) {

    for (OrderExportRecord record : cursor) {
        writer.write(record);
    }
}
```

Caution:

```text id="perf-055"
[ ] Cursor keeps DB resources open.
[ ] Keep transaction/session lifecycle explicit.
[ ] Do not use for normal low-latency API if export can be async.
[ ] Ensure cursor is closed.
[ ] Add timeout/cancellation strategy.
```

---

# 19. Batch Insert / Update

## 19.1 Multi-row insert

```xml id="perf-056"
<insert id="insertOrderItems">
    INSERT INTO order_items (
        id,
        tenant_id,
        order_id,
        product_id,
        quantity,
        unit_price,
        currency
    )
    VALUES
    <foreach collection="items"
             item="item"
             separator=",">
        (
            #{item.id},
            #{item.tenantId},
            #{item.orderId},
            #{item.productId},
            #{item.quantity},
            #{item.unitPrice},
            #{item.currency}
        )
    </foreach>
</insert>
```

Good for small-to-medium batch.

## 19.2 ExecutorType.BATCH

```java id="perf-057"
try (SqlSession session =
             sqlSessionFactory.openSession(ExecutorType.BATCH, false)) {

    OrderSqlMapper mapper = session.getMapper(OrderSqlMapper.class);

    for (OrderItemRecord item : items) {
        mapper.insertOrderItem(item);
    }

    session.flushStatements();
    session.commit();
}
```

MyBatis Java API documents `ExecutorType.BATCH` as batching update statements and demarcating them if a select is executed between them. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/java-api.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Batch checklist:

```text id="perf-058"
[ ] Define max batch size.
[ ] Chunk large batches.
[ ] Avoid mixing SELECT inside batch loop.
[ ] Flush statements intentionally.
[ ] Handle partial failure/error reporting.
[ ] Measure memory and transaction duration.
```

---

# 20. Batch Size Strategy

```text id="perf-059"
10-100 rows:
  multi-row INSERT often fine.

100-5,000 rows:
  chunked multi-row or ExecutorType.BATCH.

Very large import:
  async job, staging table, COPY, or specialized bulk path.

User-facing API:
  keep small and bounded.
```

Avoid:

```text id="perf-060"
[NO] one transaction with hundreds of thousands of rows.
[NO] unbounded request payload.
[NO] synchronous request doing report/import workload.
```

---

# 21. Dynamic SQL Performance Review

Dynamic SQL is powerful but can create too many query shapes.

Example:

```xml id="perf-061"
<select id="searchOrders" resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status,
        submitted_at
    FROM orders
    <where>
        tenant_id = #{tenantId}

        <if test="status != null">
            AND status = #{status}
        </if>

        <if test="customerId != null">
            AND customer_id = #{customerId}
        </if>

        <if test="submittedFrom != null">
            AND submitted_at &gt;= #{submittedFrom}
        </if>

        <if test="submittedTo != null">
            AND submitted_at &lt; #{submittedTo}
        </if>
    </where>
    ORDER BY ${sortColumn} ${sortDirection}, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

Review questions:

```text id="perf-062"
[ ] Which filter combinations are common?
[ ] Which combinations have indexes?
[ ] Is sortColumn allow-listed?
[ ] Do optional filters break index usefulness?
[ ] Are there too many branches for one generic query?
[ ] Should hot query paths be separate mapper statements?
```

Sometimes better:

```text id="perf-063"
searchOrdersByStatus
searchOrdersByCustomer
searchOrdersBySubmittedRange
searchOrdersGeneral
```

Instead of one overly generic query that is hard to index well.

---

# 22. Dynamic SQL Branch Test Matrix

| Branch | Test |
|---|---|
| no optional filter | returns tenant-scoped result |
| status only | uses status query path |
| customer only | uses customer filter |
| date range only | correct range boundary |
| status + date | correct intersection |
| invalid sort | rejected before mapper |
| large limit | validation rejects |
| empty result | returns empty list |
| null tenant | rejected before DB |
| malicious sort | cannot enter `${}` |

---

# 23. JSONB Query Performance

JSONB is useful, but hot query keys often need index or promotion to typed column.

Containment query:

```sql id="perf-064"
WHERE metadata @> '{"sourceSystem": "CRM"}'
```

GIN index:

```sql id="perf-065"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_metadata_gin
ON orders
USING gin (metadata);
```

Expression query:

```sql id="perf-066"
WHERE metadata ->> 'externalReference' = ?
```

Expression index:

```sql id="perf-067"
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_metadata_external_ref
ON orders ((metadata ->> 'externalReference'));
```

Rule:

```text id="perf-068"
If JSONB key becomes hot filter/sort/join:
  index it, or promote to typed column.
```

PostgreSQL docs explain that `jsonb` supports indexing and that GIN indexes can efficiently search keys/key-value pairs in many `jsonb` documents. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# 24. Transaction Duration Performance

Long transaction causes:

```text id="perf-069"
[ ] connection held longer
[ ] lock held longer
[ ] vacuum pressure
[ ] higher pool usage
[ ] more deadlock risk
```

Bad:

```java id="perf-070"
transactionManager.inTransaction(session -> {
    Order order = repository.findByIdForUpdate(tenantId, orderId).orElseThrow();

    externalPricingClient.recalculate(order); // remote call inside transaction

    order.approve();

    repository.save(order);
    return null;
});
```

Better:

```text id="perf-071"
1. Do external read before transaction if safe.
2. Start transaction.
3. Load/lock row.
4. Validate state.
5. Write DB changes.
6. Commit.
7. Publish/notify through outbox after commit.
```

---

# 25. Connection Pool Sizing

HikariCP is a production-ready JDBC connection pool; its configuration includes settings such as `maximumPoolSize`, `connectionTimeout`, `idleTimeout`, `maxLifetime`, and other lifecycle controls. ([GitHub](https://github.com/brettwooldridge/hikaricp?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 25.1 Pool sizing mental model

```text id="perf-072"
Total DB connections =
  number of app instances/pods
  × maximumPoolSize per instance
  + other apps/jobs/admin connections
```

Example:

```text id="perf-073"
20 pods × pool size 20 = 400 potential connections

If PostgreSQL max_connections is 300,
this is already unsafe before jobs/admin sessions.
```

## 25.2 Practical config

```java id="perf-074"
HikariConfig config = new HikariConfig();

config.setPoolName("order-service-pool");
config.setJdbcUrl(jdbcUrl);
config.setUsername(username);
config.setPassword(password);

config.setMaximumPoolSize(20);
config.setMinimumIdle(5);

config.setConnectionTimeout(2_000);
config.setValidationTimeout(1_000);
config.setMaxLifetime(1_800_000);
```

## 25.3 Pool tuning checklist

```text id="perf-075"
[ ] Start from measured workload, not guess.
[ ] Check DB max_connections.
[ ] Account for number of pods/instances.
[ ] Monitor active/idle/pending/acquire duration.
[ ] Keep connectionTimeout reasonably short.
[ ] Do not use pool increase as first response to slow query.
[ ] Separate long-running jobs from OLTP pool if needed.
```

---

# 26. Query Timeout Strategy

Set timeouts at several layers:

```text id="perf-076"
HTTP client timeout
Jersey/server timeout
connection pool acquisition timeout
MyBatis statement timeout
PostgreSQL statement_timeout
PostgreSQL lock_timeout
```

MyBatis mapper statement `timeout` sets how long the driver waits for database response in seconds. ([MyBatis](https://mybatis.org/mybatis-3/sqlmap-xml.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Mapper:

```xml id="perf-077"
<select id="searchOrders"
        resultMap="OrderSummaryResultMap"
        timeout="5">
    SELECT
        id,
        order_number,
        status
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId}
    ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
    LIMIT #{limit}
</select>
```

PostgreSQL local transaction timeout:

```sql id="perf-078"
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '1s';
```

Guideline:

```text id="perf-079"
User-facing OLTP query:
  short timeout.

Export/report:
  async job with separate timeout.

Lock wait:
  fail fast if user-facing.
```

---

# 27. Query Shape Smells

| Smell | Why bad | Better |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT *` | overfetch + schema drift | explicit columns |
| no `LIMIT` on list | unbounded memory/latency | limit + pagination |
| large `OFFSET` | scans/skips many rows | cursor pagination |
| function on indexed column | index may not match | expression index or rewrite |
| dynamic raw `${}` | injection risk | enum allow-list |
| leading wildcard `LIKE '%x'` | poor B-tree usage | search index/trigram strategy |
| full aggregate for list | overfetch/N+1 | projection |
| one query per child row | N+1 | batch load |
| optional filters all in one query | hard to index | split hot paths |
| no tenant filter | security + performance | tenant-scoped index/query |

---

# 28. Index Review Checklist

```text id="perf-080"
[ ] What query is this index for?
[ ] Does WHERE match index leading columns?
[ ] Does ORDER BY match index order?
[ ] Does LIMIT make index scan beneficial?
[ ] Is this query frequent enough?
[ ] Is write overhead acceptable?
[ ] Is there already similar index?
[ ] Is this partial/expression index justified?
[ ] Has EXPLAIN confirmed usage?
[ ] Is migration safe for large table?
```

Bad index request:

```text id="perf-081"
“Add index on status because query is slow.”
```

Better index request:

```text id="perf-082"
“For OrderSqlMapper.searchOrdersByStatus:
 WHERE tenant_id = ? AND status = ?
 ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 50.
 Proposed index:
 (tenant_id, status, submitted_at DESC, id DESC).
 EXPLAIN before/after attached.”
```

---

# 29. Mapper XML Performance Review Checklist

```text id="perf-083"
[ ] Statement id clear and use-case specific.
[ ] SELECT column list explicit.
[ ] resultMap/projection minimal.
[ ] WHERE tenant/security filter present.
[ ] WHERE filters indexed if hot.
[ ] ORDER BY deterministic.
[ ] LIMIT present.
[ ] OFFSET reviewed.
[ ] Dynamic SQL branches tested.
[ ] `${}` only for allow-listed fragments.
[ ] `timeout` set for critical queries.
[ ] `fetchSize` considered for large bounded reads.
[ ] Batch statements chunked.
```

---

# 30. API-Level Performance Checklist

```text id="perf-084"
[ ] Request payload size bounded.
[ ] Page size max enforced.
[ ] Sort/filter allow-list.
[ ] Response DTO minimal.
[ ] Large export is async.
[ ] No repeated remote calls per row.
[ ] No DB transaction around slow external call.
[ ] Error contract for timeout/too large request.
```

---

# 31. CI / PR Performance Gate

For important query PRs, require:

```text id="perf-085"
[ ] Mapper XML diff reviewed.
[ ] New query has integration test.
[ ] Query has bounded LIMIT if list/search.
[ ] EXPLAIN attached for critical query.
[ ] Index migration attached if needed.
[ ] Test data realistic enough.
[ ] Golden response unaffected or updated intentionally.
[ ] Metrics/logging tags available.
```

Optional performance regression test:

```java id="perf-086"
@Test
void searchOrdersShouldStayUnderReasonableThreshold() {
    seedOrders(10_000);

    long started = System.nanoTime();

    List<OrderSummaryRecord> result = mapper.searchOrders(criteria);

    long durationMs =
            TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toMillis(System.nanoTime() - started);

    assertTrue(durationMs < 500);
    assertEquals(50, result.size());
}
```

Caution:

```text id="perf-087"
Timing tests can be flaky in CI.
Use them sparingly.
Prefer EXPLAIN/regression checks for query shape,
and integration tests for correctness.
```

---

# 32. Troubleshooting Slow Endpoint

```text id="perf-088"
1. Identify endpoint and correlationId.
2. Check API latency breakdown.
3. Check repository/method duration.
4. Check Hikari pending/acquire time.
5. Check pg_stat_activity for active/waiting query.
6. Check pg_stat_statements for top query.
7. Reproduce SQL with parameters.
8. Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS).
9. Compare actual vs estimated rows.
10. Review index/query shape.
```

---

# 33. Common Anti-Pattern

| Anti-pattern | Dampak | Alternatif |
|---|---|---|
| Tuning dari pool size | root cause tidak selesai | start with query plan |
| `SELECT *` di mapper | overfetch/schema drift | explicit projection |
| Offset pagination untuk data besar | slow page | cursor/keyset |
| Generic dynamic query terlalu luas | index susah | split hot paths |
| Full aggregate list | memory/N+1 | summary projection |
| Batch tanpa chunk | timeout/lock/WAL besar | chunked batch |
| Cursor tidak ditutup | resource leak | try-with-resources |
| `EXPLAIN` tidak pernah dipakai | tuning nebak | EXPLAIN workflow |
| Index dibuat tanpa query target | index bloat | index per query shape |
| Transaction berisi remote call | lock/pool lama | move remote call outside |

---

# 34. Production Checklist

```text id="perf-089"
Query design
[ ] Explicit columns.
[ ] Tenant/security filter.
[ ] Deterministic ORDER BY.
[ ] LIMIT for list/search.
[ ] Projection for read-only list.
[ ] No N+1.

Indexing
[ ] Composite index aligns with WHERE + ORDER BY.
[ ] Partial/expression indexes justified.
[ ] EXPLAIN validates critical query.
[ ] Index write overhead reviewed.

Pagination
[ ] Offset only for small/admin use.
[ ] Cursor for large/high-churn data.
[ ] Count query strategy decided.

MyBatis
[ ] resultMap minimal.
[ ] Dynamic SQL branches tested.
[ ] timeout configured for important query.
[ ] fetchSize/cursor considered for large bounded read.
[ ] ExecutorType.BATCH/chunking for bulk write.

Runtime
[ ] Transactions short.
[ ] No external calls inside DB transaction.
[ ] Pool sizing based on workload and DB capacity.
[ ] Hikari metrics monitored.
[ ] SQLSTATE/timeouts observable.

Testing
[ ] PostgreSQL integration test.
[ ] resultMap/TypeHandler tests.
[ ] query branch tests.
[ ] tenant isolation tests.
[ ] optional EXPLAIN/performance review for critical paths.
```

# 35. Roadmap Belajar Singkat

```text id="perf-090"
1. Kuasai EXPLAIN dan EXPLAIN ANALYZE
   ↓
2. Review query shape: SELECT/WHERE/ORDER/LIMIT
   ↓
3. Pelajari composite index untuk filter + order
   ↓
4. Terapkan cursor pagination untuk data besar

6. Hilangkan N+1 dengan batch child loading
   ↓

   ↓

   ↓
```

# Seri 9/9 — Final Consolidated Checklist / Onboarding Playbook  
## MyBatis + PostgreSQL + Jersey/JAX-RS end-to-end readiness

## 1. Introduction

Ini adalah rangkuman final dari seluruh seri **MyBatis + PostgreSQL + Jersey/JAX-RS**. Tujuannya sebagai **playbook onboarding senior software engineer**: apa yang harus dipahami, dicek di PR, dites di CI, dimonitor di production, dan diwaspadai saat incident.

Mental model utama:

```text
HTTP API bukan database schema.
Domain bukan MyBatis record.
Repository bukan service.
Mapper XML bukan tempat business workflow.
PostgreSQL bukan sekadar storage.
Test harus memakai PostgreSQL asli.
Production readiness = correctness + security + performance + observability.
```

---

# 2. End-to-End Architecture Map

```text
Client
  ↓
Jersey Resource
  - @Path / @GET / @POST / @PUT / @PATCH / @DELETE
  - Request DTO
  - Bean Validation
  - Security context
  - Correlation ID
  ↓
API Mapper
  - Request DTO → Command
  - Result → Response DTO
  ↓
Application Service
  - Use-case orchestration
  - Transaction boundary
  - Authorization / permission
  - Calls domain behavior
  ↓
Domain Layer
  - Aggregate
  - Entity
  - Value Object
  - Invariant
  - Domain Event
  ↓
Repository Interface
  - Domain-friendly persistence contract
  - Tenant-scoped methods
  ↓
Repository Implementation
  - Uses MyBatis mapper
  - Maps domain ↔ persistence record
  - Translates persistence errors
  ↓
MyBatis Mapper Interface
  - Java method contract for SQL
  ↓
Mapper XML
  - SQL
  - resultMap
  - dynamic SQL
  - TypeHandler
  ↓
PostgreSQL
  - tables
  - indexes
  - constraints
  - functions/procedures
  - transactions
  - locks
  ↓
Observability
  - logs
  - metrics
  - SQLSTATE
  - pg_stat_activity
  - pg_locks
  - pg_stat_statements
```

---

# 3. Core Principles

| Principle | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **DTO ≠ Domain ≠ Record** | API DTO, domain object, and MyBatis record must stay separate. |
| **Service owns transaction** | Application service defines atomic use case; repository should not commit independently. |
| **Repository hides MyBatis** | Service depends on repository interface, not mapper XML. |
| **SQL is contract too** | Mapper XML, `resultMap`, and migration must evolve together. |
| **Tenant context is server-derived** | Never trust `tenantId` from request body for normal user-facing API. |
| **Use `#{}` by default** | `${}` only for server-side allow-listed SQL fragments. |
| **Test with PostgreSQL** | H2/mock cannot prove PostgreSQL-specific behavior. |
| **Outbox for external events** | DB change + outbox row in one transaction, publish after commit. |
| **Observe SQLSTATE** | Do not parse DB error text; map SQLSTATE to stable API errors. |
| **Tune from query plan** | Start with SQL shape and `EXPLAIN`, not pool size. |

---

# 4. Package Structure Reference

```text
com.company.app
├── api
│   ├── ApiApplication.java
│   ├── config
│   │   ├── ObjectMapperProvider.java
│   │   └── ValidationConfigProvider.java
│   ├── filter
│   │   ├── CorrelationIdRequestFilter.java
│   │   └── CorrelationIdResponseFilter.java
│   ├── error
│   │   ├── ApiErrorResponse.java
│   │   ├── FieldErrorResponse.java
│   │   ├── DomainExceptionMapper.java
│   │   ├── PersistenceExceptionMapper.java
│   │   └── UnhandledExceptionMapper.java
│   └── order
```
